Sports.title: Battle of boxing's most unlikeable stars: Conor Benn takes on troubled Ryan Garcia after burning Eddie Hearn with $10MILLION payday in his sights - but here's why Briton's fate rests solely in the hands of his narcissistic American rival
Sports.content:
‘Who ya like buddy?’ It’s the most asked question in casino-ville as the hours tick down to this Saturday’s world title fight between two angry young men.

One, America’s extravagantly gifted but troubled world welterweight champion. The other, the ever-persistent English challenger who never stops throwing punches whether they connect or not. As if in manic obsession with defeating not only opponents but also his demons and a sceptical outside world.

So, Ryan Garcia or Conor Benn?

When the denizens of this neon gambling Strip in the Nevada desert ask that question they don’t’ want to know which of these two combatants you like personally more than the other. It is their way of trying to find out who you might be betting on to prevail in the atmospheric T-Mobile Arena.

Their inquiries are even more numerous than usual on such occasions as this. Because neither the Americans nor the Mexicans who are thronging here in support of their blood brother by heredity know very much about Benn. Other than the fact he is the son of a fabled icon of the British ring.

On his two previous US visits Benn Jr made hard work of beating men who looked more like nightclub bouncers than professional boxers. Of his exploits back home only the pair of fights against Chris Eubank Jr evoked any interest whatsoever on either side of this border.

What they are aware of is the two positive tests for performance enhancing drugs and the protracted legal battle to technically clear his name which kept him out of the ring for months. Just as they know about Garcia’s conviction and suspension for a similar finding.

Conor Benn is locked in the battle of boxing's most unlikeable stars in Las Vegas

Benn is lining up a $10m payday after burning his bridges with promoter Eddie Hearn

So, what’s to like?

There can be no doubting Benn’s work ethic. He trains like a dervish to manufacture the maximum possible out of however much natural-born ability he inherited from Nigel the Dark Destroyer. Nor does he ever give up. Eubank Jr had to go beyond the normal limits of even this battle-hardened business to inflict the only defeat of Conor’s career thus far. A loss he avenged, albeit in partly contrived and contentious circumstances.

Eubank the Younger was perilously drained in the rematch by a clause in the contract which prevented him rehydrating fully after struggling to cut poundage to meet the agreed catchweight.

What goes around comes around. If not in a full measure of the irony. Benn has had to sweat and strain down by almost a stone from middleweight to make the welterweight championship limit of 147 lbs. As he puts it: ‘Five weeks in hell.’

To say his body looks shredded is putting it mildly. But he has not been subjected to rehydration limitations following his Friday morning visit to the scales.

Eubank was handsomely rewarded to put his health on the line, and now Benn has been lured into similar jeopardy by the fortune – some reports say ten million dollars – he is receiving from UFC boss Dana White to be one of the first poster boys for his venture into boxing.

Benn tells it otherwise: ‘I’m doing this because I relish challenges. Have always wanted to strap on the same green WBC belt my dad was so proud to wear. To start getting the world titles that will leave a legacy for my kids. And to prove wrong everyone who doesn’t give me a chance of winning. That puts all the pressure on him, not me.’

Hearn backed the British fighter during his controversial doping ban saga

Ryan Garcia stands in his way of the WBC title, who is the more talented of the fighters

WEIGH-IN VERDICT: After all the brouhaha Conor Benn made the weight with a full pound to spare After what he described as 'five weeks of hell' dieting down by two divisions he scaled 146 lbs in readiness to challenge world welterweight champion Ryan Garcia here this Saturday night. He did so with a told-you so smile. Throughout the speculation as to whether he could shed the best part of a stone in his training camp journey from middleweight Benn had assured one and all that he would be comfortable at his long-ago weight. Good as his word he came in only half a pound heavier than Garcia. Although he is leaner of hip the muscle is still there on arms and torso. Complete with a six pack as a reminder of his constant work ethic. The slightly taller part/Mexican great white hope of American boxing does look more natural at the weight. But Benn does not appear stressed from all his exertions. Even so Garcia is still a solid odds on favourite in the Vegas betting

Whether or not Benn can take in sufficient liquids and pasta before entering the ring, the dangers to him are greater than those with which Eubank struggled. Garcia, one year the younger at 28 but the riper in championships experience, has authentic one-hit-knockout power.

Benn goes into his first world championship fight reliant on the cumulative effect of his non-stop output. The problem with this is that King Ry is probably the best counterpuncher in the world right now and Benn’s headlong style will likely suit him nicely, thank you.

To complicate the evaluation, both have blotted their copybooks as people. Garcia, the handsome heartthrob, burnished his bad-boy rock-star image by trashing a five-star hotel room. He also needed his family’s help with overcoming mental problems aggravated by a passing fancy for social drugs and booze.

Benn invited mockery for claiming initially that he failed his drugs tests because of eating enough eggs to fill the shelves of all the Tescos in London. Then, in order to collect his bonanza from Mister UFC, he unceremoniously dumped his long-time promoter Eddie Hearn who had bankrolled his hefty legal costs and loaned him half a million quid to help sustain his flamboyant lifestyle through that crisis.

Not much to like there.

So, when it comes to the fight, who ya like? The answer is not Conor Benn’s to give. Because the real question is which Ryan Garcia turns up.

If it is the narcissist whose arrogant complacency has cost him a couple of big fights, it may not be totally beyond the bounds of possibility that Conor could pull off one of the major upsets by a British boxer abroad.

If it is King Ry fully prepared and ready to unfurl all the majesty then we can only hope the son of Nigel is not seriously hurt.

Sports.title: Ricky Hatton's mother recalls last hug with boxing champion three days before he took his own life a year ago as parents speak out for first time
Sports.content:
Ricky Hatton's mother has recalled her last hug with him three days before he took his own life one year ago as his parents speak out for the first time.

Carol and Ray Hatton have urged people to tell their friends and family they love them before it's too late after the boxing champion hanged himself on September 14 last year.

One year on from Ricky's death, aged 46, his mother has revealed the last time she embraced her son.

Just days before he took his own life, the boxing champion had been in an argument with his parents but the family were 'building bridges'.

Carol decided to make an unplanned visit to his gym in Hyde and gave him a 'real proper hug'.

She told ITV News: 'I pulled up on the car park because I saw his car. He asked if everything was okay.

'I said "yeah, everything's fine". I said I'd like to see a bit more of him.'

Ricky's mother said he told her he wanted to see his father Ray the next week. However Ricky died three days later.

Former world boxing champion Ricky Hatton died by suicide in September last year aged 46

Ray and Carol Hatton (pictured at their son's funeral) have urged people to tell their friends and family they love them before it's too late

Ricky had previously opened up about his struggle with drug and alcohol addiction and had become estranged from his parents before the reconciled

She added: 'I'm so glad (I got to see him) because nobody knows when it's the last time you're going to see somebody.'

Ray, the boxer's father, said: 'You tell your grandkids how much you love them, you tell your wife how much you love them but I think, especially with men, don't ever be afraid of getting hold of your son and telling him you love him.'

Ricky had become estranged from his parents for around a decade before he reached out to patch up their relationship several years before his death.

He had survived previous suicide attempts and struggled with drug and alcohol addiction.

Ricky fell out with his parents over money and despite the dispute he still allowed Carol and Ray to see his newborn daughter Millie.

However the boxer became upset when his girlfriend Jennifer was not invited to a Christmas Day party.

Months later he received letters from his parents' lawyers saying they wanted to see their granddaughter.

But he told Manchester Evening News in 2013 that he responded by saying: 'I replied to my parents, through solicitors, and said we did not want them to have contact with Millie.'

Carol Hatton wipes a tear from her eye while reading a statement at her home after Ricky's death

Ricky had survived previous suicide attempts before he died in September last year

'We have never stopped them seeing her, as far as I was concerned they had just not been ******.

'I know that sounds harsh and I am sure they see it differently, but it is how I feel.'

He added that the situation 'was a mess', describing the family feud as 'bitter and horrible', referring to back-and-forth letters between his and his parents' lawyers.

This culminated in his father attacking him in a car park fist fight.

Angry about 'all that stuff you've written about your mum in that solicitor's letter', Ray then punched his boxing champion son in the face before Ricky hit back and his father then drove off.

But Ricky's parents are still struggling to come to terms with his death and Carol said the couple 'have to move forward' but will continue 'remembering him and loving him'.

Carol and Ray have now called for a statue of Ricky to be erected in Manchester, saying it would be a 'fitting tribute' to their son who 'brought a lot of pride' to the city.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury looks set for CARDIFF - at 2am: Welsh venue set to waive curfew to take boxing's biggest fight away from Wembley and New York
Sports.content:
Cardiff's Principality Stadium now looks set to be the unlikely winner of the venue war for boxing's biggest fight - by hosting Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury in the early hours of the morning.

The local authorities could today approve lifting the stadium's 10.30pm curfew to host the fight - stepping in after rows over holding it at Wembley Stadium or Madison Square Garden in New York.

Cardiff has history of hosting late-night boxing. Joe Calzaghe fought Mikkel Kessler at the Principality in 2007 at 2am. Fury and Joshua could fight at a similar time to satisfy broadcaster Netflix's huge audience in the United States.

Netflix had wanted the fight in New York to suit their prime timezones, while Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn pitched Wembley to host under the guise that Britain's biggest fight of the century should be hosted in the UK - and he has refused to budge unless contracts are rewritten with upgraded financial offerings.

Cardiff now appears to be the compromise. The Principality Stadium has an 80,000 capacity and a retractable roof - unlike Wembley - which could be useful in late November or December. A date of Saturday, November 28 has been mooted.

The Times report a press conference is tentatively scheduled for next week pending the approval.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua could now be set to fight in Cardiff, Wales in November

Joshua and his camp wanted the fight in the UK - while broadcasters Netflix wanted a US host

Wembley looked an ideal venue for the fight but the strict 11pm curfew has been a sticking point, despite London mayor Sadiq Khan saying he wanted to ensure allowances were made to host the fight.

Boxing dealmaker Turki Al-Sheikh has been insistent on a start time of 2am.

Netflix have been running s for Fury-Joshua as recently as Thursday night, clearly confident an agreement will be struck.

The streaming giant has yet to sign off on Cardiff but American sportswriter Dan Rafael last night reported he had asked Netflix if they would approve, with a source telling him: 'I think they're OK.'

A spokesperson for the Welsh Rugby Union said: 'We'd be delighted to host this fight.

'We are very keen to attract more boxing to the stadium, which has a rich history in the sport, enhanced by its closable roof, unrivalled sight lines and unique city-centre location.'

Joe Calzaghe trains at the Principality Stadium before his 2am fight there in 2007

Joshua has fought in Cardiff twice previously, beating Carlos Takam and Joseph Parker in the Welsh capital in 2017 and 2018.

While Joshua has left Hearn to do the talking on his side of the deal, Fury has been publicly speaking and threatening that the heavyweight contest will be called off.

This week he suggested he will no longer be fighting Joshua in another social media rant as rows over the location and contract surrounding the fight continued.

'So it looks like AJ has s*** his pants yet again,' Fury said on social media on Sunday. 'After 11 years, he's finally s*** his pants yet again.'

Last week, Fury, who regularly takes to social media to express his views on potential opponents, was keen to make clear he feels Joshua is not motivated by a love of his country. Earlier this year Daily Mail Sport revealed Joshua had in fact quit the UK to move to Dubai – even as thousands tried to flee amid rising panic in the Middle East warzone.

And Fury, a tax exile to the Isle of Man himself, brought up a 2020 speech at a Black Lives Matter march, where Joshua read out a letter from his friend Reece Campbell to urge attendees to stop spending money with white-owned shops and businesses.

'Show them where it hurts', Joshua had said. 'Abstain from spending your money in their shops and economies, and invest in black-owned businesses.'

Fury re-posted the video of the speech, writing: 'This is the man who loves England, absolute s*** bag! Total piece of s*** bully with zero guts! Don't let them deceive you! & Living in Dubai.'

Provided Cardiff hits no further stumbling blocks, the Welsh capital may now offer the solution to get the fight on at last.

Sports.title: What made Red Bull so fast in the Azerbaijan GP after Verstappen’s qualifying issue
Sports.content:
Red Bull might consider the FIA’s assessment that it has the strongest power unit as a blessing and a curse, but at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix it was key to its first double Formula 1 podium.

After fixing Max Verstappen’s ill-behaving internal combustion engine after qualifying, an issue that triggered his painful Q3 which left him eighth on the grid, both he and team-mate Isack Hadjar were able to demonstrate Red Bull’s prowess in Baku to surge up to second and third respectively.

It marked Red Bull’s first double podium in almost two-and-a-half years and left the team accepting a victory would have been more likely without Verstappen’s qualifying woes.

But where did this turn of pace come from having been considered to have the fourth-fastest car on the grid for long periods of this season?

Red Bull team boss Laurent Mekies detailed a couple of factors, starting with its Red Bull-Ford power unit: “We have a fantastic PU, we have a fairly narrow band to use it at best. And it takes a lot of energy from everyone back in Milton Keynes and on the race track to try to keep us on the narrow window of performance. So that's what we do every day, there was nothing different this weekend.

“Every track comes with this challenge on how you do that and you hear it with our radio communications, with our drivers. So getting the right energy management, getting the right deployment and getting the right power is certainly something that keeps us busy.”

Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

As is well documented, Red Bull has the most powerful internal combustion engine on the grid, and getting it into the “fairly narrow band” along with optimising electrical deployment meant it had plenty of punch on Baku’s straights. Red Bull’s sister squad, Racing Bulls, which runs the same engines, topped the speed trap in the race with Liam Lawson clocking 349.4km/h, while both Verstappen and Hadjar sat into the top 10 for highest speeds.

It was a tool that gave both drivers the ability to carve through the frontrunners and Mekies acknowledged had it not been for Verstappen’s engine problem in qualifying, an even better result was possible.

“We had two different issues in terms of power units,” he said. “It has cost us a lot yesterday [in qualifying]. But that's what it is, that's part of the game.

“I think in fairness Max was very strong from Friday onwards and probably would have been fighting for that first row or more yesterday without the issues we had with the PU. So of course, fixing that today [in the race] with the new engine has allowed us to go back to the competitive level that we were hoping to have.”

Verstappen felt Baku was Red Bull’s best – and potentially last – chance of a first win in 2026 with dominant squad Mercedes set to deliver a major upgrade package next weekend at the Bahrain GP in Malaysia.

Mekies echoed the common theme of upgrades having a major influence on the performance order in F1 this season and, despite his team admitting it will not deliver another major update package this year, he remains optimistic it will still have opportunities to avoid a first win-less F1 season for the team since 2015.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Alex Pantling / LAT Images via Getty Images

“We have seen this year the pecking order has been alternating based on the timing of the upgrades,” he said. “I think what is however important is that in the fairly long timeframe between Australia and here, where we didn't have a big package coming, we have nonetheless managed to close that gap.

“If you look at Madrid, we were a tenth-and-a-half from pole in Madrid, I think we were two tenths from pole in Monza. So we have managed to close that gap with everyone in the team, chassis side, PU side, extracting from the actual car specifications. And then yes, the upgrades today probably gave us another edge and has eaten up that last tenth.

“We need to see how it's lasting on other tracks and then how we will react to the other competitors.”

Sports.title: Norris apologises to Colapinto over F1 race ban comments
Sports.content:
Reigning world champion Lando Norris has apologised to Franco Colapinto for demanding a race ban for the Alpine driver after the collision at Formula 1’s Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Colapinto caused a pile-up at the lap 36 restart by locking up into Turn 1 of the slippery Baku street circuit, which eliminated himself, team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren’s Norris.

Norris was left furious by the accident, feeling Colapinto's careless driving should be punished harshly by F1's race stewards.

"I've not seen it. I just got taken out. I think the FIA should be stricter and start handing out bans for this kind of stuff," Norris vented.

"It's careless from people. It costs a lot of money. All my parts are in the bin now. People should just get banned, because that's not driving that deserves to be in Formula 1."

When asked if there were mitigating circumstances for what happened on the slippery Baku circuit, Norris added: "In Formula 1, I think you expect drivers to anticipate things.

“Grip is going to be low. Tyre temps are low, they weren't even that low. In Formula 1, we want to be against the best drivers in the world, and when stuff like this happens, it's because [they] shouldn't be there.

Franco Colapinto, Alpine, Lando Norris, McLaren, Pierre Gasly, Alpine Photo by: Michael Potts / LAT images via Getty Images

"I've not seen it, but if you cause a crash in a restart like this, you should have at least a one-race ban."

With the benefit of two days to reflect on the incident, Norris has now rowed back those comments and says he has privately apologised to Colapinto, having sparked further online abuse that has overshadowed the Argentinian's F1 career.

"Tough weekend overall in Baku and of course a disappointing and early end to the race," Norris posted on social media.

"After the race, I sent Franco a message apologising for the comments I made that I simply should not have said.

“I know better and emotions were running high but that is not an excuse, it was wrong of me. I've made mistakes of my own over the years and I know this is very much a part of racing and fighting on the limit.

"Me and Franco came to a good understanding, are still good friends and are both excited to get back racing this weekend."

Colapinto took responsibility for his "big mistake", which also angered Alpine chief Flavio Briatore as it cost the team a double points finish.

Sports.title: Why McLaren was so much slower than Mercedes on Baku's straights
Sports.content:
For all the talk of rivals catching Mercedes, which has held fire on its more significant upgrades until next weekend's Formula 1 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, the Brackley team has been able to weather the storm by excelling on some of the most power sensitive circuits like Monza and Baku, vindicating its patience.

But while Mercedes' dominant power unit package helps explain its gap to Ferrari and Red Bull, George Russell's scarcely believable eight-tenth gap to McLaren's Oscar Piastri was less straightforward to digest. Lando Norris fared even worse, 1.1s behind in Baku qualifying.

Read Also: Formula 1 Why Mercedes is still quicker than McLaren

Compared to Piastri, Russell made the difference by having better energy deployment through sector two, before motoring away on Baku's ultra-long straight, where his top speed was up to 10km/h higher than the Australian. In the race, Russell also enjoyed a leisurely cruise until a double safety car made things interesting for him at the end, setting up a grandstand finish with Max Verstappen.

When gaps between two otherwise closely matched teams sharing the same power unit are so vast, there are usually several compounding factors at play, and that's also what appeared to be the case in Azerbaijan.

To begin with, Baku isn't McLaren's happiest of hunting grounds. The MCL40 has continued a trend from its predecessors in that it's not the most competitive in low-speed corners, which the 6km Baku circuit almost exclusively features. McLaren's high-downforce prowess, which yielded wins in Hungary and Zandvoort and should have led to another victory for Norris in Madrid, counted for little.

McLaren's other aerodynamic weakness, a relative lack of efficiency on the straights, was also exposed despite the team bringing a suite of upgrades to generate more efficient downforce in all corner types. "The upgrades worked well throughout the weekend, we added some lap time to the car," said team boss Andrea Stella. "Somehow, we didn't see the effect of the upgrades because our car in general does not perform very well in these kinds of corners, so we would have needed a much bigger set to make a difference in Baku."

Without wanting to overlook Russell's return to form either, that again doesn't explain a gap of eight tenths. While McLaren feels its understanding of its Mercedes power unit, and its collaboration with Mercedes HPP, has improved compared to the start of the year, Stella acknowledged the team hadn't optimised its power unit as well for the race as it did in qualifying "and we paid a price in the race".

GPS traces provided by GP-Tempo show McLaren's shorter gearing compared to Mercedes. Comparing their fastest qualifying laps, Piastri (orange trace) was shifting up noticeably earlier than Russell (teal) Photo by: GP-Tempo.com

One baked in factor contributing to a top-speed deficit is the gear ratios it picked at the start of the year. The MCL40 is geared shorter than the Mercedes, costing it some top end speed on the likes of Monza and Baku.

"If we had to do it again, I think we would re-ratio to be closer to where Mercedes are," McLaren's technical director Neil Houldey said earlier this summer. "There are some performance opportunities that we can take because the ratios are shorter. We end up shifting less into lower gears around corners, potentially on restarts, things like that.

"But then when you're looking at the high-speed side, I think you'd probably take what the other teams have got. So it's a couple of compromises in either direction. It's a small lap time, but all these small little lap times add up to be some decent lap time performance."

McLaren elected not to use its one joker to make a mid-season gearing adjustment, opting to spend resources elsewhere instead.

"It is very apparent that it is not a single factor," said Stella. "Certainly, we've always talked quite openly and transparently that we need to improve the aerodynamic drag of the car. But at the same time there's a few factors which refer to our ratios, for instance we need to look whether we are on the right ratios to compete in circuits in which you have this sort of top speeds.

"And at the same time when we look at the data and we compare with MGP, we see that our power unit was not optimised. I think while for qualifying we managed to exploit pretty much the most that was available in the power unit, there's a few items that we were not able to optimise, and we paid a price in the race."

Lando Norris was collateral damage in Franco Colapinto's Turn 1 clash with Pierre Gasly Photo by: Alex Pantling / LAT Images via Getty Images

As to why Norris, who had been hitting his best form yet over the summer, had such a difficult weekend compared to an improving Piastri, it turns out the world champion had his own specific gremlins to deal with. The team found a power deficit in qualifying, believed to be linked to a fuel injection issue, that returned in the grand prix, while Norris didn't have his cleanest race and struggled for pace on the medium tyres.

"We occasionally saw the same problem during the race, but not as systematic as in qualifying," Stella explained. "Definitely there's a significant opportunity on the topic of fuel injection that we see occasionally also on Oscar's car during the race.

"In addition to that, Lando was overtaken by Verstappen, who was a quicker car. Lando was struggling a bit with the medium tyres. But credit to Oscar, Oscar managed to keep Verstappen behind. On Lando's side, we were struggling a little bit with power unit deployment.

"And also, Lando was having some inconsistencies in his driving, when he was overtaken by Hamilton, he had a lock-up and he had a few mistakes that meant that cars behind were within range. And when they are within range, then we struggle to defend, which goes back to the point on top speed."

Norris was furious after being a collateral victim of Alpine's Franco Colapinto spearing into his team-mate Pierre Gasly. But the Briton contributed to his own downfall by going off at Turn 1 right before the safety car, which cost him three positions and dumped him into the danger zone on the subsequent restart.

"I would say that for Lando this was one of the most difficult events in general that he has experienced in 2026," Stella concluded. "It's something that we need to take away, looking at whatever can be improved. But I would say most of the opportunities lie on the team side and on the car side, because we need to be able to offer our drivers a car that is more and just more consistent in terms of predictability."

Oscar Piastri suffered a monumental lock-up trying to hold off Isack Hadjar Photo by: Alex Pantling / LAT Images via Getty Images

With Piastri also locking up at Turn 1 later on, costing him a potential podium as he dropped down to 13th at the finish, the bitter end result of a series of minor problems, execution errors and shortcomings is a point-less weekend for the Woking squad.

"We had issues and some mistakes, but at the same time I think we paid for some fundamental limitations of our package in this kind of circuit," Stella's concluded.

"We were not fast enough in the corners, but at the same time and mainly we were not fast enough in the straights. This continuously exposed our drivers to being attacked and having to spend their race watching the mirrors rather than thinking about how they can progress in the race."

Sports.title: Alpine condemns abuse again following Colapinto's Azerbaijan GP crash
Sports.content:
The Alpine Formula 1 team has again spoken out against social media abuse following Franco Colapinto’s shunt in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Argentinian fans’ behaviour has been scrutinised lately following waves of hateful comments. Those were aimed at FIA stewards and the Alpine squad when Colapinto was handed a drive-through penalty for overtaking under a double yellow flag in Zandvoort.

Pierre Gasly was at the receiving end of abuse too after the Frenchman briefly refused to let his Alpine team-mate through in Madrid. Gasly revealed the threats targeted his family too; Colapinto meekly labelled the behaviour as “not nice to see” while insisting it was ‘not just his fans’.

This weekend in Baku, Colapinto lost control and caused a pile-up at a safety car restart, taking both Gasly and Lando Norris out of the race. The reigning champion was particularly upset and, before being able to view the footage himself, suggested whoever caused the crash should get “at least a one-race ban”.

While Norris did not even refer to Colapinto by name, this did trigger abuse on social media yet again – mainly aimed at the Briton, but Gasly and others weren’t spared.

“Mistakes happen when racing at the limit and no matter the result or outcome, nobody should be subject to hateful or abusive comments,” Alpine insisted in a statement on Sunday.

The team made a point of not antagonising its own driver’s fanbase: “Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport.

Franco Colapinto, Alpine Photo by: Bryn Lennon / Formula 1 via Getty Images

“As we have said in previous instances, we strongly condemn the reaction of some fans online and stand in solidarity with Formula One, the FIA, and other teams in wanting to stamp it out. It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned.”

The latest abuse has occurred shortly after Alpine F1 boss Flavio Briatore reportedly threatened Argentinian media not to let them speak to Colapinto again if the hatred kept being spewed, damaging the outfit’s reputation.

Alpine’s statement in full

“As a team, we feel it’s necessary to speak out once more about the hate and abuse online following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Not only aimed at one of our own drivers, but also members of the Formula One community, including media, and to our racing counterparts who we respect, admire, and revel competing against in the pinnacle of motorsport. Mistakes happen when racing at the limit and no matter the result or outcome, nobody should be subject to hateful or abusive comments.

“Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport. As we have said in previous instances, we strongly condemn the reaction of some fans online and stand in solidarity with Formula One, the FIA, and other teams in wanting to stamp it out. It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned.

“We know as a proud participant and stakeholder in the sport, we hold a responsibility to speak out and also help support in finding a solution. We will continue to work closely with the championship promoter and rights-holder, and the governing body to discuss ways in which to tackle online abuse and encourage healthy sporting rivalry, which Formula One is renowned for and what makes it so special.”

Sports.title: The detail that impressed Red Bull the most about Hadjar's F1 return
Sports.content:
After his wrist injury, Isack Hadjar certainly did not return behind the wheel of the Red Bull Racing RB22 at the easiest track on the Formula 1 calendar. The Baku City Circuit not only carries a considerable risk of crashes, but also features several very technical sections around the city's old town.

It requires confidence, but Hadjar had plenty of it despite missing three race weekends – having already made clear after practice that his wrist would not be a limiting factor.

Hadjar qualified fourth on the shores of the Caspian Sea and then produced a faultless race to claim his second podium of the season and his third F1 podium overall. His race weekend in Baku impressed Red Bull, Mekies acknowledged when addressing the written media post-race.

"I think it was outstanding what Isack has produced this weekend, really outstanding," Red Bull's team principal said. "At first, the most important thing is that straight away he felt good in the car, no pain. It means that every time we met together in the last few weeks and we said we will wait for Isack to come back at 100% because that's the priority, well, that's what happened.

"He was in the car, he didn't have any pain. Nonetheless, even without pain, this is not an easy track to come back to because there is no margin for error."

Hadjar himself was well aware of the latter and therefore built up his weekend steadily at one of the most treacherous street circuits.

"He has been building up his rhythm, session after session, very calmly, and with a lot of positive energy," Mekies added. "Already yesterday, to stick the car in P4 was a very, very strong result. I think today, the sort of race pace that he has shown on the medium and on the soft, is something we had not seen before.

Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

"So on the weekend of his return, he has raised the bar again. We say to each other very often that we have seen him adding something to the business every time he was going out on track in the first part of the season, and he is continuing to do that."

Red Bull impressed by Hadjar's mature radio communication

Aside from his outright pace, there is another aspect that impressed Mekies: the way Hadjar conducted himself during the first stint. Red Bull asked the young Frenchman to give up his position to Verstappen, but even when the four-time world champion struggled with Pirelli's medium tyre, Hadjar remained calm.

"And on top of that, allow me to say that he also raced extremely cleverly with Max, very disciplined with his tyres," Mekies said. "It allowed us to have very, very strong teamwork between the two of them and between the pitwall. That has ultimately produced the best result possible."

It underlines that Hadjar is also making progress in that respect. In the junior categories and during the first year of his F1 career, Hadjar could often come across as hot-headed over the team radio, but Saturday in Baku was the exact opposite.

Of course, after several laps Hadjar asked whether he was free to attack – to which the team responded that he had to keep it clean – but the radio communication that preceded it was telling. When asked how much quicker Hadjar could go in clean air, the man behind the wheel replied: "Two or three tenths, but I’m honestly happy to be here."

In other words, Hadjar did not need the position back, thereby maximising the race time of both drivers and, with it, Red Bull’s chances. When Autosport asked Mekies about this specific moment, it was clear that this is what impressed the team principal most of all.

Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

"I think you are pinpointing exactly on the right details that make you understand a lot more about the right pictures," Mekies said.

"It shows you how cleverly the kid is racing, and how much of brain capacity he is developing while in the car, and also how much emotional control he is managing to have.

"Those are as many indicators of the steps he has made in all these areas, on top of producing more speed. So it's exactly that trajectory that has been impressing us every day since he has joined the team, and probably last year as well.

"And also for that, we want to give him the best possible environment to continue to develop because that step was truly impressive."

Providing that best possible environment includes the contract extension for 2027 and the timing of it. Mekies acknowledges that Red Bull deliberately did so to take all the pressure off Hadjar’s shoulders, and as he walks away at the end of the media session, Mekies laughs: "I think Isack repaid our faith today!"

Sports.title: Colapinto handed Sepang penalty for causing Baku F1 pile-up
Sports.content:
Franco Colapinto has been given a five-place grid penalty for the Malaysian Grand Prix, following the pile-up he caused in today’s Formula 1 race at Baku.

The Azerbaijan GP was neutralised by the safety car when Alexander Albon crashed out shortly after mid-race, but Colapinto had a monumental lock-up on the inside at the restart. The Alpine driver careened into Pierre Gasly’s sister car, which in turn crashed into Lando Norris’ McLaren.

A livid Norris called for Colapinto to get a race ban – one should point out he did so before viewing a replay of the incident – but the stewards opted for a 10-second penalty, which they converted into a five-place grid drop for the Sepang race, given the offender failed to finish today’s event.

Read Also: Formula 1 Norris demands ban for Colapinto after Azerbaijan GP crash

“The Stewards reviewed video, timing and in-car video evidence,” the stewards’ report read.

“Following the restart, COL approached GAS from behind into Turn 1. COL braked too late and entered the corner on the inside at a speed which did not allow him to make the corner in a controlled manner. He overshot the corner and made contact with the left-hand side of GAS, who then hit NOR and both cars retired.

“The Stewards considered that COL was wholly or predominantly to blame for the collision. Although the incident occurred at the first corner following the restart, there was no contribution from another driver which would justify applying the first-lap / [first-corner] more [lenient] approach.

“The standard penalty for causing a collision is a 10-second time penalty. As COL had retired from the Race and was therefore unable to serve the time penalty, the Stewards converted the penalty to a drop of 5 grid positions at the next Race in which the driver participates in accordance which Article B1.9.6.(e) of the FIA 2026 F1 Regulations.”

Why Arvid Lindblad got no penalty

Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Alex Pantling / LAT Images via Getty Images

Meanwhile, the stewards have explained why they took no further action on Arvid Lindblad spinning his Racing Bulls team-mate Liam Lawson at the exact same time – the reason being that incident was influenced by the Colapinto shunt.

“Following the restart, LIN and LAW approached Turn 1, with LIN in a three-car situation,” they wrote.

“Ahead of them, a collision occurred involving COL, GAS and NOR. That incident, together with COL locking his brakes, triggered a braking reaction among the cars immediately ahead of LIN. At the same time, LIN was positioned between cars on either side.”

“During the corner, LIN made contact with LAW. Having reviewed the positioning and movement of the cars involved, the Stewards determined that the contact was primarily the result of the restricted space available to LIN and the chain reaction caused by the incident ahead, rather than any action or error for which LIN could be considered wholly or predominantly to blame.

“The Stewards therefore considered this to be a typical first-corner incident following a restart, with no driver predominantly to blame.”

Sports.title: Why Verstappen says 0.196s Baku finish-line gap to Russell is slightly misleading
Sports.content:
At the Baku City Circuit, the words Russell spoke after qualifying became reality: the Mercedes driver had already predicted on Friday that, despite starting eighth, Verstappen would pose the biggest threat for victory, and that proved to be the case in a thrilling finale around the streets of Baku.

Verstappen fell just 0.196 seconds short of his first victory of the 2026 Formula 1 season at the line, although he stressed afterwards that the actual gap was slightly larger than that.

"Of course, it looked close on the line, but I think that was more because George suffered from a little bit of boost lag in Turn 15 with the yellow flag", Verstappen said.

"So if you look at the last stint, it was always one second, so that’s probably also where we would have finished."

It is a theory that Russell himself also confirms. After lifting off for Valtteri Bottas’ crash, the Mercedes power unit did not immediately deliver the acceleration he was expecting.

"When the yellow flag came out, I lifted off the power and when I went back on, I had no turbo, so then I had no power”, the Mercedes driver explained. “Max almost got me at the line. That would have been a real shame, but all in all, it’s been an incredible weekend."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Alex Pantling / LAT Images via Getty Images

Verstappen also believes the outcome of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix would have been the same had he started from the front row.

On Friday, the four-time world champion concluded that Red Bull had "done a great job messing up" its best chance of a victory this year with the engine problem, but 24 hours later Verstappen believes the closing stages of the race would have played out in more or less the same way.

"I mean, that’s what happened yesterday. You have a problem and that means that you have to start from P8. But I think even if I started second, I think with the pace of George, it would have been very hard to pass", the Dutchman admitted.

"So maybe I could have followed him a bit better in that first stint, of course. But then you box, you’re second, and then we would probably have done the same race, just pushing each other along."

Verstappen able to enjoy F1 for one of the first times in 2026

Verstappen does, however, say that he enjoyed the closing stages in Baku, which, given all the shortcomings of the technical regulations, was one of the first times he had done so all year.

"I have to say that those last laps were very enjoyable because there was barely any deg, really. We were just pushing to the end and the gap was always, like, one second or 1.1. That was nice."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

Verstappen also took risks in that respect, risks he perhaps would not have taken for any result other than a potential race win. He knew Red Bull – especially with overtake mode – had an impressive amount of top speed, while Mercedes was faster in the twisty section around Baku’s old town.

To still give himself a chance on the longest straight of the F1 calendar and at least close the gap again on every lap, Verstappen tried to ‘open up’ the final few corners as much as possible.

"That last stint was fun. I kissed a few walls as well, but that was just to leave my mark here in Baku!", Verstappen smiled.

"So, yeah, it’s always very challenging around here, qualifying and now at the end of the race as well, just pushing flat out. That comes with risk, of course, being close to certain walls on the inside and the outside, but it was cool."

Read Also: Formula 1 Top 10 F1 closest finishes

Sports.title: Briatore to reflect on necessary action after Colapinto's "poor" Baku blunder
Sports.content:
Alpine F1 executive Flavio Briatore has been left "extremely disappointed" with his team's double DNF in F1's Azerbaijan GP, criticising Franco Colapinto for "a very poor move" to take out team-mate Peirre Gasly.

On a lap 36 restart, Colapinto locked his front tyres on the dusty, low-grip inside of the Baku street circuit, slamming into the side of Pierre Gasly, taking both drivers out of the race. McLaren driver Lando Norris was also collected in the incident, which robbed Alpine of a likely double points finish.

Both Gasly and Norris were upset with Colapinto's driving, with the latter even going as far as calling for the FIA to consider a one-race ban for careless driving behaviour.

Colapinto's boss Briatore was also distinctly unimpressed and didn't shy away from criticising the Argentinian.

"Obviously I'm extremely disappointed with the outcome of today's race, knowing we lost valuable points in the Championship fight," Briatore was quoted in Alpine's post-race press release.

"These sorts of incidents shouldn't happen, particularly when we were running well with both cars in point-scoring positions. I feel very sorry for the team and for Pierre who did a great job all weekend and my apologies also go to Lando and McLaren for ruining their race.

"I know that Franco has taken full responsibility for it, as he should; in fact, he braked far too late considering the context of the race and the safety car restart. It was a very poor move for a driver of his experience."

Franco Colapinto, Alpine, Pierre Gasly, Alpine Photo by: Alex Pantling / LAT Images via Getty Images

Briatore said he would consider his next steps after the incident to avoid a future repeat. "I want to take time to reflect on it and consider what course of action should be taken, so we can learn from it and avoid such a situation in future," the Italian said.

Colapnto's Baku blunder comes after the 23-year-old had been enjoying his strongest spell of form in F1 to date, earning him a new Alpine deal for the 2027 season to remain alongside Gasly at the Enstone-based team.

Verstappen passed Hadjar at the beginning of lap seven. Red Bull told Hadjar not to put up a fight against his team mate: his race engineer Richard Wood pointed out “race time is priority here”:

Sports.title: Norris apologised to Colapinto for saying he “shouldn’t be in Formula 1” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris has revealed he apologised to Franco Colapinto for the comments he made about him following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The reigning world champion slated the Alpine driver for triggering a three-car collision which eliminated the pair and Colapinto’s team mate Pierre Gasly

Following the crash Norris said he “just got taken out” and “some drivers […] shouldn’t be in Formula 1 to be honest.” He also called for Colapinto to face a race ban for triggering the collision.

However in a social media post two days later Norris said he has cleared the air with Colapinto.

“[A] tough weekend overall in Baku and of course a disappointing and early end to the race,” he said.

“After the race, I sent Franco a message apologising for the comments I made that I simply should not have said. I know better and emotions were running high but that is not an excuse, it was wrong of me. I’ve made mistakes of my own over the years and I know this is very much a part of racing and fighting on the limit.

“Me and Franco came to a good understanding, are still good friends and are both excited to get back racing this weekend.”

Yesterday Alpine issued a statement criticising abusive social media comments aimed at multiple people following the crash.

Sports.title: Alpine condemn online abuse again: “It has become a regular occurrence” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Alpine has issued another condemnation of social media abuse following the reaction to the crash triggered by Franco Colapinto yesterday.

Further abusive comments targeted various people involved in yesterday’s crash. Lando Norris , who sharply criticised Colapinto’s driving, was among those who received abusive messages.

“As a team, we feel it’s necessary to speak out once more about the hate and abuse online following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix,” said Alpine in a statement. “Not only aimed at one of our own drivers, but also members of the Formula One community, including media, and to our racing counterparts who we respect, admire, and revel competing against in the pinnacle of motorsport. Mistakes happen when racing at the limit and no matter the result or outcome, nobody should be subject to hateful or abusive comments.

“Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport. As we have said in previous instances, we strongly condemn the reaction of some fans online and stand in solidarity with Formula One, the FIA, and other teams in wanting to stamp it out. It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned.

“We know as a proud participant and stakeholder in the sport, we hold a responsibility to speak out and also help support in finding a solution. We will continue to work closely with the championship promoter and rights-holder, and the governing body to discuss ways in which to tackle online abuse and encourage healthy sporting rivalry, which Formula One is renowned for and what makes it so special.”

Alpine’s statement comes just three days after the FIA condemned the abuse aimed at Alpine’s other driver, Pierre Gasly, who was attacked by supporters of Colapinto for briefly delaying his team mate during the Spanish Grand Prix.

The FIA also defended its stewards last month following further abuse by supporters of Colapinto over the two penalties he received in the Dutch Grand Prix.

Sports.title: Final laps of Azerbaijan GP “exceptionally fun” because tyres didn’t degrade – Russell | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell said the final stint of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix was an exciting challenge because the tyres performed so well.

Formula 1’s high-degradation tyres ordinarily do not allow drivers to push flat-out continuously. However Pirelli’s selection for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix proved unusually durable.

Russell spent the final laps of the race being pursued by Max Verstappen. Both drivers were running the soft tyre but found they didn’t have to manage it as much as usual and could drive closer to the limit.

“Max and I spoke about this,” said Russell, “the final stint, I think, is the most fun I’ve had in a race for as long as I can remember because the tyre felt great.

“We were pushing flat-out every single lap. It was like qualifying, one after another. You needed to be so alert around this circuit because the walls are so close, especially through the castle. You’re threading the needle.”

Verstappen was seldom more than a second behind Russell following the final Safety Car restart but never got close enough to attempt a pass.

“Those final 10 laps felt really, really fun. It almost felt like the stories I hear of the drivers in the early-mid-2000s, when every lap was like a qualifying lap. The heart rate is higher, you’re pushing the limit every single lap, there’s no management.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

While F1 has faced criticism this year as its power unit regulations force drivers to conserve energy, Russell pointed out that tyre management often continues to prevent them from pushing flat-out.

“We’ve had a lot of conversations this year about [power unit] energy management, but the tyre management is still there and it has been there for years and years,” he said. “But just with how the temperatures and the circuit fell out today, with the tyres there was no management, and that was exceptionally fun.”

Verstappen also enjoyed the final laps of the race.

“The last stint was fun,” he said. “I kissed a few walls as well, just to leave my mark here in Baku.

“It’s always very challenging around here, qualifying and in the race now at the end as well, just pushing flat-out. It comes with risk, being close to certain walls on the inside, the outside. But it’s cool.”

Sports.title: Hadjar says Red Bull made clear performance gain with car during his absence | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar said he immediately felt an improvement in performance from Red Bull’s car when he returned from injury this weekend.

He finished on the podium in his first race having sat out the last three rounds with a wrist injury. Hadjar said he immediately felt confident in the car around the Baku City Circuit

“Baku is a very specific track, specific Tarmac. But to me, the way the car was behaving in terms of through-corner balance this weekend, from lap one in FP1, I was like, ‘Okay, this is looking pretty good.’

“Then the second half of the car, we’re lacking compared to Mercedes, definitely. But in terms of handling on the brakes, the car was, to me, compared to Budapest, it definitely did a step. So I’m really pleased with that.”

Hadjar finished on the podium earlier in the season in Monaco but called yesterday’s result “an actual first proper podium on pure pace.”

“The Monaco podium, of course it was a podium, but it was not on pure pace, not because I qualified in the top three or whatever,” he said. “I felt like this is my first time with the team that I actually get to do a very clean weekend and actually, like, fight my way into that podium.

!So actually, for me, it feels like a real first and it gives me good confidence heading into the next races.”

Sports.title: Chris Eubank Jr Offers to Rescue Fury–Joshua
Sports.content:
Chris Eubank Jr says he’ll stop dieting and step in if Tyson Fury’s December 11 fight with Anthony Joshua falls through. He’s joking, but he picked his moment well. The heavyweights have a signed fight in Cardiff, yet arguments over Dana White’s role and drug testing are already competing with the fight itself for attention.

“If Fury vs AJ falls through… I’ll stop dieting, put the extra lbs back on & step up to the plate. Let me know boys,” said Eubank Jr. on X.

Eubank tagged both men and showed a scale reading of 206 pounds. He’s carrying a paunch, too. It’s a funny reveal from a fighter whose recent bouts were at middleweight, and he surely knows that putting on weight does not prepare him for Fury or Joshua.

Junior also knows how to get his name beside a huge payday without agreeing to a fight. One post has put him into the Fury–Joshua conversation, even though there is no sign that either camp wants him as an opponent. It costs him nothing, gets people talking, and lets him take a shot at a promotion that is giving him plenty of material.

The joke works because fans have waited years for Fury and Joshua to meet. A contract and a date should have settled the question of whether they will fight. Instead, the public is hearing about disagreements before the first press conference. Those disputes do not mean either man plans to pull out, but they give Eubank’s line an audience.

If the Cardiff main event collapses, finding another fight that can fill the same stadium and carry the same broadcast would be difficult. Eubank against either heavyweight would attract curiosity, but it would be a size mismatch sold on celebrity. His post gets a laugh because everyone can see the absurdity—and because, in boxing, a signed Fury–Joshua fight still has people discussing substitutes.

If Fury vs AJ falls through… I’ll stop dieting, put the extra lbs back on & step up to the plate. Let me know boys @anthonyjoshua @Tyson_Fury pic.twitter.com/TVU54krrF5 — Chris Eubank Jr (@ChrisEubankJr) September 28, 2026

Sports.title: Dana White Side Disputes Joshua Contract Clause
Sports.content:
Dana White’s role in Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua has produced a new argument over the wording of Joshua’s contract. Eddie Hearn says White cannot help promote the December 11 fight in Cardiff. White’s side reportedly believes the restriction names his companies but does not name him personally.

That distinction might give White room to appear at the event, but it would do little to ease Hearn’s concern. White is the public face of Zuffa Boxing. If he stands at the podium and promotes Fury–Joshua to a global Netflix audience, few viewers will care whether the event credits list him or his company.

The Sun’s Jack Figg, who questioned White about his involvement, described what he had been told on talkSPORT: “I’ve been told from the other side, from Dana White’s side, that that contract detail includes Zuffa and TKO, not Dana White personally.”

Figg said he had not examined the contracts. Neither agreement has been released, so White’s side of the argument remains an account of its position, not an established reading of Joshua’s deal.

There is more at stake for Hearn than a place on a fight poster. Zuffa has signed former Matchroom fighters Conor Benn and Johnny Fisher, and it now has a UK television presence through Sky Sports. White taking a prominent role in the biggest British heavyweight fight would put that rival promotion in front of a vast audience on Matchroom’s home turf.

White was asked whether he would step aside if his involvement put the fight at risk. He said it was not up to him, without saying who would decide. Figg also said Wednesday’s planned press conference was uncertain.

The fight has a date and venue, but the people behind it still need to agree on what White can actually do. Changing the name beside his face on a poster may not be enough for Hearn.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley’s McKenna Plans Run Into Hernandez
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley wanted to turn his WBO middleweight title into a UK unification fight with IBF champion Aaron McKenna. First, he has to defend it against Yoenli Hernandez. WBO president Gustavo Olivieri says their purse bid is tomorrow, September 29, putting Bentley’s preferred fight on hold while the business of facing his mandatory moves forward.

“TOMORROW-Purse Bid Bentley/Hernandez”

— Gustavo Olivieri, X

McKenna offered Bentley a fight British television could sell easily: two champions, a unification and a local audience that knows both men. Hernandez brings less commercial appeal and a much more dangerous fight on paper. The Cuban comes forward looking for knockouts, which means Bentley could be forced into hard exchanges from the opening rounds. That is a steep price to pay just to keep the McKenna fight within reach.

That makes the risk hard to balance against the reward. Beating Hernandez keeps Bentley’s title and his McKenna plans alive, but it may do little to raise his profile with casual fans. Losing would hand Hernandez the WBO belt and end Bentley’s side of the proposed unification. Hernandez could then pursue McKenna himself.

Bentley would prefer to face Hernandez at home, but he may lose that advantage if another promoter wins the purse bid. A trip abroad would make an already dangerous title defense even harder.

Fighting at home may not help Bentley against Hernandez. A British crowd would urge him to stand and trade when Yoenli comes forward, and that is exactly the fight the Cuban wants. If Bentley lets the crowd set his pace, home advantage could become a liability.

Bentley could avoid Hernandez by giving up the belt, but that would weaken his case for a major fight. He needs the title more than he needs an easier route to McKenna. Hernandez knows it, and tomorrow’s bid brings the matchup one step closer.

Sports.title: Jack Catterall’s Countdown Corners Teofimo Lopez
Sports.content:
Jack Catterall is counting down the days while Teofimo Lopez looks toward a lucrative fight with Ryan Garcia.

On Monday, Catterall tagged Lopez on X: “23 days @TeofimoLopez ⏳.” He is making the mandatory fight difficult to ignore.

The WBA ordered Lopez and Catterall to negotiate on September 22. Its official deadline is October 22, a day later than Catterall’s countdown suggests. If they cannot agree, the WBA may order a purse bid.

Teofimo faces a risky choice. Catterall is a southpaw who can deny him the exchanges he wants, counter when he lunges, and turn twelve rounds into a frustrating night. Lopez has had trouble pinning down cautious opponents before. He recently won the WBA title from Rolando Rolly Romero in August by a narrow 12-round majority decision, with one judge scoring the fight even. Catterall would give him another demanding style to solve, with a much larger payday potentially waiting against Ryan.

If talks break down, Matchroom could win a purse bid and bring the fight to Britain, forcing Teofimo to face Catterall in front of his home crowd. Teofimo wants to fight Ryan in May 2027, but holding on to the WBA belt until then would leave Catterall waiting for a shot he has already earned. Catterall has made it clear he won’t step aside.

If Teofimo gives up the belt just weeks after scraping past Romero, he loses bargaining power for the Ryan Garcia fight. Fans will also ask why he won the title only to walk away when Catterall came calling. Garcia has his own WBC title and drawing power, so the fight could still sell without Lopez’s belt.

Catterall’s countdown puts the pressure on Lopez. If Lopez gives up the belt, the boxing world will watch him walk away from his mandatory challenger in broad daylight.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Faces Bektemir Melikuziev’s Fight or Vacate Demand
Sports.content:
Bektemir Melikuziev wants Jaime Munguia to defend his WBA super middleweight title or give it up. Reports that Munguia’s camp is considering vacating have given that demand an edge: if the champion leaves without a major fight lined up, fans will have reason to ask why he would not face the challenger he was ordered to fight.

“Now it’s simple for Munguia. Fight me, or give up the title. I earned my opportunity. I waited long enough. Now it’s time to fight. There are no more excuses, and no other opponents. I am his mandatory challenger. I earned this position in the ring. When I was already the mandatory, I was asked to step aside, and I agreed to work with the promoters because I was promised that I would be next,” said Melikuziev to The Ring.

Melikuziev earned his mandatory position by beating Darius Fulghum last year. The WBA has now given both camps until October 21 to reach a deal and may call a purse bid if they cannot.

The promotional connection makes the choice more striking. Golden Boy has worked with both fighters and knows Melikuziev’s southpaw stance, pressure, and body attack. Those are genuine risks for Munguia, who can leave openings while pressing forward. None of that proves his team fears the matchup. It does make a decision to surrender the belt harder to explain as an inability to assess the challenger.

Rick Glaser has reported that Munguia’s camp is examining whether to vacate. Munguia has announced no such decision. A purse bid, if one is called, would add uncertainty over who stages the fight, though its outcome cannot be assumed.

Munguia won the belt from Armando Resendiz in May. Since losing to Canelo Alvarez, his run has included a win over Erik Bazinyan, a knockout loss to Bruno Surace, victory in their rematch, and the Resendiz title win.

If he gives up the belt now, a substantial next fight would at least explain the trade. Without one, vacating would look like he wanted the standing of a champion but balked when Bek’s promised opportunity came due. Melikuziev could still pursue a vacant title, but he would lose the chance to take it directly from Munguia.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Risks Ring Rust Against Lucas Bahdi
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield is eager to punish Lucas Bahdi for his pre-fight trash talk. That could be a dangerous way to approach their October 10 lightweight title fight. Schofield has not fought in more than 15 months, and Bahdi has already knocked out one unbeaten prospect who appeared to be in control.

Schofield’s last fight ended in 78 seconds when he stopped Tevin Farmer in June 2025. It was an impressive finish, but it offered no evidence of how his timing or stamina will look after a long layoff. Bahdi presents a different problem from a quick return opponent: he can change a fight with one punch. Schofield made clear that their comments have stayed with him.

“I’m going to beat some ass October 10th. I will be victorious, and I just can’t wait to get in that ring. I got something for all the trash talking that Lucas was doing, him and his team,” said Schofield to MillCity Boxing.

Schofield also said he respects Bahdi as a fighter and a father. Once the fight starts, though, that anger could affect his decisions. If he rushes in looking to make Bahdi pay immediately, he gives a dangerous counterpuncher the exchanges he wants.

Bahdi produced his breakthrough by knocking out Ashton Sylve in 2024 while trailing on the scorecards. He later went twelve rounds to beat Roger Gutierrez, showing he does not need an early knockout to win. Bahdi has had a layoff of his own since that August 2025 victory, so neither man comes in with recent fight activity on his side.

The vacant WBA belt has not generated much buzz by itself. Gervonta Davis is champion in recess, and the Schofield–Bahdi winner will become the active lightweight champion.

Davis may choose other opponents rather than fight the winner, leaving Schofield or Bahdi to carry the belt forward. For Schofield, the more immediate task is staying disciplined if Bahdi survives the opening rounds and starts firing back.

Sports.title: Takuma Inoue Wants More Belts After Nasukawa Win
Sports.content:
Takuma Inoue wants to collect bantamweight belts after beating Tenshin Nasukawa for a second time on September 27. The demand is clear. The harder question is whether he can take one from a champion whose boxing experience matches his own.

“I’m not satisfied with just this one belt. I want to collect more,” said Takuma.

The Ring shared Inoue’s comment after his unanimous decision victory in Tokyo. His WBC title remains secure, and he is now 23-2. But two decision wins over Nasukawa tell us more about Inoue’s ability to handle a talented boxing convert than his chances against the division’s other champions.

Nasukawa’s stoppage of Juan Francisco Estrada earned him another opportunity. It did not erase the difference in professional boxing experience between him and Inoue. Takuma could control their exchanges without proving he can discourage a seasoned bantamweight who keeps pressing after the first counter lands.

The opponent who makes this title chase especially interesting is Seiya Tsutsumi. He already beat Inoue by unanimous decision to take the WBA belt in 2024. Tsutsumi is currently listed by the WBA as champion in recess, while Antonio Vargas holds its world title, so a rematch would require the sanctioning body’s title situation to be resolved. Still, Tsutsumi has done what Nasukawa could not: impose himself on Inoue over twelve rounds.

IBF champion Jose Salas Reyes and WBO champion Christian Medina offer other routes to a second belt. Medina stopped former WBO titleholder Yoshiki Takei, making him a more meaningful test of whether Inoue’s careful, low-output approach can hold up against a champion who brings a genuine finishing threat. Ryosuke Nishida has moved to super bantamweight, and Takei no longer holds the WBO belt; neither should be presented as a current bantamweight unification opponent.

Takuma does not need to fight like his explosive older brother Naoya to be a good champion. He does need to show that his style works against someone beyond Nasukawa. If he wants more belts, Medina or Salas Reyes would give him the chance to prove it.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Pushes Ryan Garcia Fight to May
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia asked Teofimo Lopez to fight in December. Lopez’s answer was May 2027. The two welterweight champions agree that they want a unification fight, but Lopez says a meeting with Garcia’s promoter has already put a later date in view.

Garcia challenged Teofimo on X after asking why other fighters did not want to face him. Teofimo replied that he and Golden Boy Boxing had met for lunch two days after Garcia’s win over Conor Benn.

“We’ve said that a showdown in May 2027 is ideal for the welterweight world championship unification fight,” said Teofimo in response.

That is an expression of preference, not an announced deal. Garcia, the WBC champion, wants to return sooner. Lopez holds the WBA title he won from Rolando Romero in August. If Garcia takes a December fight of his own, the two could still meet in May, provided both retain their belts.

Lopez has a more immediate problem. The WBA has ordered him to face Jack Catterall, with their negotiation period ending October 22. If they fail to agree, the organization may order a purse bid. Lopez cannot simply pencil in a May unification and assume his title will still be available for it.

That order gives Catterall a place in the discussion that neither champion can dismiss through social media. Lopez could fight him, seek an agreement that lets him face Garcia first, or give up the WBA belt. The last option would remove the unification label Lopez used in his reply.

Garcia’s December challenge puts pressure on Lopez to explain what happens between now and May. Lopez’s response puts the same question back on Garcia: if May is already the preferred window, is Ryan asking for the unification early, or asking Lopez to abandon the plan?

Until the Catterall order and the date are settled, their public exchange is a negotiation over timing, with two titles at stake.

Ryan Garcia Pushes Teofimo Lopez Toward December Decision

Garcia has challenged Teofimo to fight in December, turning a possible 2027 welterweight unification into an immediate question for the WBA champion. The timing puts Teofimo in a bind: he has already been ordered to negotiate with Jack Catterall, and Garcia is asking him to make room for a different fight.

“Literally no one really wants the smoke in boxing what’s actually going on??? Yall really scared??? Teo does December sound good to go???” posted Ryan on X with his direct challenge of Teofimo.

Ryan holds the WBC welterweight title, and Lopez won the WBA belt from Rolando Romero in August. Their fight would be a unification, but Lopez has an obligation to Jack Catterall, who earned his shot by beating Shakhram Giyasov. Lopez and Catterall have until October 22 to reach an agreement.

That order gives Catterall a real say in Garcia’s December plan. He has indicated that he wants the Lopez fight rather than a payment to step aside. If Lopez cannot obtain an exception or reach an arrangement with Catterall, he may have to defend the title first or give it up to pursue Garcia. A fight without Lopez’s belt would still be valuable, but it would lose its unification claim and some of Lopez’s bargaining power.

Ryan also gains something by making the challenge publicly. He can show fans that he asked for the biggest available December opponent. If Lopez declines, Garcia can return to his proposed fight with Isaac “Pitbull” Cruz while arguing that he tried to make the unification first. That is a negotiating advantage, though a post alone cannot establish why any eventual fight fails to happen.

December would be a quick turnaround for both men. Garcia fought only two rounds against Benn; Lopez went twelve with Romero and was cut and shaken during their August bout. That makes Garcia’s proposed timing understandable from his side, but it does not establish that Lopez would be drained or unprepared.

A major fight would still need a contract, a date, a venue, and a broadcast agreement in the coming weeks. Ryan has put Lopez on the clock in public. Catterall and the WBA have already put him on one in writing. Lopez’s response to the mandatory order will say more about the prospects for December than either champion’s next callout.

Ghana News.title: GNAT rejects gov’t fresh assurances, demands implementation of August 31 agreement
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT) has rejected fresh assurances from the government over the concerns that triggered the ongoing teachers’ strike, insisting that the August 31 agreement must first be implemented.

The Ministry of Education has renewed its appeal to striking pre-tertiary teachers to return to the classroom, despite the unions’ refusal to call off their indefinite industrial action.

GNAT Head of Salaries, Isaac Baah, said the union is unwilling to call off the strike based on another round of promises, arguing that similar commitments were made during an earlier meeting involving the relevant stakeholders.

“We have not changed our stand. Because we have heard this one before,” he said on JoyNews’ The Pulse.

According to Mr Baah, GNAT met the Education Minister and other stakeholders on August 31, where specific commitments were reached on the placement of promoted teachers on the salary scale.

He said the agreement stated that all promoted teachers would be placed on their respective salary scales by the end of September 2026, with supplementary payrolls to be raised for any affected teachers who remained unpaid.

The agreement also provided that placement would be done automatically, meaning promoted teachers would not be required to submit payslips, forms or applications.

Mr Baah said the commitments were agreed to and signed at the meeting, which also had the Controller and Accountant-General present.

He questioned why teachers should accept fresh assurances when the earlier agreement is yet to be fully implemented.

“We are saying that we have an agreement that was signed on August 31. Why should we believe you again?” he asked.

He further criticised what he described as additional validation requirements being introduced for promoted teachers.

According to him, the Ghana Education Service (GES) already conducts the promotion process and submits a master list of successful candidates to the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department (CAGD) for placement.

He argued that requiring teachers to submit their promotion letters or other documents again creates unnecessary delays.

“Placement on scale shall be done automatically,” he stressed, insisting that the process should be seamless once the promotion exercise has been completed and the master list submitted.

GNAT is therefore demanding concrete implementation of the August 31 commitments, rather than further assurances, before considering a return to the classroom.

The union is among the teacher groups that began an indefinite strike on September 25 over outstanding concerns including promotion-related arrears, delays in concluding a new Collective Agreement and the Deprived Area Allowance.

Ghana News.title: Gabriel Tanko Kwamigah-Atokple appointed Patron of NDC UK and Ireland Aldershot Branch
Ghana News.content:
Member of the Council of State, Gabriel Tanko Kwamigah-Atokple, has been appointed Patron of the Aldershot Branch of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) UK and Ireland Chapter.

Kwamigah-Atokple said he had accepted the appointment in good faith and recognised the responsibility and expectations that came with the role.

He said the position offered an opportunity to work with the branch to strengthen its activities, deepen its contribution to the NDC’s diaspora network and support practical development initiatives in Ghana.

The Aldershot Branch, he noted, occupies an important position within the party’s diaspora structure, having been inaugurated by President John Dramani Mahama.

He urged members to look beyond political mobilisation and use their professional experience, business networks and international connections to support investment and job creation in Ghana.

Kwamigah-Atokple said the Ghanaian diaspora possesses expertise and access to potential investors that could be leveraged to attract businesses and create employment opportunities.

He encouraged the NDC UK and Ireland Chapter to make investment promotion a key part of its contribution to Ghana’s development, particularly in relation to President Mahama’s Reset Agenda and the 24-Hour Economy policy.

He called on members to identify credible investment opportunities, facilitate engagements with prospective investors and support businesses seeking to establish or expand operations in Ghana.

According to him, the diaspora’s contribution should extend beyond remittances and political activities to practical interventions that support economic growth and job creation.

The call is consistent with remarks Kwamigah-Atokple made earlier this month urging Ghanaians abroad to deploy their expertise, technology and international networks to support businesses and employment in Ghana.

The new Patron also expressed support for the Aldershot Branch’s decision to use its second anniversary celebration to raise funds for potable water and other social intervention projects in Ghana.

He said access to clean drinking water remained a challenge in some communities and described it as fundamental to human health and dignity.

He called for contributions from citizens, institutions, businesses and organised associations to help address such challenges.

As part of his support for the initiative, Kwamigah-Atokple donated an undisclosed amount in US dollars towards the branch’s fundraising efforts.

He said the contribution was intended to support the provision of potable water and other planned social projects in Ghana.

Kwamigah-Atokple also announced plans to visit the NDC UK and Ireland Chapter in the coming months to meet its executives and members and participate more directly in its activities.

He said the engagements would provide an opportunity to explore ways of strengthening the chapter, attracting investment to Ghana and supporting projects that improve living conditions.

He reaffirmed his support for the NDC and said advancing the cause of the party remained his topmost priority.

He also congratulated the Aldershot Branch on its second anniversary and commended its members for using the occasion to support social intervention projects in Ghana.

He encouraged the branch to sustain such initiatives and continue exploring ways for the NDC’s diaspora structures to contribute to Ghana’s development.
