World.title: Fire guts Customs office in Lagos
World.content:
A fire on Monday gutted the Nigeria Customs Service Western Marine Command office in Apapa, Lagos, destroying property worth millions of naira.

According to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN), the fire started at about 10:23 a.m. after an electrical surge in the conference room and spread to other parts of the building.

Officers at the command tried to put out the fire before officials of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service arrived at about 10:45 a.m. to help contain it.

The incident happened shortly after Timothy Jonah resumed as the Deputy Comptroller of the command.

Mr Jonah, who described the incident as unfortunate, said the command would investigate the cause of the fire.

“I just resumed duty to take over, only to witness this fire outbreak.

“Every challenge, though negative, is an opportunity to strengthen our operations. In the meantime, we will set up a committee to investigate the cause of the fire,” he stated.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He commended the officers who responded to the fire and the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service for their efforts.

Mr Jonah also said the command would strengthen its safety measures to prevent a similar incident.

The fire came about three months after a fire broke out at the Bono Energy Terminal in the Coconut area of Olodi Apapa.

The July 3 incident involved a five-million-litre Automotive Gas Oil storage tank. The Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service said the fire was contained before it spread to nearby petroleum storage facilities.

No casualty was recorded, while the cause of the fire was still under investigation, the agency said.

World.title: NIPC, Kaduna take top spots in transparency, integrity ranking
World.content:
The Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission (NIPC) and the Kaduna State Government have emerged as leaders in the 2026 Transparency and Integrity Index (TII), according to a report released on Monday by the Centre for Fiscal Transparency and Public Integrity (CeFTPI).

NIPC was ranked as the most transparent federal institution, while Kaduna State secured the top position among state governments on the transparency table.

While the NIPC scored 84.14 per cent, leading 518 assessed Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), and government-owned enterprises, while Kaduna scored 54.68 per cent, leading 35 other states.

Umar Yakubu, the executive director of CeFTPI, presented the report at the Federal Ministry of Finance in Abuja.

The TII, developed in 2021 by CeFPTI in collaboration with the Bureau of Public Service Reforms (BPSR), evaluates institutions against established standards of transparency, accountability, and integrity across five core thematic areas: Fiscal Transparency, Open Procurement and Contracting, Human Resources and Inclusion, Control of Corruption, and Citizens’ Engagement.

TII 2026 performance

The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) ranked second with a score of 80.13, improving upon its third-place finish in the 2025 rankings.

The anti-corruption agency is followed by the Development Bank of Nigeria (DBN) 78.43, National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA) 73.22, Tertiary Education Fund (TETFUND) 68.65, Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) 60.87, National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) 60.43, Bank of Industry (BOI) 57.56, Nigeria Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) 49.83, and Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) 49.60.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The report noted that only a few institutions performed well, with many scoring less than 20 per cent. It added that 120 institutions scored 14.50 per cent.

The Ministry of Youth and Sports Development ranked the lowest with 0 per cent.

For states, Osun followed Kaduna with 50.54 per cent. All other states scored below 50 per cent. Niger State came last.

SGF charges institutions, states

The Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, said the institutions assessed should be spurred by the report to improve on their performances.

“For agencies scoring well, the task is to consolidate and sustain those best practices,” Mr Akume said. “For those with gaps, the task is introspection and action. Leaders should ask, why did we score this way and what practical steps can we take to improve?”

He encouraged institutions to integrate the findings into their strategic plans and reforms.

“Discuss them in your management meetings. The report should not sit on the shelf and should inform management decisions, budget priorities, procurement processes, staff training, digital disclosure and how you communicate with the people.”

Mr Akume commended the CeFTPI and BPRS for sustaining this initiative and developing its practical tools. He noted that the annual evaluation sets benchmarks to see what has been done “and where we must do better.”

“Today, we have all been reminded that the push to end corruption globally is an ideal that would be accomplished through promoting transparency, accountability and integrity in governance. The 2026 Index that would help define us is one practical way through which these ideas are being advanced,” he said.

The Director General, BPSR, Dasuki Arabi, stressed the importance of the report, noting “that it answers the questions Nigerians are asking.”

He said, “Nigerians are becoming anxious to know how public resources are distributed and managed, what procedures are employed in the procurement process, and to know if recruitment processes are fair and open.

“The motive behind the index is not punitive, nor is it meant to shame or disgrace anybody or any institution of government, but it’s a fair and proactive method to get institutions of government to publicly declare information that they are supposed to make open.”

Thematic performances

For financial disclosure, the Financial Reporting Council of Nigeria (FRC) scored 100 per cent.

Only 14 institutions scored above the 50 per cent threshold under this themaric area.

They are NIPC, NDIC, Nigerian Content and Development and Monitoring Board, TETFund, Family Homes Fund, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria (ABU), DBN, ICPC, National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency, NHRC, Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority, BOI and Nigeria Maritime University Okerenkoko, Delta.

Twenty-four states performed above 50 percent. The top five are Kwara State, 100 per cent, followed by Kogi and Rivers at 95.55, Bauchi State at 93.33 and Gombe at 91.11.

Procurement, human resources, and inclusion

Under procurement, ICPC and NIPC scored 100 per cent, TETFund 93.33, NHRC 80 per cent, NOSDRA 73.33, DBN 60, and Federal Housing Authority, Petroleum Training Institute, Effurun, Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) collectively scored 53.33.

For states, only Delta (80) and Osun (66.67) scored above 50 per cent.

Under human resource and inclusion, ICPC scored 87.50, then NOSDRA and NERC scored 82.50, and DBN and NIPC scored 75.

Similarly, NNPCL, Police Service Commission (PSC) and TETFund scored 62.50, and the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities, National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) and UBEC scored 50 per cent.

All other institutions scored less than 50 per cent. In this category, all states performed below 30 per cent.

Control of corruption

For control of corruption, BOI, DBN and NOSDRA topped the chart at 100 per cent, followed by ICPC, NESREA, Nigeria Atomic Energy Commission, NDIC, Nigeria Electricity Liability Management Limited, Nigerian Communication Satellite Limited, NIPC, Nigerian Stored Products Research Institute, Ibadan, at 80 per cent.

Also, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), National Horticultural Research Institute, Ibadan; NHRC, National Inland Waterways Authority, National Institute for Cultural Orientation, National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, NSIA, Nigerian Law Reform Commission and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) came third with 60 per cent.

All of the other institutions scored below 50 per cent.

For states, only Kaduna scored 100 per cent; meanwhile, all other states scored 40 per cent and below.

Citizens engagement

More than half the institutions excelled in citizens’ engagement. The report noted that 378 institutions scored above the 50 per cent threshold.

The DBN and NIC emerged as the top institutions with 100 per cent in this category.

Thirty-one states did well in this category, scoring 60 per cent and above. Only Delta, Imo, Niger, and Zamfara scored 40 per cent. Ebonyi scored 0 per cent.

Major gaps

Speaking on the overall performance, Mr Umar said there are gaps and disparities between the states.

“A lot needs to be done in the states. The key takeaways are that compliance is concentrated. It’s not really well spread. Ministries need to do a lot better.

“A lot is being done under citizen engagement and control of corruption, but you need to do more under financials and open procurement.”

Mr Arabi also said, from previous reports, it was obvious that many public institutions “are becoming increasingly proactive in disclosing information contributing to stronger governance systems and improved accountability across the public sector.”

In the 2025 TII report, none of the institutions scored 80 per cent in the overall ranking; however, this year’s performance shows improvement.

World.title: CBN urges Nigerians to handle Naira with care
World.content:
The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has urged Nigerians, particularly traders, to handle the Naira with care, pride and dignity.

This, according to the central bank, will extend its lifespan and reduce the cost of replacing soiled and mutilated notes.

The Director, Currency Operations and Branch Management, Adedeji Adetona, gave the advice in Kano on Monday during a roadshow and public awareness campaign on proper handling of the Naira at Galadima Market.

Represented by Ibrahim Yahya, deputy director, Currency Operations Department, Mr Adetona said the sensitisation was aimed at taking the message of proper handling of the Naira directly to the people, particularly those who frequently engage in cash transactions.

He described the Naira as a symbol of Nigeria’s sovereignty and national pride, while stressing the need for Nigerians to handle the currency carefully and effectively.

“The key message is about proper handling of the Naira. The Naira is the symbol of our sovereignty. It is our national pride, and we need to handle the Naira very carefully and effectively,” he advised.

According to him, the CBN and, by extension, the federal government, spend substantial resources replacing currency notes that become dirty, soiled, spoiled or mutilated.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said proper handling of the currency would help extend its lifespan and save resources that would otherwise be spent on replacing damaged notes.

“We believe that by handling the Naira carefully, we are extending the lifespan of that Naira and, by extension, saving a lot of money in terms of replacement of the Naira,” Mr Adetona said.

He said the CBN had commenced the sensitisation campaign at Galadima Market in Kano, with plans to take the message to other markets across the state.

Mr Adetona urged members of the public to handle the Naira with pride and dignity, saying the campaign was intended to encourage responsible handling of the national currency.

He explained that markets were selected as major points of engagement because they were important centres for exchange and cash transactions.

“We believe the market is the major place for exchange transactions. People bring cash, and we understand the strategic nature of Kano in terms of commerce.

“Kano is a centre of commerce that records substantial cash transactions, making traders important stakeholders in efforts to promote proper handling of the currency,” he said.

Mr Adetona said traders receive and handle cash frequently from customers and, in many cases, accumulate the money before taking the proceeds to banks.

According to him, ensuring that traders properly handle the cash they receive from customers is an important starting point in achieving the objective of protecting the Naira.

“So we believe that when we talk to the traders themselves, that is the starting point.

“They accumulate cash and may be the part that they have used in their transactions and the remaining, they might likely take the remaining to the bank.

“So, we believe that proper handling by them as the first step will go a long way in achieving our objectives,” the director said.

He said the CBN would continue to engage relevant stakeholders and members of the public to create greater awareness on the importance of preserving the Naira.

Earlier, the Chairman of Galadima Market Traders Association, Shu’aibu Suleiman, said the market leadership would collaborate with the CBN to sensitise traders, particularly small-scale sellers, on the proper handling of Naira notes.

He welcomed the CBN’s decision to select the market for the awareness campaign, saying it would help promote responsible handling of the national currency.

He noted that the market has many small traders, including fish sellers, who would be reached through the sensitisation programme.

Mr Suleiman assured the CBN team of the market’s cooperation in taking the campaign to traders and customers.

He said continuous public awareness was necessary to encourage members of the public to handle the Naira properly and preserve its quality.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the CBN team visited Galadima Market, Sabon Gari Market, Abattoir, Yankaba Market, Tarauni Market, ‘Yan Lemo and Dawanau International Grains Market.

World.title: Court orders NMDPRA to continue issuing fuel import licences to Matrix, AA Rano, AYM Shafa
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja has ordered the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) to continue issuing and renewing petroleum products import licences to three major oil marketers, ruling that the regulator’s refusal to do so violates the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA).

Justice Inyang Ekwo delivered the judgement on Monday. The judge reportedly ruled that the authority’s refusal to grant or renew import licences for Matrix Energy, AA Rano and AYM Shafa was in “direct non-compliance” with the PIA, Nairametrics reported.

It said the judge specifically directed the regulator to continue granting, issuing, extending, renewing or reissuing licences, permits and authorisations for midstream and downstream petroleum operations, particularly the importation of petroleum products, once the companies meet all statutory and regulatory requirements.

The judgement followed a suit filed in June by the three oil marketers challenging the NMDPRA’s refusal to regularly issue or renew their petroleum products import licences.

The companies, through their lawyers, Raji Ahmed, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, and Chris Ekemezie, argued that the PIA does not prohibit the importation of petroleum products into Nigeria or prevent the regulator from issuing licences to eligible importers.

The Court rulings

Delivering judgement on Monday, Mr Ekwo held that the NMDPRA’s refusal to issue and renew the licences was inconsistent with the provisions of the PIA and that the authority had acted beyond the limits of the law.

He ruled that any exercise of regulatory powers relating to import licences in violation of the PIA and other relevant laws was “null and void”.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The judge also held that the plaintiffs had successfully established their claims against the regulator.

In a key part of the judgment, the court declared that Sections 31, 32 and other relevant provisions of the PIA, read alongside Section 72 of the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act, mandate the NMDPRA to promote competition in the midstream and downstream petroleum sectors.

The provisions also require the regulator to prevent the abuse of dominant market positions and restrictive business practices.

The court further declared that the three oil marketers were entitled to the issuance, extension or renewal of their import licences upon fulfilling the conditions stipulated by the NMDPRA.

The judge, however, clarified that the authority retains exclusive regulatory powers to grant, modify, extend, renew, suspend, cancel or terminate licences and permits for midstream and downstream petroleum operations.

Why the oil marketers went to court

In an affidavit filed on 26 June in support of the suit, Sabiu Saidu Mahuta, executive director of AA Rano Nigeria Limited, said the NMDPRA had, since July 2025, issued, extended or renewed import licences for the three companies only sporadically rather than regularly.

He argued that the regulator’s actions and inactions were entrenching market dominance and monopolisation of the downstream petroleum sector by local refineries.

Mr Mahuta also said the three companies had collectively invested more than $20 billion in infrastructure, logistics and retail networks to support their petroleum businesses.

“Collectively, the plaintiffs have invested more than $20,000,000,000 [Twenty Billion United States of America Dollars] in infrastructure, logistics and retail networks for the smooth operations of their licensed petroleum products businesses,” he stated.

The companies argued that allowing petroleum imports alongside local refining would promote competition, prevent monopolistic practices and price-fixing, and improve the overall performance of Nigeria’s midstream and downstream petroleum sectors.

Their lawyer, Mr Raji, urged the court to affirm the legality of petroleum products imports and the regulator’s obligation to issue licences to eligible operators.

Dangote Refinery’s legal suits

The judgement comes amid an ongoing legal dispute over the issuance of petrol import licences in Nigeria, particularly following the expansion of domestic refining capacity by the Dangote Refinery.

Dangote Refinery has argued in a separate suit that the continued issuance of petroleum products import licences contravenes Nigerian law, which it maintains permits imports only when local refineries cannot meet domestic demand.

The refinery recently filed a fresh N100 billion suit against the Attorney-General of the Federation at the Federal High Court in Lagos over the continued issuance of import licences.

Matrix Energy, AA Rano and AYM Shafa have also applied to join that suit.

The case remains pending before the court.

The latest ruling in Abuja, however, addresses the three oil marketers’ rights to obtain import licences from the NMDPRA, provided they meet the applicable statutory and regulatory conditions.

Nigeria’s changing petrol supply dynamics

The legal dispute comes as Nigeria’s petroleum supply landscape continues to change following increased output from domestic refineries.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that NMDPRA data published last week showed that petrol imports declined sharply in the first quarter of 2026, while supplies from local refineries rose to about 3.18 billion litres.

The statistical presentation of the report showed that crude oil receipts by domestic refineries increased to 683,000 barrels per day (bpd) in August from 585,000 bpd in July, representing a 17 per cent increase.

The increase became profound as domestic petrol receipts rose significantly while reliance on imported petrol declined.

According to the data, average daily Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) receipts increased by 11 per cent, from 45.5 million litres per day in July to 50.5 million litres per day in August.

The report indicated that domestic PMS receipts accounted for most of the increase, rising by 39 per cent, from 25.8 million litres per day to 35.9 million litres per day.

In contrast, PMS imports fell by 26 per cent, from 19.7 million litres per day in July to 14.6 million litres per day in August.

The growth in domestic refining has intensified discussions about the role of fuel imports, market competition, and the regulatory conditions governing the supply of petroleum products.

Meanwhile, PREMIUM TIMES reported last week that NMDPRS approved petrol import permits covering about 830,000 metric tonnes for multiple companies ahead of the fourth quarter of 2026.

George Ene-Ita, spokesperson for the authority, confirmed the development to PREMIUM TIMES last Tuesday.

“Yes, petrol import permits were approved for Q4 2026 to ensure no supply gaps are heading into the critical end-of-year period,” Mr Ene-Ita said.

Companies reportedly granted the permits include Matrix Energy, A.A. Rano, AYM Shafa, NIPCO, Pinnacle Oil and Bono Energy.

The approvals were reportedly issued on 18 September, although details of the individual allocations to the marketers are still sketchy. A request for details from PREMIUM TIMES, sent via email to the authority last week, was acknowledged, but has yet to be received.

World.title: Federal government approves upgrade of four South-South ports
World.content:
The federal government has approved the comprehensive modernisation and upgrade of Onne, Rivers, Delta, and Calabar ports as part of efforts to expand Nigeria’s maritime capacity and reduce the concentration of cargo traffic around Lagos.

The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, announced the approval in a tweet on his official X account on Sunday.

Mr Oyetola said the approval followed an earlier decision by the federal government to modernise and upgrade the Apapa and Tin Can Island ports in Lagos.

According to him, extending the programme to the South-south region would create additional gateways for international trade and contribute to a more balanced and efficient national port system.

Targets faster cargo movement

Mr Oyetola said the upgrade of the four ports would improve cargo handling, reduce vessel turnaround times and strengthen regional connectivity.

The minister said the ports had strategic roles in Nigeria’s trade, industrial, and regional development and needed to be equipped to meet the demands of a growing economy.

He said the expansion beyond Lagos would complement ongoing investments in Apapa and Tin Can Island ports while helping to reduce the concentration of cargo traffic around Lagos.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“This is part of a broader expansion of Nigeria’s maritime infrastructure, including federal government approvals for the development of the Ibom, Bakassi, Agge, Gateway, Ondo, and Bonny deep seaports,” Mr Oyetola said.

He said the government was pursuing a dual approach: upgrading existing ports and facilitating the development of new deep-seaports.

“Our approach is comprehensive. We are modernising existing ports while facilitating the development of new deep-seaports. Together, these investments will expand Nigeria’s maritime capacity, create stronger economic corridors and position our country as a major maritime and logistics hub in Africa,” he said.

Delta ports have faced years of underuse

The approval comes against a background of repeated calls for the revival of ports in the Niger Delta.

In August, Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori urged the federal government to revive the Warri, Koko, Sapele, and Burutu ports.

Mr Oborevwori said Delta was “strategically blessed with four seaports” and argued that their revival would create employment, stimulate trade and strengthen the economies of Delta and Nigeria.

Calabar Port faces longstanding dredging challenge

Calabar Port has similarly faced years of calls for rehabilitation and dredging.

In 2023, The Punch newspaper previously reported that Governor Bassey Otu of Cross River State appealed to the federal government to dredge the Calabar channel, with maritime operators saying improved access would allow the port to handle more cargo and serve importers in the South-East and other parts of the country.

The dredging project, according to the newspaper, had been stalled by a dispute involving the Nigerian Ports Authority and the contractor. However, the government had initiated an out-of-court settlement.

The National Assembly has also raised concerns about the unfinished dredging of the port. In 2024, the House of Representatives urged the Federal Government to re-award the dredging contract to a reputable company and mandated its Committee on Ports and Harbours to investigate earlier contracts awarded for the project, The Nation reported.

The latest approval, therefore, comes after years of demands for improved infrastructure and navigational access at the Calabar facility.

FG links ports upgrade to economic diversification

Mr Oyetola said modern ports were central to President Bola Tinubu’s infrastructure renewal and economic diversification agenda.

“Our vision is an integrated maritime and logistics system in which ports, roads, rail, inland waterways and other transport infrastructure work together to enable the seamless movement of cargo,” he said.

Mr Oyetola said the government wanted Nigerian businesses to spend less time and resources moving their goods, while creating an environment that attracts investment and supports employment.

He added that the ministry would work with state governments, terminal operators, investors, shipping companies, es and other stakeholders to ensure that the project delivers tangible improvements.

“Nigeria has the geography, market, and maritime resources to become a leading maritime hub. Our responsibility is to provide the infrastructure, policies, and enabling environment required to turn that potential into sustainable economic value,” the minister said.

World.title: Resident doctors give FG 14-day ultimatum to meet demands or face industrial action
World.content:
Resident doctors have given the federal government a 14-day ultimatum to begin implementing outstanding agreements on their welfare and working conditions or face “further industrial action.”

The ultimatum takes effect from 1 October 2026, according to a communique issued at the end of the Nigerian Association of Resident Doctors’ (NARD) 46th Annual General Meeting (AGM) in Calabar, Cross River State.

According to the document signed by the association’s new President, Ogar Idoko, Secretary-General, Besongngem Akotanchi, and Publicity and Social Secretary, Ashimom Msughter, the meeting was held from 21 to 26 September.

The doctors said the ultimatum became necessary due to ongoing delays in resolving several welfare and professional issues, despite the government’s previous engagements and commitments.

Outstanding allowances, salaries

The resident doctors demanded the immediate payment of 19 months of outstanding Professional Allowance Table (PAT) arrears.

They also demanded payment of outstanding arrears arising from the 25/35 per cent upward review of the Consolidated Medical Salary Structure (CONMESS) for doctors and other affected health workers.

The association said several medical doctors were still owed salary and promotion arrears in various federal health institutions.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It also demanded the immediate correction of omissions and errors in the payment of the 2026 Medical Residency Training Fund (MRTF). It called for an upward review of the fund to reflect the current cost of residency training.

The doctors said the reviewed MRTF should also be captured in the 2027 Appropriation Act.

Other demands

The resident doctors called for the accelerated conclusion of the long-running Collective Bargaining Agreement between the Nigerian Medical Association and the federal government.

They said the unresolved review of the CONMESS salary structure had remained outstanding for about 17 years and was contributing to the brain drain affecting the health sector.

The association also called for a sustainable recruitment system to address “the critical manpower shortages occasioned by brain drain and guarantee safe and effective healthcare delivery.”

It demanded the implementation of the approved work-hour regulation policy, including functional biometric systems to document working hours and a standardised system for compensating doctors for excess workload.

The doctors also called for the implementation of “the Assault on Health Workers Prevention Policy across all health institutions with clear accountability mechanisms” and the payment of outstanding pension contributions.

The association further demanded urgent improvements in healthcare infrastructure, equipment and essential medical facilities across the country.

It said poor infrastructure and inadequate equipment were affecting patient safety, healthcare delivery and the training of resident doctors.

Threat of industrial action

Under the resolution, the AGM mandates that the NARD National Executive Council (NEC) “closely monitor” the government’s response over the next two weeks.

The association said it would take “all necessary lawful and constitutionally sanctioned actions”, including further industrial action, if the authorities failed to demonstrate meaningful compliance within the stipulated period.

The latest ultimatum follows several rounds of disputes between resident doctors and the federal government this year.

In January, the doctors suspended a planned nationwide strike scheduled to begin on 12 January after the National Industrial Court restrained the association from embarking on the action, and the government made fresh commitments.

In April, resident doctors commenced a nationwide strike over the reversal of the Professional Allowance Table and other outstanding financial obligations. The action was suspended less than 24 hours later following government interventions.

In June, the association issued another 21-day ultimatum over unpaid allowances, salary arrears and delays in the residency training fund.

The resident doctors’ latest ultimatum, therefore, gives the federal government until 1 October to “commence demonstrable implementation of the resolutions contained in this communique.”

World.title: APC wins all local council chairmanship, councillorship seats in Enugu
World.content:
The ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) has won all the 17 local government chairmanship seats in the Saturday’s council election in Enugu State.

The Chairman of the Enugu State Independent Electoral Commission (ENSIEC), Christian Ngwu, announced the results of the exercise at the commission’s headquarters in Enugu on Sunday.

Mr Ngwu, a professor, also announced that the APC candidates equally won all the 260 councillorship seats in the state.

The new chairpersons-elect

According to the results announced by Mr Ngwu, Ugochukwu Nwanjoku won in Aninri LGA while Uchenna Okolo emerged winner for Awgu LGA and Beloved-Dan Anike clinched victory for Enugu East LGA.

In Enugu North LGA, Ibenaku Onoh was declared winner, Caleb Ani emerged victorious in Enugu South LGA while Vitalis Ngwu cruised to victory in Ezeagu LGA.

Others were Martin Amadieze (Igbo Etiti LGA); Chris Simon (Igbo Eze North LGA); Ferdinand Ukwueze (Igbo Eze South LGA); Brendan Ani (Isi-Uzo), and Mike Ogbuekwe (Nkanu East LGA).

John Ogbodo emerged winner in Nkanu West LGA, Jude Asogwa won in Nsukka LGA while Greg Anyaegbudike picked victory in Oji River LGA and Innocent Ezeoha was declared winner in Udenu LGA.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The streak of victory continued in Udi LGA where Hyginus Agu emerged winner while Chijioke Ezeukwu won in Uzo-Uwani LGA.

12 re-elected, 5 elected for the first time

A PREMIUM TIMES review of the 17 chairpersons-elect shows that 12 of them were re-elected for a second term in office while five others were elected for the first time.

Those re-elected for a second term in office were: Mr Anike (Enugu East LGA), Mr Ukwueze (Igbo Eze South LGA), Mr Nwanjoku (Aninri LGA), Mr Okolo (Awgu LGA), Mr Onoh (Enugu North LGA), Mr Ani (Enugu South LGA) and Mr Ngwu (Ezeagu LGA).

Others included: Mr Ogbodo (Nkanu West LGA), Mr Asogwa (Nsukka LGA), Mr Anyaegbudike (Oji River LGA), Mr Agu (Udi LGA), and Mr Ezeukwu (Uzo-Uwani LGA).

Those elected for the first time were : Mr Amadieze (Igbo-Etiti LGA), Mr Simon (Igbo-Eze North LGA), Mr Ani (Isi-Uzo LGA), Mr Ogbuekwe (Nkanu East LGA), and Mr Ezeoha (Udenu LGA).

Praise of voters, others

Mr Ngwu, while declaring the results, praised the Enugu State people for their participation in the elections.

The ENSIEC chairman stressed that the citizens’ involvement gave meaning to the electoral process.

He also lauded the security agencies, civil society organisations and the media for their contributions to the successful conduct of the exercise. He congratulated the chairpersons-elect and urged them to regard their victories as a call to service and an opportunity to serve the people of their respective local government areas.

He subsequently issued certificates of return to the 17 newly elected council chairpersons.

World.title: FG inaugurates farmers’ coalition as agriculture grows
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

Sector records 4.39% growth in Q2

By Gabriel Ewepu

ABUJA — The Federal Government has inaugurated the Coalition of Farmers Associations for Food Security in Nigeria, COA-FARMERS, as the agriculture sector recorded 4.39 per cent growth in the second quarter of 2026.

The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, who inaugurated the coalition on behalf of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Abuja on Monday, described the sector’s performance as its strongest since 2021.

Kyari attributed the growth largely to farmers’ response to the administration’s declaration of a state of emergency on food security.

He said the coalition should serve as more than an umbrella body for farmers’ groups by helping government identify challenges facing producers, improve the flow of information from farmers and assess the impact of agricultural programmes.

“A country cannot secure its food future if the people who produce its food are heard only after decisions have been made,” the minister said.

Kyari said the renaming of the ministry as the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security reflected the administration’s focus on translating agricultural policies into increased food production and availability.

He also highlighted the importance of women farmers, calling for greater opportunities for them to participate in decision-making, production, processing, aggregation and marketing.

“Food security will not be secured by speaking for women farmers. It will be strengthened by ensuring that women farmers have the space, the tools and the opportunity to organise, invest, produce and grow,” he said.

The minister urged COA-FARMERS to provide honest feedback on government programmes and identify areas requiring improvement.

He said the government expected the ministry to deliver better access to inputs, increased production and productivity, improved markets and more secure livelihoods.

Kyari also said Nigeria’s election in February to chair the Governing Council of the International Fund for Agricultural Development, IFAD, underscored the importance of giving farmers a stronger voice in agricultural policy.

He said, “When Nigeria speaks in that forum, it must speak with the authority of its own farmers, and this coalition will help give that voice its substance.”

The minister disclosed that President Tinubu had appointed him Director of the Presidential Campaign Council for Agro-Allied Commodities Mobilisation, while the Minister of State for Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Aliyu Sabi Abdullahi, would serve as Deputy Director.

Abdullahi, in his remarks, acknowledged the coalition’s support for Tinubu’s re-election bid and urged members to highlight what they described as the administration’s achievements in agriculture and other sectors.

“They should work towards that goal collectively by going back to the people, showcasing the achievement of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in agriculture and the other sectors of the economy,” he said.

National President of COA-FARMERS, Chief Emmanuel Anoh, commended farmers across grains, roots and tubers, livestock, fisheries, horticulture, cash crops and agro-allied services for their contributions to the economy.

Anoh said the coalition comprised 99 farmer associations and commodity organisations representing producers, aggregators, processors and marketers across the agricultural value chain.

He commended government interventions, including fertiliser distribution, tractor mechanisation, the National Agricultural Growth Scheme–Agro-Pocket and Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones.

However, he called for a direct-to-farm model for distributing agricultural interventions and quarterly stakeholder meetings with the ministry.

Anoh also requested the minister’s support for a formal presentation of the coalition to President Tinubu.

The event concluded with the formal inauguration of COA-FARMERS as an umbrella platform bringing together commodity associations, farmers, agribusiness organisations, registered farmers’ associations and cooperative societies across Nigeria.

World.title: ASUU urges Soludo to implement 2025 agreement
World.content:
Soludo

By Vincent Ujumadu

The Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU, Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu University, COOU, chapter, has appealed to Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo to prevail on the university management and governing council to implement the 2025 ASUU-Federal Government agreement.

The union expressed concern over what it described as continued delay in implementing the agreement, warning that it may begin processes towards industrial action if its September 2026 salary is paid without the provisions of the agreement.

Chairman of the university’s ASUU branch, Comrade Bruno Ibekilo, and Secretary, Comrade Bernard Alajekwu, said the union had made several efforts to engage the university administration on the matter without success.

They said representatives of ASUU national and its Owerri Zone visited the university administration in July 2026 to advocate for implementation of the agreement.

According to the union, several meetings were subsequently held between its leadership, the university administration and the governing council, during which the financial and non-financial implications of the agreement were presented and discussed.

The union said relevant documents required to support implementation were also produced during the engagements.

In a statement, ASUU-COOU said its congress on August 26, 2026, resolved to continue consultations with relevant stakeholders, describing engagement as the preferred approach.

It, however, said the continued wait had not produced the desired outcome.

The statement read in part: “Accordingly, ASUU-COOU hereby draws the attention of the Anambra State Government, the Visitor to the University, the Governing Council, University Management, other stakeholders and the general public, to the continued non-implementation of this agreement.”

The union said its members had remained on the same salary structure, with no structured salary increment since the post-2009 agreement, despite continuing to discharge their academic responsibilities.

It said the delay had affected the welfare of its members and urged the state government and university authorities to act.

“We therefore appeal to the Anambra State Government, the Governing Council and University administration to honour and implement the agreement to improve the welfare and conditions of service of our members who now borrow to journey to Igbariam and Uli campuses to render their services,” the union said.

ASUU-COOU also expressed concern over what it described as the migration of qualified academics from the university, saying implementation of the agreement would help improve staff morale, retain academics and sustain the quality of education.

The union said improved staff welfare was necessary to maintain the university’s academic standards and fulfil the objectives for which the institution was established.

World.title: Liverpool’s Gakpo withdraws from Netherlands squad due to injury
World.content:
Gakpo

By Adegboyega Adeleye

Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo has withdrawn from the Netherlands squad due to injury and will return to his club for further assessment.

The Dutch football federation, KNVB, confirmed that Gakpo is not fit enough to remain with the squad for the rest of the international window.

The Netherlands have also decided not to call up a replacement for the Liverpool forward.

Gakpo was forced off early during the Netherlands’ 2-1 Nations League victory over Serbia in Belgrade after appearing to twist his ankle following a challenge from Serbia midfielder Sasa Lukic.

The Liverpool star tried to continue after the incident but was eventually replaced by Ruben van Bommel shortly afterwards.

The injury has now ruled Gakpo out of the Netherlands’ remaining fixtures during the international break, with the forward set to return to Liverpool for further medical assessment.

The development is another injury concern for Liverpool, with striker Alexander Isak also withdrawing from the Sweden squad earlier in the international window due to a minor injury.

Isak played the full match as Sweden defeated Romania 2-1 on Friday but will miss the country’s next three Nations League matches and is expected to be assessed by Liverpool’s medical staff.

Liverpool are scheduled to return to action against Manchester City on October 1.

World.title: 2027: Show us budget for new Army divisions, Makinde challenges Tinubu
World.content:
Gov Seyi Makinde

By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA — Presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, Seyi Makinde, has challenged President Bola Tinubu’s administration to produce the 2026 budget provision for the expansion of Army divisions, questioning the planning behind the move amid persistent insecurity in the North-Central.

Makinde said tackling insecurity required more than announcements, arguing that any decision to expand military formations must be backed by proper planning and funding.

Speaking Monday at the APM North-Central Town Hall Meeting in Lafia, Nasarawa State, Makinde also criticised the Federal Government’s economic policies, saying increased allocations to states had not translated into relief from hunger and claiming that Oyo State’s dependence on federal allocation had risen again under the Tinubu administration.

“I was looking at the budget for 2026. I was looking for the item in that budget relating to the expansion of those army divisions. I did not see it.

“If they have it in the budget that they prepared for 2026, let them bring it out. So, you cannot just wake up and say, well, without any plan, I am setting up or expanding army divisions to tackle insecurity. There has to be a lot of planning that will go into this,” he said.

The APM candidate contrasted the federal approach with his administration’s budget preparation in Oyo State, where he said consultations with residents across the state’s geopolitical zones had already begun ahead of the 2027 budget.

He said the exercise enabled the government to hear directly from residents and determine their priorities before finalising the spending plan.

On the economy, Makinde acknowledged that states were receiving more money from the Federation Account but questioned whether the additional revenue had eased the hardship facing Nigerians.

“Yes, we have more money, but has it translated to fighting hunger in our society? The answer is no,” he said.

Makinde said Oyo State depended on federal allocation for more than 80 per cent of its revenue when he assumed office in 2019, but that his administration reduced the figure to 65 per cent by 2022.

He claimed the figure had since climbed back to almost 80 per cent, blaming what he called the Federal Government’s “voodoo economy”.

“By 2023, when they came on board with their voodoo economy, the resultant effect is that today Oyo State is back to almost 80 per cent dependence on federal allocation. That is their voodoo economy,” Makinde said.

On his presidential bid, Makinde said his proposed ‘Reset Nigeria’ agenda could be implemented within four years, covering security, education, the economy and the country’s socio-political environment.

“The reset agenda can be completed in four years. After all, we had someone who was head of state in this country for 10 months, and he was able to end military rule and usher in the democracy that we now enjoy in Nigeria,” he said.

He also promised that an APM administration would run a transitional government of national unity from May 29, 2027, which he said would culminate in “new players and a new agenda for Nigeria’s sustainable development.”

The APM vice-presidential candidate, Lawal Daura, said the party’s proposed reset was driven by what he described as Nigerians’ desire for tangible improvement in their lives.

“We don’t need to say that, for quite some time, people have been given the opportunity to rule this nation without really having an idea of how to fix it. I need to borrow a common phrase: it is always motion without movement. Ours is going to be motion with movement for the betterment of Nigerians and Nigeria,” Daura said.

He said the party’s approach would be built around sincerity, honesty, commitment and results, citing poverty and insecurity among the problems that had continued to affect Nigerians.

APM National Chairman, Yusuf Dantalle, described the North-Central as critical to Nigeria’s unity and development, while citing poor roads and insecurity as evidence of the region’s challenges.

Dantalle also criticised the rising cost of petrol and electricity supply, urging Nigerians to hold the Federal Government to its earlier promise on electricity.

“Oyo State is your laboratory to evaluate the capability of our presidential candidates,” he said, asking voters to assess Makinde’s record in the state.

He urged Nigerians to support the APM’s candidates, saying the party’s agenda would include a new security architecture, a different approach to education and an economy driven by data, science and logic.

World.title: Real Madrid’s Perez summoned over Barcelona referee payments comments
World.content:
Real Madrid President Florentino Perez talks to media at Real Madrid Sports City in Valdebebas, in the outskirts of Madrid, on May 12, 2026. (Photo by JAVIER SORIANO / AFP)

Real Madrid president Florentino Perez and FC Barcelona have been summoned to appear before a Madrid court on November 25 for a conciliation hearing ahead of possible criminal proceedings for defamation against Perez, sources close to the case said on Monday.

The hearing follows legal action launched by Barcelona on June 12 over comments made by Perez in May accusing the Catalan club of manoeuvring to obtain favourable treatment from referees.

Barcelona said its action was intended to force Perez to retract statements it described as knowingly false, defamatory and damaging to the club’s image and reputation.

It warned that if the conciliation process failed, it would file a criminal complaint.

The dispute centres on comments Perez made at a May 12 press conference concerning the so-called Negreira case.

Spanish courts are investigating payments said to be up to 7 million euros made over almost two decades by Barcelona to companies linked to Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira, a former vice-president of Spain’s refereeing committee, to determine whether they were intended to obtain a competitive advantage.

Barcelona denies wrongdoing and says the payments were for reports on referees and a court dismissed bribery charges against Barcelona in 2024.

Perez described the affair as “the most serious case of corruption in football”, adding: “We could never have imagined Barcelona giving money to the head of the referees.”

He also claimed Real Madrid had been denied league titles, saying: “I’ve won seven leagues. I could have won twice as many. The others were stolen from me.”

AFP

World.title: Telecom subscriptions hit 195.1m in July
World.content:
…Adds 2.88m subscriptions in one month

By Juliet Umeh

Nigeria’s active telecommunications subscriptions rose by 2.88 million in July 2026 to 195.11 million, up from 192.23 million recorded in June, according to the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC.

The increase represents a monthly growth of about 1.5 per cent, while the country’s teledensity rose from 88.67 per cent in June to 90 per cent in July.

MTN remained the largest mobile network operator with 100.86 million subscriptions, followed by Airtel with 66.76 million.

Globacom recorded 23.63 million subscriptions, while T2 had 3.61 million.

Despite the continued expansion of newer network technologies, 2G accounted for 36.54 per cent of mobile subscriptions in July.

4G had the largest share at 54.31 per cent, while 3G accounted for 4.42 per cent and 5G, 4.74 per cent.

Broadband subscriptions also increased from 123.11 million in June to 124.42 million in July, pushing broadband penetration from 56.79 per cent to 57.40 per cent.

The growth in connectivity was accompanied by higher internet data consumption, with Nigerians using 1.66 million terabytes of data in July, compared with 1.53 million terabytes in June, representing an increase of about 8.5 per cent.

Data consumption stood at 1.50 million terabytes in May.

The NCC also recorded 157.27 million mobile internet subscriptions, 204,082 fixed internet subscriptions and 230,613 Voice over Internet Protocol subscriptions in July.

A total of 1,251 mobile numbers were ported during the month.

Meanwhile, fibre-to-the-X subscriptions rose from 241,750 in the first quarter of 2026 to 319,735 in the second quarter, representing an increase of 77,985.

The fibre-to-the-X category covers fibre connections to homes, offices and other locations.

The telecommunications sector contributed 9.72 per cent to Nigeria’s gross domestic product in the second quarter of 2026.

World.title: DSS arraigns 4 IPOB members allegedly linked to operative’s killing
World.content:
The Department of State Services (DSS) on Monday arraigned four suspected members of the outlawed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) over their alleged involvement in the kidnapping and killing of its officer, Ekpeyong Asuquo Owoh.

The defendants were arraigned before Justice Joyce Abdulmalik of a Federal High Court in Abuja on a six-count charge bordering on terrorism and kidnapping.

The defendants are Michael Okafor, a.k.a Onyechimeleze; Chinedu Chukwudozie, alias Kante; Chibunna Olisa; and Chigozie Olisa, a.k.a Ability.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the prosecution alleged that the defendants conspired to commit acts of terrorism and were involved in the abduction of Owoh, an officer of the DSS, while he was travelling from Port Harcourt in Rivers to Awka in Anambra.

They were further accused of taking the operative hostage and causing his death in the course of the alleged criminal operation.

The suspects were also accused of belonging to the proscribed IPOB and its armed wing, the Eastern Security Network (ESN), as well as involvement in activities allegedly linked to terrorism.

In addition, the prosecution alleged that the suspects were involved in the unlawful possession of firearms, including AK-47 and pump-action rifles, in connection with the alleged offences.

The charges followed investigations into the circumstances surrounding the abduction and killing of the officer and the alleged activities of the defendants.

However, when the charges were read to them, they pleaded not guilty.

Munirat Oladunjoye, who appeared for the DSS, sought a trial trial.

Kelvin Ekwe, who appeared for the defendants, did not opposed the application.

Oladunjoye, however, informed the court that the prosecution had three witnesses that would give evidence during trial.

Justice Abdulmalik consequently adjourned the matter until Oct. 6 for commencement of trial.

The judge ordered that the four accused persons be remanded at the DSS custody.

(NAN)

World.title: Osogbo residents lost millions of Naira in food Ponzi scheme
World.content:
By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo

There was panic in Osogbo, Osun State, on Monday after a food outlet allegedly operating an investment scheme shut its premises, leaving hundreds of customers worried about funds they had paid for food supplies.

The outlet, Global Food Initiative, reportedly began operations in early August around the Odi-Olowo area of the state capital, offering food items to participants at prices said to be significantly below prevailing market rates.

Participants were required to pay in advance for food items they would collect later, with some customers reportedly investing amounts ranging from N50,000 to as much as N50 million.

The items reportedly included 50kg bags of rice and various sizes of vegetable oil, among other food products.

However, concerns heightened after an anchor of a radio programme in the state described the scheme as fraudulent during a live broadcast and warned residents against participating.

The development reportedly triggered panic among participants, who besieged the outlet on Monday, only to find the premises locked.

More than 200 people reportedly gathered at the location, with several participants expressing concern over funds they had paid into the scheme.

One trader was said to have invested N50 million in rice, while another participant, identified as Kafayat, reportedly claimed to have paid N1 million.

Other customers displayed receipts for payments ranging from N50,000 to N250,000 and above as they demanded clarification on the status of their investments.

Tension reportedly rose as some of the aggrieved participants threatened to damage the building housing the outlet’s warehouse, prompting the intervention of police operatives.

As of the time of filing this report, some of the participants who arrived at the premises as early as 7:30am were still waiting, hoping that the operators would return and address their concerns.

Confirming the development, the Osun State Police Command said it deployed personnel to the area after receiving information about a possible breakdown of law and order.

A police spokesperson said the command became aware of the alleged scheme only after officers arrived at the scene to prevent a possible riot.

“We were not aware of the scheme until we got to the area to curb breakdown of law and order that we heard of the scheme.

“As of the time of speaking with you, we are still waiting for someone to report the incident and provide details to the police. However, we are monitoring the situation to avoid crisis,” the police said.

World.title: Katsina Rewards Best Performing Primary School Teacher with Vehicle
World.content:
Francis Sardauna in Katsina

The Katsina State Government has rewarded the state’s best-performing primary school teacher for 2026 with a brand-new Peugeot 206.

The awardee, Hadiza Nazifi of Bayajidda Memorial Primary School, Daura, received the vehicle from the Executive Chairman of the State Universal Basic Education Board (SUBEB), Dr Kabir Magaji, at the board’s headquarters.

Presenting the vehicle to the awardee, Magaji said she was recognised as the “Best Primary School Teacher” in the state for her dedication to duty, diligence, resilience, punctuality and outstanding commitment to teaching and learning.

He explained that her selection was endorsed by the award committee as well as internal and external evaluators who assessed her performance.

He added that the initiative was part of Governor Dikko Umaru Radda-led government to recognise and reward outstanding civil servants, while promoting excellence and professionalism in the state’s public service.

Magaji congratulated the primary school teacher for her achievement and urged her to sustain the standard that earned her the state-wide recognition.

He also called on teachers across the state to rededicate themselves to their duties and contribute to improving the quality of basic education in the state.

Describing teachers as indispensable partners in the development of the education sector and the overall progress of Katsina State, the SUBEB boss warned them against absenteeism

World.title: Minister: Security Is Fundamental Foundation of National Unity, Shared Prosperity
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (rtd), has said that security is not merely an operational task but the fundamental foundation upon which national unity and shared prosperity are built.

This came as the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, said that democracy is sustained by peace and unity.

The minister said the Armed Forces of Nigeria remain resolutely committed to safeguarding the nation’s sovereignty and restoring lasting peace across all regions.

Musa stated this when he joined the Christian faithful, top government officials and members of the diplomatic corps for an inter-denominational church service at the National Christian Centre in Abuja, Sunday to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary.

According to a statement by the Special Assistant on Media to the Minister of Defence, Leah Katung-Babatunde, the service, themed ‘Anchored on Hope: The Path to Divine Stability and Shared Prosperity,’ formed a major part of the official activities lined up for the national celebration.

Musa delivered the first Scripture reading, focusing his message on faith, national peace and collective security.

Highlighting the imperative of national cohesion and the sacrifices of the nation’s security forces, the minister stated: “As we mark 66 years of our nationhood, our hope for a peaceful, secure and prosperous Nigeria remains unshakeable.

“I urge all Nigerians to remain steadfast, support our men and women in uniform, and unite in faith as we build a nation anchored on divine stability.”

In his remarks, Senate President Godswill Akpabio offered prayers for the nation, emphasising the need for harmony and concerted national effort towards achieving sustainable peace.

Delivering the vote of thanks, Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, reiterated the importance of democratic stability as the country prepares for future civic milestones.

“As we look towards the 2027 elections, let us remember that democracy is sustained by peace and unity,” Akume remarked, encouraging citizens to maintain unwavering support for the democratic process.

The service drew key state leaders, including the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General Olufemi Oluyede; the service chiefs; members of the diplomatic community and respected clergy.

The inter-denominational service concluded with the ceremonial cutting of the 66th Independence Anniversary cake by the Minister of Defence and other dignitaries.

World.title: UBEC Launches Digital Platform for Education Funds, Begins New 10-Year Roadmap
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) has digitised the management of its intervention funds and started work on a new 10-year strategic roadmap for basic education in Nigeria.

The Executive Secretary of UBEC, Dr. Aisha Garba, announced the reforms on Monday in Abuja at a consultative meeting on the Basic Education Action Plan Management System (BEAPMS) and the 10-year UBE Roadmap 2026–2035.

Garba said the new digital workflow will replace the manual process of accessing UBEC funds. States will now develop, submit, review and get approval for their action plans through an integrated online platform.

She said the innovation builds on the unified framework and revised guidelines introduced in 2025, which all 36 states and the FCT adopted.

According to her, technical support from the commission helped many states access their matching grants.

“Building on this process, the commission has now upgraded the process into an integrated digital workflow that improves efficiency, transparency, timeliness, traceability and consistency across the fund access cycle,” Garba said.

She explained that UBEC’s BRT and Solina technical teams, working with relevant departments, have converted the existing manual templates into a modular digital platform to enable better decision-making, faster feedback, improved documentation and stronger accountability.

On the roadmap, Garba said UBEC is replacing the current 2021–2030 plan with a new framework for 2026–2035 to align with ongoing reforms in the education sector and emerging national and global priorities.

The new roadmap, she said, would focus on policy prioritisation, resource alignment, institutional coordination, monitoring and results-based accountability.

It is also designed to drive the shift from “education for all” to “learning for all” and will guide states in developing realistic, evidence-based medium-term plans that respond to local needs.

She urged chairmen and Directors of Planning, Research and Statistics of State Universal Basic Education Boards (SUBEBs) to take ownership of the reforms by ensuring timely data submission, disciplined planning and sustained collaboration with UBEC.

She added that the meeting was expected to agree on system requirements, implementation timelines, reporting obligations, capacity-building needs and coordination mechanisms to make both the digital system and the roadmap effective tools for improving learning outcomes.

In his remarks, the Dean of SUBEBs, Shehu Adaramaja, called for stronger coordination between UBEC and SUBEBs to ensure proper planning, implementation and monitoring of interventions.

Also speaking, the Director of Physical Planning, Nura Ibrahim, said effective physical planning is critical to ensuring that infrastructure investments meet the real needs of schools and communities, and called for closer collaboration among stakeholders to improve accountability and learning environments.

World.title: Atiku to Tinubu: Account for Existing Debt Before Seeking Another $1.5bn Loan
World.content:
Former Vice President and ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has accused President Bola Tinubu of running a government that demands endless sacrifice from Nigerians while reaching endlessly for fresh loans.

Atiku said with public debt at ₦166.79 trillion, Tinubu was now seeking another $1.5 billion from the World Bank and must first account for the money already borrowed.

He made the remarks in a statement issued by the Director of Strategic Communications of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, on Monday.

Atiku said Tinubu’s record was an indictment of his economic stewardship, noting that families were struggling to afford food, fuel and electricity, while the debt continued to climb.

“Nigerians were promised that painful policies would free resources for development. They have felt the pain. Where is the development?” he asked.

According to Atiku, if Nigeria’s public debt were divided among everyone, each person’s share would be ₦716,822 today, compared with ₦383,442 three years ago.

“That is an 87 per cent increase,” he said.

Atiku added: “Tinubu has made today difficult and tomorrow more uncertain. He cannot keep loading debt onto the country and expect Nigerians to applaud programme titles.

“What has this government built? Who has benefited? Why should Nigerians trust him with another term in office?”

He said the proposed $500 million facilities for climate resilience, social protection and early childhood development addressed real needs.

However, he said worthy programme names could not stand in for a public account of how previous loans were spent or a clear plan for delivering measurable results.

“Before these loans are concluded, the government must publish the projects to be funded, the communities and citizens expected to benefit, the targets for each programme, the terms of borrowing and disbursement, and a timetable Nigerians can use to track delivery,” he said.

Atiku said climate resilience must mean identifiable land restored, irrigation delivered and communities protected from flooding.

“Social protection must identify who receives support and when. Early childhood development must produce measurable gains in nutrition, healthcare and learning,” he added.

Atiku also challenged the government to reconcile its appetite for borrowing with its repeated claims of higher revenue and savings from petrol subsidy removal.

“If more money is coming in, why does the debt keep climbing? If Nigerians have sacrificed so much, where are the results?

“A government cannot keep announcing savings, signing loans and asking the same struggling families to wait for relief.”

He said the question before Tinubu was no longer how many development programmes his government could name, but what Nigerians could see, use and independently verify.

“Show us the money already received. Show us what it built. Show us who benefited. Account for the debt already on Nigeria’s books before borrowing another dollar.”

World.title: NBA Raises The Alarm Over Plateau Killings, Seeks State Police, Security Reforms
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

The four branches of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) in Plateau State have condemned the worsening wave of attacks across the state and called for urgent constitutional, security and judicial reforms to halt the persistent loss of lives and property.

Addressing a joint press conference Monday in Jos, the NBA branches in Jos, Bukuru, Pankshin and Shendam described the recent attacks in Mangu, Barkin Ladi, Riyom and Bokkos Local Government Areas as a grave indictment of the state’s capacity to fulfil its constitutional responsibility of protecting citizens.

The association lamented the continuing bloodshed despite security measures, noting that terrorists had in some instances attacked communities during curfew hours, killing residents and vigilantes.

It warned that the unchecked violence, displacement of communities and alleged occupation of ancestral lands by attackers pose a serious threat to public confidence, law and order.

While commending President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for his recent visit to Plateau and his support for the creation of state police, the NBA urged the Federal Government to go further by sponsoring constitutional amendments that would place security on the Concurrent Legislative List, thereby granting state governors greater operational control over security architecture within their states.

The association also called for improved welfare and equipment for security personnel, enhanced border surveillance and the establishment of a military formation in the Pai River Game Reserve area, which it alleged has become a haven for bandits and terrorists operating around the borders of Plateau, Bauchi and Taraba States.

The NBA equally acknowledged efforts by the Plateau State Government, including the strengthening of Operation Rainbow, training of neighbourhood watch personnel, procurement of security vehicles and support for state policing initiatives.

However, it urged the state government to further empower Operation Rainbow, enforce the state’s anti-land grabbing law and provide additional support for police formations and forward operating bases.

The lawyers called on local government authorities, traditional rulers and communities to deepen intelligence gathering and lawful collaboration with security agencies, while cautioning citizens against spreading unverified information capable of escalating tensions.

Expressing concern over recurring reports of delayed security responses to attacks, the NBA urged security agencies to regain public trust through professionalism, patriotism and accountability. It also demanded investigations into cases where security personnel allegedly arrived at attack scenes after the assailants had fled.

On the judiciary, the association advocated expedited trials for terrorism-related offences, stiffer sanctions for lawyers who deliberately frustrate criminal proceedings, and greater transparency in the prosecution of terrorism suspects and their sponsors.

The NBA pledged to deploy the expertise of its members in criminal justice, human rights and public-interest litigation to support efforts aimed at securing justice for victims, preserving evidence of atrocities and ensuring accountability for perpetrators.

It maintained that lasting peace in Plateau State can only be achieved through the rule of law, accountability and effective protection of the constitutional right to life, warning that the continued devaluation of human life threatens national unity and public confidence in government institutions.

World.title: Tinubu: NCGC Guarantees N46.95bn Loans For 67,512 Nigerian Borrowers
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja



President Bola Tinubu has disclosed that the National Credit Guarantee Company (NCGC) has guaranteed N46.95 billion loans to Nigerian borrowers across the country.

According to him, a total of 67,512 borrowers across 25 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) have so far accessed credit backed by the NCGC, including 11,374 women.

The president, who made this disclosure Monday on his verified X handle, @officialABAT, also noted that 33.5 per cent of the beneficiaries are first-time formal borrowers, bringing more than 22,000 Nigerians into the formal credit system for the first time.

He explained that NCGC has issued N21.59 billion in guarantees, enabling participating financial institutions to extend N46.95 billion in loans to Nigerians.

The president said the figures mean that every N1 provided in guarantees has helped unlock about N2.17 in credit, describing the development as part of his administration’s efforts to move Nigeria towards a credit-based economy.

Tinubu said: “They now have a credit record they can build. Each successful repayment strengthens that record and can make the next loan easier to secure.

“Credit matters because of what people can do with it. A trader can restock before the festive season. When a manufacturer takes a bigger order and buys another machine to fill it, another Nigerian gets a job. NCGC estimates that the businesses it has supported account for 661,291 direct and indirect jobs.”

He stressed that the development provides the beneficiaries with credit records they can build upon, adding that successful repayments could strengthen their records and improve their prospects of securing future loans.

The president said access to credit gives individuals and businesses the capacity to meet immediate needs and invest in future growth, citing traders who require funds to restock and manufacturers seeking to expand production and create jobs.

According to him, NCGC estimates that businesses supported through the scheme account for 661,291 direct and indirect jobs.

Tinubu recalled that while seeking the mandate of Nigerians, he promised to move the country towards a credit-based economy and establish a loan guarantee scheme to help small businesses overcome barriers to accessing finance.

He explained that the objective was to create a system where workers could access credit to meet family needs and repay over time, while small businesses could invest against anticipated future income.

The Federal Government, he said, has been building institutions to support that objective, including CREDICORP for consumer credit and NELFUND for student financing, while the Bank of Industry (BoI) and Development Bank of Nigeria continue to provide financing to businesses.

He described NCGC as an intervention designed to address one of the major obstacles confronting viable businesses seeking bank credit, particularly where entrepreneurs have limited collateral or no established credit history.

“This is how we move from reforms to opportunities. Our reforms laid the foundation. Credit gives Nigerians the means to build on it. Tens of thousands who stood outside formal credit a year ago are now inside, borrowing to grow.”

Tinubu explained that the company shares part of the lending risk with participating financial institutions, giving lenders greater confidence to extend credit to businesses and borrowers they might otherwise be reluctant to finance.

He said NCGC currently works with 19 financial institutions comprising 13 commercial banks, three microfinance banks and three development finance institutions.

“We will keep widening that road until the opportunities our reforms create reach homes and businesses in every part of Nigeria,” the president stressed.

Reflecting on the company’s first year of operations, Tinubu said the results demonstrated how government reforms could translate into opportunities for Nigerians, particularly those previously excluded from formal credit.

He reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to expanding access to credit until more households and businesses across the country are able to benefit from the opportunities created by ongoing economic reforms.

“Promise made, promise kept. We are moving from reforms to opportunities. Nigeria First,” the president further stated.

World.title: FG Calls for Urgent Action to Protect Nigeria’s Rivers
World.content:
The Federal Government has called for integrated management of Nigeria’s rivers, forests, wetlands and watersheds to safeguard water resources, public health and livelihoods.

The Minister of Water Resources and Sanitation, Prof. Joseph Utsev, made the call on Monday in Abuja at the commemoration of the 2026 World Rivers Day.

Utsev said sustainable water resources management required coordinated action by governments, communities, traditional institutions, the private sector, development partners and civil society.

He said the theme of the celebration, ‘No Forests, No Rivers, No Water, No Life,’ underscored the interdependence between healthy ecosystems and sustainable water resources.

According to him, rivers support agriculture, food production, domestic and industrial water supply, fisheries, biodiversity, livelihoods and economic development.

He said forests, wetlands, floodplains and groundwater recharge areas helped protect river sources and regulate water flow, adding that their degradation threatened rivers and communities that depended on them.

Utsev said Nigeria’s rivers, including the Niger and Benue, as well as streams, wetlands and tributaries, constituted a shared national heritage requiring collective protection.

He identified population growth, urbanisation, untreated wastewater, indiscriminate dumping, agricultural runoff, erosion and sand mining among pressures threatening the country’s rivers.

The minister added that climate change, changing rainfall patterns, flooding and drought were compounding the challenges, requiring integrated management of watersheds and water resources.

He said the ministry was strengthening its capacity to collect, analyse and use data on rainfall, river flows, groundwater and water quality to support evidence-based water management.

Utsev said sanitation was central to river protection, noting that untreated sewage and wastewater could contaminate water sources, threaten public health, affect livelihoods and compromise water supplies.

He said 179 local government areas had been validated as Open Defecation Free under the Clean Nigeria Campaign, while more than 5,238 public sanitation facilities had been supported nationwide.

“These achievements reflect our commitment to keeping human waste out of our drains, streams and rivers,” he said.

The minister urged Nigerians to stop open defecation and indiscriminate dumping of refuse, plastics and effluents into drains, streams and rivers.

He also called for conservation of forests and wetlands, responsible wastewater management, efficient water use and stronger collaboration among stakeholders.

Utsev said the government was identifying dams requiring rehabilitation and locations for new ones as part of measures to manage excess water and mitigate flooding.

He said the government was exploring private-sector participation in dam construction and rehabilitation, stressing that government alone could not undertake all the required projects.

The minister said the ministry was also engaging relevant state governments on water-resource management, including discussions with Kebbi on measures to manage water from the Lagdo Dam.

He urged young Nigerians to deploy education, technology, entrepreneurship and community action to tackle plastic pollution, open defecation, wastewater management and ecosystem degradation.

Utsev called on the media to sustain public awareness on the relationship between forests, rivers, water and sanitation, saying behavioural change was essential to protecting water resources.

He said the Federal Government would continue to strengthen policies, institutions and programmes aimed at sustainable water resources management and improved sanitation services nationwide.

Earlier, the Director overseeing the Office of the Permanent Secretary in the ministry, Ali Dallah, said the choice of Wupa River as the venue provided an opportunity to demonstrate the need to protect and restore water bodies.

Dallah said activities for the celebration, including public enlightenment, environmental awareness and stakeholder engagement, were designed to encourage practical action to protect rivers.

He said Nigerian rivers faced pollution from domestic, industrial and agricultural activities, indiscriminate waste disposal, deforestation, erosion and uncontrolled development along river corridors.

According to him, the challenges had implications for water quality, public health, agriculture, biodiversity and the livelihoods of millions of Nigerians dependent on water resources.

Dallah said healthy forests and watersheds helped regulate water flows, reduce soil erosion, protect water quality, support groundwater recharge and maintain aquatic ecosystems.

He urged communities, institutions, businesses and individuals to support government efforts by preventing pollution, protecting watersheds and forests and promoting responsible waste management.

World Rivers Day is observed annually on the fourth Sunday of September to raise awareness of the importance of rivers and promote their conservation and sustainable management.

The event has grown into an international observance involving communities in more than 100 countries through activities such as river clean-ups, restoration projects, educational programmes and community events. (NAN)
