World.title: Tweah Warns Education Crisis Could Become Liberia’s Next Security Threat
World.content:
MONROVIA — Former Finance and Development Planning Minister Samuel Tweah has warned that Liberia’s failure to provide quality education to its citizens could evolve into a national security threat, cautioning against efforts to lower academic standards simply to increase pass rates.

By Obediah Johnson

Tweah said that while successive governments have made efforts to expand access to education, the quality of education remains a major concern, particularly amid what he described as a declining appetite for knowledge among young Liberians.



He specifically criticized the lowering of passing standards for public examinations, including the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) and university entrance examinations, arguing that reducing academic thresholds could undermine the future of Liberian students.

“This education challenge must be declared a national security [issue] by this government or any government because if the children of this country are not educated, there is a national security risk for the future,” Tweah said.

“If we lower the standard so that more people can pass WASSCE or UL entrance, we are hurting the future of the country.”

Tweah made the remarks over the weekend while delivering the keynote address at the closing and graduation ceremony of the Mother Tegeste Stewart School in Brewerville, outside Monrovia.

‘Accommodating System’

Tweah argued that Liberia’s education system risks becoming too accommodating to students who have not met the required academic standards.

He said many students have developed a habit of “by-passing the system” rather than putting in the necessary effort to study, calling for stronger academic checkpoints to ensure students meet required standards before advancing.

“The reason why somebody can pass WASSCE and not UL entrance is because they are not studying and the system is accommodative,” he said. “Accommodative system is a threat to our national security and the future of our children.”

Tweah said Liberia should focus not only on getting children into schools but also on ensuring that they receive an education capable of preparing them for university, employment and national development.

“If you start accommodation in education, you will be accommodated throughout your life,” he said. “We talk about corruption in the country, but the worst place to do corruption is with the mind.”

He further warned that compromising academic standards could increase the number of young Liberians leaving the education system without the knowledge and skills required to compete.

Tweah also questioned what he described as a disparity between students’ performance in WASSCE and their subsequent performance in university entrance examinations.

“Why would most students pass WASSCE but when those same students sit the University of Liberia [entrance examination], they don’t meet the same high threshold? What is happening in this country?” he asked.

Access Versus Quality

While acknowledging government efforts to expand access to education, Tweah said access alone would not address Liberia’s educational challenges unless greater attention was paid to quality.

He called for increased government investment in education, including funding for school construction and teacher training, in line with Liberia’s commitments under the Maputo Declaration.

Tweah also called for the construction of a community college in Montserrado County’s District 17, arguing that additional educational opportunities are needed to serve communities outside central Monrovia.

He said the government’s education agenda should strike a balance between expanding access and maintaining standards.

“Though government is striving to provide access to education for all citizens, the quality of the education being rendered must be its major concern,” he said.

‘Appetite for Prosperity’

Tweah said Liberia is facing a broader cultural challenge in which the desire for material prosperity appears to be outpacing the desire for knowledge.

“The appetite for knowledge is declining in Liberia, while the appetite for prosperity and good life is increasing,” he said.

He urged students to prioritize learning and resist pressures to compromise their education for short-term pleasure.

Addressing the graduates, Tweah said academic performance at graduation should not determine the limits of their future.

“You can graduate at the bottom of this class and you can excel beyond the valedictorian who is standing here in the next 10 years because of the choice you will make today,” he said.

He encouraged the graduates to take advantage of opportunities presented by the digital age and to make sound decisions throughout their educational and professional journeys.

Parents, Teachers Warned

Tweah also cautioned parents against seeking undue favors from school administrators and teachers to secure passing grades for their children.

He argued that such practices could contribute to the erosion of academic standards and ultimately harm students.

He also warned school owners and teachers against manipulating grades, saying corruption in education could have long-term consequences for Liberia’s development.

Tweah suggested that schools consider evaluation systems that limit students’ knowledge of who is responsible for assigning their grades, which he said could help reduce opportunities for academic manipulation.

Bishop Brown Calls for Discipline

For his part, the proprietor of Mother Tegeste Stewart School, Bishop Kortu Brown, urged the graduates to remain disciplined and God-fearing as they pursue their future goals.

Brown encouraged the graduates to be grateful for completing another stage of their educational journey and urged Liberians to continue peacefully coexisting and working together to address national challenges.

He also called for continued improvement in Liberia’s education system to enable Liberian students to compete with their peers across Africa and globally.

About 42 students who successfully passed the WASSCE graduated from the school.

World.title: Liberia: Rubber Farmer Takes Agriculture Minister To Task Over Executive Order 166, Calls For Presidential Repeal
World.content:
Monrovia – Since informing the House Committee on Agriculture that he gave the advisement to President Joseph Nyuma Boakai for the issuance of Executive Order 166 on the exportation of raw rubber, Agriculture Minister Dr. Alexander Nuetah has been a subject of heavy criticism from local rubber farmers.

By Emmanuel Weedee-Conway

The CEO of Meawon Liberia Incorporated, Mr. Charles Bamakpeh, is one of several rubber farmers to have taken the Minister to task for advising the President to issue what rubber farmers see as a “death sentence” for local farmers and businesses.



Predicated upon this, Bamakpeh wants the Order, which was signed on June 26, 2026, repealed so as to boost the local rubber industry.

Bamakpeh, who has been a leading voice against the operationalization of this Executive Order, points out that this Presidential directive is crippling the businesses of local rubber farmers.

Bamakpeh, as usual, informed the media on the weekend that warehouses across the country are overflowing with unsold rubber, long-standing export contracts have been terminated, and thousands of smallholder farmers are now forced to sell at rock-bottom prices just to survive.

“Meawon Liberia Inc. and many other Liberian-owned companies have been completely cut off. We can no longer honor our international trade agreements. Our workers are now jobless, and farming families cannot sustain their homes or send their children to school,” he stated.

For him, Executive Order 151, which allowed the export of unprocessed rubber upon payment of US$150 per metric ton – a system he intoned, kept local businesses alive while generating revenue for government was the best option that supports the growth of local economy.

According to the Meawon boss, the new Order does not serve ordinary Liberians, but rather protects foreign concession companies and paves the way for a foreign monopoly over Liberia’s rubber sector.

During his appearance before the House Committee on Agriculture, when he was called to provide clarity on the controversies surrounding the Order, Minister Nuetah told lawmakers of the Lower Chamber of Liberia’s bicameral Legislature that the directive was the best way forward for the industry.

But to the local farmers, this is a betrayal of trust by siding with foreign interests and, as such, the President should have him dismissed and appoint a new minister who prioritizes the business interests of local farmers.

Most disappointingly, Bamakpeh noted that the ban was imposed without any grace period, despite the Ministry of Agriculture knowing that local exporters were holding huge stocks.

“The Minister has been confrontational with farmers in the field instead of addressing their welfare and this is really killing us. He is seeking foreign investors at the United Nations General Assembly while suppressing Liberian businesses at home,” Bamakpeh asserted.

“It is my perspective that Minister Alexander Nuetah is operating with executive shielding to the detriment of Liberia’s rubber industry. We urgently request that the administration repeal Executive Order 166 and dismiss the Minister of Agriculture without delay,” Bamakpeh added.

World.title: Stakeholders call for sustained investment in key sectors
World.content:
Stakeholders have called for sustained policy direction and investment in key sectors to ensure the successful implementation of the Grow Zambia Agenda.

The stakeholders, who spoke to the media today ahead of the ceremonial opening of the First Session of the 14th National Assembly on October 9, 2026, said President Hakainde Hichilema should prioritise policies that promote sustainability in agriculture, education and economic development.

Media Network on Child Rights and Development Executive Director, Henry Kabwe says increased investment is needed in education and child protection to address challenges affecting children and their contribution to national development.

Mr Kabwe said the growing number of children living on the streets, commonly referred to as junkies, requires a comprehensive response that combines protection, rehabilitation and psychosocial support, rather than incarceration alone.

He stated that child marriage, sexual abuse and bullying in schools should also receive greater attention because of their impact on children’s development.

“Increased budgetary allocations towards free education, school feeding programmes, recruitment of more teachers, infrastructure development and provision of learning materials to cope with the country’s growing learner population under free education, currently estimated at about 2.5 million,” he added.

Mr Kabwe implored government to also strengthen measures to protect children from technological abuse while promoting responsible use of technology to enhance learning and empowerment.

He has proposed compulsory education and skills training for children living on the streets to enable them to acquire livelihoods and contribute to national development.

Mr Kabwe has also called for the inclusion of children in Ward Development Committees and other community development structures, arguing that children’s needs are often different from those of adults.

Meanwhile, Agricultural Institute of Zambia Chief Executive Officer, Mathews Ngosa has called for agricultural policies focused on raising productivity per hectare through improved seed, efficient fertiliser use, soil management, technology transfer and better farm management.

Mr Ngosa pointed out that accelerated irrigation development is also necessary to reduce the sector’s dependence on rainfall and support the Grow Zambia Agenda’s targets of producing 10 million tonnes of maize, three million tonnes of soya, one million tonnes of wheat and one million tonnes of sugar.

He said Zambia should also modernise agriculture through mechanisation and improve access to machinery for small and emerging farmers.

Mr Ngosa further called for deliberate policies to strengthen technical capacity and agricultural financing, as well as reform and expansion of the Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP) electronic voucher system.

“The transition towards fully electronic transactions in the supply of farming inputs could improve productivity and support crop diversification,” he added.

Mr Ngosa has also called for greater diversification into soya beans, livestock, fisheries, horticulture and other commercially viable value chains.

He also said investment in agricultural value addition, export-oriented production and animal health will be critical to increasing livestock and fisheries production.

Mr Ngosa has further urged increased private-sector participation in the agricultural value chain, adding that the successful implementation of the Grow Zambia Agenda will require experienced personnel in the agriculture sector.

World.title: Zesco Utd Chair demands CAF qualification
World.content:
Zesco United Board Chairperson Patricia Musiya has challenged players and technical staff to deliver a CAF slot as the 2026/27 Super Division season kicks off on October 3.

In a rallying statement ahead of the new campaign, Musiya said wearing the ZESCO badge comes with responsibility and the Ndola giants must compete strongly domestically and reclaim their place on the continent.

“We enter the season with clear ambitions. We want to compete strongly domestically, continue growing as a team and, importantly, get back to representing the country at the CAF stage,” Musiya said.

She said achieving the twin targets will require unity, discipline, commitment and a collective desire to succeed.

To the players and technical bench, Musiya urged focus and teamwork.

“Trust in the work you have put in during preparation. Remain focused, support one another and always put the team first. There will be challenges along the way, but our strength will be measured by how we respond to them,” she said.

Musiya assured the team of full board backing.

“The Board remains fully behind the team and is committed to providing the support necessary for you to perform at your best. In return, we ask you to uphold the values of ZESCO United, represent the Club with professionalism and give your very best every time you step onto the pitch.”

She also thanked supporters for their unwavering belief and urged them to continue standing with the team throughout the season.

ZESCO United, nine-time Zambian champions, missed CAF inter-club competition last season after finishing outside the top two.

World.title: Thole trial set for October 1
World.content:
The Kabwe Magistrates’ Court has set October 1, 2026 for commencement of trial in a matter in which 33-year-old businessman James Thole, popularly known as Commander One, is facing charges of assault, malicious damage, criminal trespass and undue influence.

Thole, of house number ZC149 in Katondo Compound, is facing five counts before Resident Magistrate Sebastian Mwenya.

When the matter came up for mention, Magistrate Mwenya adjourned it to October 1 for commencement of trial after the State and defence counsel agreed on the date.

“Today you just appeared so that we set your date to start your trial. Your counsel and the State have agreed that we start your case on October 1, 2026. Meanwhile, you are remanded in police custody,” Magistrate Mwenya ruled.

Meanwhile, Magistrate Mwenya, sitting in for Principal Resident Magistrate Mubita Kalaluka, adjourned another matter in which Thole is accused of assaulting his wife, Sandra Nachilindi, to October 9, 2026 for commencement of trial.

Thole is facing one count of assaulting Ms Nachilindi on September 4, 2026, contrary to the law.

“In the absence of the trial magistrate, who is out of the station for other duties, your matter is adjourned to October 9, 2026 for commencement of trial,” Magistrate Mwenya said.

In three other matters before Magistrate Neto Zulu, Magistrate Mwenya adjourned the cases to October 1, 2026 for mention.

Thole was scheduled to appear before Magistrate Zulu for a ruling and possible trial, but the court could not proceed because Magistrate Zulu was away on other national duties.

Thole is currently facing a total of nine charges in three different courts at the Kabwe Magistrates’ Court.

The accused remains in police custody.

World.title: World Bank supports Capital Projects in Central
World.content:
Central Province Permanent Secretary Milner Mwanakampwe has commended the World Bank for supporting local councils to undertake capital projects through the Zambia Devolution Support Programme.

Dr Mwanakampwe said the province has benefited from the construction of truck parks, water schemes and a bus station under the programme, which aims to strengthen financing, institutional performance and accountability of local authorities.

He said this when a World Bank team led by Senior Public Sector Specialist Lobna Ahmed paid a courtesy call on him.

Dr Mwanakampwe said the Zambia Devolution programme has facilitated the construction of truck parks in Chitambo, Kapiri Mposhi and Chibombo districts.

He said although some projects are still under construction, the truck parks would help reduce traffic congestion caused by trucks parked along roadsides.

“Districts such as Kapiri Mposhi and Chibombo look like border towns because of the way trucks are parked. They were posing threats of Road Traffic Accidents,” he said.

Dr Mwanakampwe said the truck parks would also enable councils to raise revenue through parking fees.

He further said the programme has facilitated the construction of eight water schemes in Shibuyunji District to improve access to clean and safe water.

“We have seen the construction of eight water schemes, even in some places where people would share water access points with domestic animals,” he said.

He said a bus station is also under construction in Mumbwa District.

And World Bank Senior Public Sector Specialist Lobna Ahmed said the institution has partnered with the Ministry of Local Government to provide councils with funding for capital projects through structured frameworks.

Ms Ahmed said councils are required to meet specific minimum conditions and institutional requirements, including clean audit records and transparency.

She said the World Bank has allocated 210 million United States dollars towards the Zambia Devolution Support Programme over a five-year period.

Ms Ahmed said some councils were awarded K2.8 million in 2024.

“We have been awarding councils since 2023, though I must state that the funds for the year 2025 have not yet been released,” she said.

World.title: FNB offers K1.5 million land loans in Luanshya
World.content:
FNB Zambia has introduced vacant land loans of up to K1.5 million for residents of Luanshya as it reopens its refurbished branch and seeks to support the district’s economic growth.

FNB Zambia Retail Banking Executive Mwamba Musambo said the loans are repayable over a period of up to 10 years, with the land serving as security.

Mrs Musambo urged residents to prepare for opportunities expected from the development of Shaft 28, including increased demand for housing.

She said small and medium-sized enterprises can also access unsecured loans of up to approximately K1.5 million and encouraged entrepreneurs to approach the bank for business financing.

“Don’t let this pass you by. Let’s all take advantage of the opportunity,” she said.

Mrs Musambo said the refurbished branch features a business customer adviser, premium banking area, customer service centre and meeting room.

She said the investment demonstrates FNB Zambia’s commitment to Luanshya after more than 10 years of operations in the district.

“Today for us is not about opening a branch. It’s not about putting on new paint. It’s about demonstrating that Luanshya is important to us,” she said.

Luanshya District Commissioner Paul Malele welcomed the refurbishment, saying improved access to financial services would help residents and businesses participate in the district’s economic growth.

Mr Malele commended FNB for continuing to serve customers through a mobile banking unit, agents and digital channels while the branch was being refurbished.

He said investment by financial institutions supports the government’s Grow Zambia Agenda by helping entrepreneurs access capital, expand their businesses and create jobs.

Speaking on behalf of customers, local businessman Francis Chatepa said the refurbished branch had made banking more comfortable.

Mr Chatepa said customers who previously stood in queues can now sit while waiting to be served.

“We thank you so much. We just appeal to you to continue maintaining your quality service and to keep improving,” he said.

The launch was attended by Luanshya Town Clerk Collins Ndelema, who led government departmental heads, members of the business community, SMEs and residents.

World.title: Police recover suspected stolen cattle carcasses
World.content:
Police in Kitwe have recovered carcasses believed to be from two cattle suspected to have been stolen from Luanshya District.

The carcasses were recovered from a house in Garnetone, Kitwe, on Sunday morning.

Copperbelt Division Commissioner of Police Rae Hamoonga said officers from Garnetone Police Station visited the house after receiving a report that five men had been seen skinning two slaughtered cattle, one black and one brown.

Mr Hamoonga said officers recovered four pieces of carcass and a red Toyota Sienta, registration number BCG 6947 and apprehended one suspect identified as 36-year-old Tilimbali Nyirenda of Kitwe while four other suspects escaped.

Mr Hamoonga said the suspect, carcasses and vehicle were handed over to Luanshya Central Police Station for further investigations.

Mr Nyirenda has been charged with being in possession of property suspected to have been stolen or unlawfully obtained.

Police are investigating the origin and ownership of the cattle as the search for the four escaped suspects continues.

Mr Hamoonga has urged anyone who recently lost cattle matching the description to visit Luanshya Central Police Station with information or documents that could help establish ownership.

He has also appealed to cattle owners in Luanshya and surrounding areas to assist in identifying the animals.

World.title: Luanshya urged to invest in manufacturing
World.content:
Luanshya District Commissioner Paul Malele has called on residents and investors to establish manufacturing industries that can turn the district’s growing economic activity into jobs and sustainable local businesses.

Mr Malele said Luanshya should build on its agricultural production by developing industries that add value to locally produced goods, rather than relying solely on the revival of mining.

He said farmers in the district produced more than 185,000 50-kilogramme bags of maize, equivalent to approximately 9,250 metric tonnes.

Mr Malele said the district should move beyond producing raw commodities and establish industries that can utilise local agricultural products.

“Let’s open industrial parks and manufacturing industries,” he said.

He was speaking on the sidelines of the reopening of FNB Zambia’s refurbished Luanshya branch.

Mr Malele said Luanshya’s economic growth should be driven by opportunities in agriculture, commerce, entrepreneurship and manufacturing, alongside its mining heritage.

He urged residents to actively participate in establishing businesses that can create employment and stimulate local economic activity.

Mr Malele said the call was in line with the Eighth National Development Plan, which prioritises economic diversification, private sector development and increased citizen participation in economic growth.

He welcomed FNB Zambia’s continued investment in Luanshya, saying access to financial services and capital could help entrepreneurs establish and expand businesses.

He encouraged residents to utilise available financial services to turn the district’s potential into sustainable economic activity.

World.title: Economist highlights impact of Turkish airlines exit
World.content:
A Lusaka-based Economist Kelvin Chisanga says the Turkish Airlines’ decision to permanently remove Lusaka from its future schedule is more than the loss of an airline route.

Mr Chisanga says the withdrawal is a serious warning about Zambia’s economic connectivity and the strength of the demand that the country is creating for global markets and opportunities.

He explained that the removal means losing an important channel for investors, tourists, business travelers and international commercial relationships.

Mr Chisanga told the media that for investors, connectivity affects the cost and convenience of reaching Zambia, visiting projects and meeting partners.

On the tourism front, Mr Chisanga added that it affects how easily visitors can reach our destinations.

“This matters because Zambia recorded 2.19 million international tourist arrivals in 2024, a 58% increase from 2023. That demonstrates significant tourism potential but connectivity must grow alongside demand.

At the same time, Zambia’s macroeconomic picture is improving: GDP grew 7.2% in Q2 2026, while inflation fell to 6.2% in August,” Mr Chisanga indicated.

He said the challenge now is converting macroeconomic stability into investment, tourism, trade, jobs and stronger international demand.

And he charged that Zambia needs a National Air Connectivity Strategy linking aviation directly to investment, tourism and trade.

“We should identify priority routes, review airport and aviation costs, strengthen tourism and conference marketing, develop air-cargo opportunities, attract more business travel and consider targeted, performance-based route incentives,” he recommended.

Mr Chisanga noted the need to build an economy where global airlines see growing demand to serve Lusaka.

The Istanbul-based carrier, Turkish Airline is permanently discontinuing five African routes including Luanda in Angola, Juba in South Sudan, Kinshasa in the Democratic Republic of Congo Libreville in Gabon and Lusaka Zambia.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - September 28, 2026
World.content:
press review

Monrovia — At Least 27 Killed in Separate South African Mass Shootings

Two mass shootings hours apart between Saturday night and early Sunday morning have left at least 27 people dead in townships near Johannesburg and Cape Town. The South African Police Service (SAPS) confirmed the incidents, which mark the latest wave of severe criminal violence in a country long struggling with exceptionally high rates of gun violence and homicide. SAPS said officers are searching for multiple suspects responsible for the attack. Between April and June, South Africa recorded 5,427 homicides - an average of nearly 60 per day -predominantly concentrated in impoverished districts. The country's severe violence prompted President Cyril Ramaphosa to deploy soldiers to the streets in March, describing organized gang crime as the single greatest threat to South Africa's democracy and economic development

Weah, Opposition Leaders Launch New Coalition in Liberia

Opposition leaders who were once staunch rivals have signed a joint communiqué agreeing to unite against the policies of President Joseph Boakai. The coalition includes former President George Weah, Alexander Cummings - who previously formed an opposition bloc against the Weah administration - and several other prominent politicians. In the communiqué, the parties pledged to "jointly and constructively" hold the Boakai Government accountable for its stewardship of the Republic. They accused the administration of failing to protect territorial integrity along the border with Guinea, engaging in selective anti-corruption and anti-drug efforts, defying Supreme Court rulings, and leveraging a new cybercrime law to silence critics.

Kenya High Court Pardons Police Chief Kanja Over Protest Order Breach

Kenya's High Court has pardoned Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja for failing to comply with an order prohibiting police from barricading roads during public demonstrations. The court, however, issued a stern warning that Kanja could face a custodial sentence if the order is breached again. The court said Kanja appeared in person alongside other senior police officials, assuring the bench that the judicial order would be strictly respected and enforced moving forward.

Two Dead Following Massive Gathering at Mozambique Beach

At least two people died when tens of thousands gathered at Macaneta Beach in the Marracuene District of Mozambique's Maputo Province. The tragedy occurred during national holiday celebrations marking the 60th anniversary of the National Liberation Struggle and Armed Forces Day. Marracuene authorities clarified that the deaths occurred on land and were not caused by drowning, pushing back against rumors claiming up to 20 people had drowned. Local officials confirmed that municipal police and lifeguard teams were deployed to manage the crowd, estimated between 30,000 and 40,000 people.

Nigerian Presidency Dismisses Concerns Over Tinubu's Absence

The statement follows mounting public criticism regarding his absence, including his decision to skip the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York.

World.title: South Africa: 'We Were Never Consulted' - Cape Town Residents Challenge Equinix Data Centre
World.content:
The Housing Assemblyâs Kenneth Matlawe hosted a panel discussion about the impact of data centres with Mohammad Amir Anwar from the University of Edinburgh and Pitso Tsibolane and Timothy Carr from the University of Cape Town.

Rezoning appeal has temporarily halted plans

About 70 activists and community representatives attended a panel discussion about the possible impact of a proposed hyperscale data centre in Cape Town.

The application to rezone King Air Industria was approved by the Municipal Planning Tribunal on 14 July.

The approval is temporarily halted as local activists and residents appeal it.

Bishop Lavis community leader Michael Hoffmeester lives less than three kilometres from the site of where a hyperscale data centre has been proposed for Cape Town.

He said he has been struggling to answer questions from the community about the data centres. The little information they have received about the facility, Hoffmeester said, has been technical and complex.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"We cannot understand them," Hoffmeester said. "How can I explain to the community what we were told if I don't even understand it?"

Hoffmeester joined about 70 activists and representatives from communities surrounding the proposed site at a meeting hosted by the Housing Assembly at the Central Methodist Church on Saturday.

Also in attendance were members of non-profit organisations such as Open Secrets and Foxglove, the Legal Resources Centre, the South African Human Rights Commission and Green Anglicans.

Communities surrounding the proposed data centre include the Barcelona informal settlement, Bishop Lavis, Gugulethu and KTC, where some residents still battle daily with unreliable access to water and electricity.

The application for rezoning, subdivision, consolidation and amendment of conditions, which paves the way for one, possibly two, data centres, was approved by the Municipal Planning Tribunal on 14 July.

Activists and residents lodged a formal appeal in August against the land use approval that will allow US technology company Equinix to build a data centre at King Air Industria. They say the application should have been rejected because of inadequate information about the data centre's impact on surrounding communities, in particular on electricity and water resources, as well as emissions and noise.

The appeal has legally suspended the approval until the formal internal appeal process has been completed.

Hoffmeester told the meeting on Saturday that he and other Bishop Lavis residents were never consulted about the project. Hoffmeester suggested that the land for the project be used for housing or to create a recreational area for young people.

Pitso Tsibolane, a senior lecturer in information systems at UCT, said, "We just survived loadshedding ... For over a decade, you and I had to battle through a full day without guaranteed electricity, and in some households, for days and weeks even. Suddenly, we have enough electricity to power all of these data centres."

Some panellists challenged the suggestion that data centres would bring jobs to the surrounding communities. University of Edinburgh senior lecturer Mohammad Amir Anwar said that based on his research, he roughly estimated that the proposed Equinix facility would create only about 120 jobs directly at the construction phase and 40 once it is running.

Close 

Several activists raised concerns about the prioritisation of such a facility over housing.

The Housing Assembly's Kashiefa Achmat said the lack of easy-to-understand information about the centre is concerning. She said they are campaigning for a moratorium on data centre development until there is a better understanding and commitment on how communities' rights and concerns will be taken into account.

World.title: Kenya: Murkomen Wants Community Reports Turned Into Strategic Security Intelligence
World.content:
Nairobi — Interior and National Administration Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has called for a stronger system to turn community information into actionable intelligence, saying citizen participation could become a critical pillar of Kenya's national security strategy.

Murkomen said the Government should develop mechanisms that allow information gathered from different communities to be analysed collectively, enabling security agencies to identify emerging threats and respond before they escalate.

"Ten communities reporting similar patterns is a signal that can reveal a pattern, enabling us to anticipate future risks and guide policy. It then becomes strategic intelligence," Murkomen said.

The CS spoke at the National Defence College in Nairobi while delivering a lecture on Citizen Participation as a Strategic Pillar of National Security.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

He said the Government's approach should move beyond conventional community policing to create a continuous flow of information between citizens and security agencies.

Murkomen cited Rwanda's experience in citizen participation in strategic intelligence as a lesson Kenya could draw from, while identifying Jukwaa La Usalama as a platform that could help institutionalize public participation in security governance.

"Jukwaa La Usalama gives Kenya an opportunity to make that relationship between Government and citizens a permanent part of security governance," he said.

The CS said the Government was committed to institutionalizing the platform to give Kenyans a structured avenue to raise security concerns and participate in decision-making.

However, Murkomen said the success of Jukwaa La Usalama should not be measured simply by the number of public meetings held, but by what happens after citizens raise concerns.

"We will therefore continue to enrich the model, creating a continuous two-way relationship, identifying problems, connecting those problems to multi-agency action, and reporting back on what has changed," he said.

The proposed approach would place greater emphasis on tracking issues raised by communities, the response from government agencies and whether interventions produce measurable changes.

Murkomen said stronger citizen engagement could therefore help bridge the gap between information held by communities and formal government security structures, while strengthening public participation in national security matters.

World.title: Harbaugh brothers really love J.J. McCarthy and that's one reason he's going to the New York Giants in a trade
World.content:
Jim Harbaugh famously said J.J. McCarthy was the greatest quarterback ever to play at the University of Michigan and then boasted he was the best quarterback available before the 2024 draft. John Harbaugh, Jim's brother, apparently believes him.

The New York Giants and Minnesota Vikings have agreed to a trade that will send McCarthy, a 2024 first-round pick, to play for John Harbaugh's team in the Big Apple in exchange for a mid-round 2027 draft pick and a chance to salvage their season.

John Harbaugh apparently thinks McCarthy has some of what his brother predicted still in him despite rough times in Minnesota. And as the Giants are 2-1, the coach is doing what he can to win.

MINNESOTA VIKINGS SURPRISINGLY DEMOTE FORMER FIRST-ROUND PICK JJ MCCARTHY TO THIRD STRING

But, let's be honest.

If McCarthy continues being what he's been, this ain't going to salvage the season for the Giants. Sorry to rain on your tickertape parade, Giants fans.

This move is more to avoid humiliation if starter Jameis Winston gets hurt.

The Vikings are trading McCarthy for a fifth-round pick in 2027 only three years after drafting him in the first round because, well, the experiment failed. They do not believe they can salvage him.

The Vikings won't say this publicly.

They'll say something like they wish McCarthy the best with his new team. But the truth is they've moved on because McCarthy has been too-often injured and too inconsistent when he has been able to play or practice.

Lately, McCarthy dropped from the team's starter at the end of last season, to fighting for the starting job with Kyler Murray in training camp, to losing that battle, to then dropping to third string when the regular season began.

When Murray missed time after suffering a concussion in the season-opener, the Vikings turned to Carson Wentz in his place. McCarthy remained a backup.

That was a signal the Vikings, perhaps been most successful team at lifting up quarterbacks in recent years after they resurrected Sam Darnold's career, were waving the white flag on McCarthy.

JAXSON DART TORE HIS MCL AND MENISCUS WHICH REQUIRE SURGERY AND ENDS HIS 2026 SEASON WITH THE NEW YORK GIANTS

But one team's trash is another team's treasure.

The Giants see McCarthy as a backup option to Winston after they lost starter Jaxson Dart to a likely season-ending knee injury in Week 2.

McCarthy is expected to join the Giants and try to learn the system and eventually unseat Jake Haener as the backup this season.

In a best-case scenario, the Giants are thinking McCarthy might even be worth a look as a starter later this season if Winston is injured or his performance falters.

The long-term outlook of this trade is not that the Giants are replacing Dart with McCarthy. That's not it.

They are not replacing one oft-injured quarterback prospect with big upside with an oft-injured quarterback prospect that has less upside. The Giants remain committed to Dart and his development.

But McCarthy serves in the short-term and becomes something of a rental through 2027 while he's still on his rookie contract.

And if he ever lives up to his 2024 Jim Harbaugh billing, well, awesome!

Brother John Harbaugh will benefit and look like a genius.

World.title: Actor Robert Davi swapped LA’s homelessness and crime for Florida skies
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

While veteran actor, singer and filmmaker Robert Davi has long been an outspoken critic of California’s political leadership, its current policies and Hollywood’s cultural direction, he never really saw himself leaving the Golden State.

The 75-year-old character actor, known for playing iconic tough guys in films like "The Goonies" and "Die Hard," as well as a James Bond villain in "License to Kill," may have been born and raised in a tight-knit Italian family in Queens, New York but Los Angeles became his adopted home in 1977.

Like many others before and after him, he headed west to the Golden State when his on-screen career began to take off, and he grew accustomed to the California lifestyle.

ZACHARY LEVI CALLS CALIFORNIA A ‘FAILED STATE’ THAT IS ‘LITERALLY AND FIGURATIVELY ON FIRE’ AFTER TEXAS MOVE

But for Davi, who has also been vocal about what he sees as a political blacklist in Hollywood because of his support for President Donald Trump, there were multiple breaking points that he said ultimately led him to sell his home and leave the state for Florida.

This January will mark four years since he and his family joined other Californians who left for the Sunshine State.

"The overwhelming influx of homelessness in all communities, the political corruption and the waste of money by the local education agencies in Los Angeles that’s not used for students but for administration costs, and most of that goes to the political party of their choice, and the mismanagement of the LA fires were all [contributing] factors," Davi told Fox News Digital.

HOMEOWNERS IN LEAFY ENCLAVES HIT BY BURGLARS ZEROING IN ON HIGH-END HOMES FOR SMASH-AND-GRAB SCORES

"When I first came to LA, I could go to CVS and it was fine. I could go to a store. It was fine. Now they have gates, they have guards and items are behind lock and key because of the rampant crime," Davi added, noting, "It’s about people coming in and the acceptable aspect of going into any store and ripping off what they want and not being stopped."

Still, like many who fall in love with California’s weather and relaxed lifestyle, Davi hung on to the home he loved, hoping what he saw as rising crime and political dysfunction might somehow improve.

But it was the Dec. 1, 2021, home invasion and killing of Jacqueline Avant — the wife of Grammy-winning music executive Clarence Avant — at her Beverly Hills home that became the last straw for Davi.

The 81-year-old was the mother of Alexander Avant and Nicole Avant, the former U.S. ambassador to the Bahamas and wife of Netflix co-CEO and chief content officer, Ted Sarandos.

KELSEY GRAMMER SUSPECTS HE 'MAY HAVE' LOST HOLLYWOOD ROLES DUE TO CONSERVATIVE VIEWS

"Why did I leave California? It was knowing this and watching this happen. It was the nail in my coffin," Davi said. "California was seeping into this s---, the crime that was happening within communities and continually encroaching into communities … a home invasion and murder by a criminal that was let go three different times?"

A classically trained singer in both opera and traditional pop and jazz, Davi is known for performing the music of his idol, Frank Sinatra. World.title: Reporter's Notebook: Senate Republicans scrap early exit from Washington as midterm stakes soar
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

It’s a calculation by Republicans to keep the Senate in session this week.

Yes. The Senate was scheduled to meet anyway over the next few days. But the general consensus early last week was that the Senate would be done then, and those facing competitive races would be back home campaigning.

Then Wednesday hit.

Republicans wanted to stay in Washington. For a very specific reason. And many of them told Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., as much at their weekly luncheon.

"Odds are we plan on being here next week," said Thune.

REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: CONGRESS STRUGGLES TO FIND A MESSAGE THAT RESONATES WITH VOTERS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS

One Senate aide compared the Senate’s schedule to a cat chasing a beam of light from a laser pointer.

But the Senate is in fact meeting. There are reasons. Most of them are political.

The Senate wasn’t quite done with the bill to regulate money in intercollegiate athletics last week. And with the affordability question vexing Republicans, they really didn’t want to pass the college sports bill and promptly vacate Washington. That would be an awkward punctuation point at the end of the legislative sentence before the midterms. GOPers wanted something more substantive. Democrats might have presented that opportunity to Republicans on a platter.

Before the House left for the midterms the week before last, it accentuated its session by passing the Ratepayer Protection Act, 417-3. Let me tell you, not much passes around here with 417 votes. Like their Senate colleagues, House Republicans also worry about voters doubting they’re addressing affordability. So this bill hit the mark for them.

The legislation defrays the costs ratepayers fork out for their utility bills if they’re driven up by data centers. This forces the tech companies which run the data centers to foot the bill.

Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, is one of the most vulnerable Republicans on the ballot this fall. Husted’s longtime support for data centers is also dragging him down in the eyes of some voters. Husted tried to fix that. He went to the floor and asked for the Senate to pass on the spot the House bill. However, Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., objected, blocking the effort.

FOX NEWS POLL: ECONOMIC ANXIETY AND CANDIDATE CONCERNS DEFINE OHIO SENATE RACE

Republicans viewed that as an opening. Democrats stood in the way of passing a bill on affordability which 417 bipartisan House members supported without blinking. Senate GOPers immediately seized this opportunity as a wedge against their adversaries. And, they interpreted this as a chance to assist their Ohio colleague.

"Tell the data centers we're happy to have you. But you've got to pay your own electricity. People are not going to pay for it," said Sen. John Kennedy, R-La.

Republicans were already leery about the uneven political footing when it comes to AI. Even more so with data centers. Voters are not enamored with the results of the Big, Beautiful Bill, passed last summer. But dealing with data centers is more immediate and might resonate with those who soured on the Republican brand.

"In Missouri, people are absolutely scared to death that these data centers are going to take all the prime farm ground of the state. And then they're going to raise electricity bills so high, no one will be able to afford them," said Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo.

The official schedule intended for the Senate to meet this week. But once September hit and no government shutdown loomed, senators from both sides – especially those facing challenging elections – wanted to skip Washington and campaign back home. Yours truly asked Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., why his party stood in the way of the Senate aligning with the House on that data center/utilities measure.

"Was this blocked in the Senate last week by Democrats as an effort to prevent Sen. Husted from having a win in this competitive race?" I asked.

"Sen. Husted's bill is a fraud. It's voluntary. No company has to do it. The bill we have is mandatory. It is much stronger and is what is needed," replied Schumer.

There is something to Schumer’s argument about how muscular the bill is. The legislation says public utility regulators must only consider a standard for ratepayers. Nothing is required. Thus, there’s wiggle room for tech firms.

HAWLEY TAKES AIM AT 'CORPORATE WELFARE' AFTER GOP-BACKED TAX BREAK BOOSTED CONTROVERSIAL INDUSTRY

"What we're saying is that we can do much better," said Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md. "Is it a little step forward? Yes. But it's not meeting the moment. So our view is we should expand it to make sure that ratepayers aren't having to subsidize the richest corporations on the planet."

But a lot of Republicans aren’t buying what Schumer and Van Hollen are saying. The Democratic objections are all about three things: Politics. An endangered GOP senator in the most expensive Senate contest in the country. And, Democrats are hoping to flip the seat in their favor.

"Sen. Schumer, what he cares about is the midterm election and politics. And I don't think he cares about the substance of this," said Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas. "Obviously there's a hot and heavy Senate race going on in Ohio, and he doesn't want to let Sen. Husted have something he can talk about when he goes home."

Republicans view the opportunity to turn the affordability issue against Democrats – capitalizing on Schumer’s remark and forcing Democrats to take a stand. Either you’re for affordability (especially as it pertains to the toxic issue of data centers) or you’re not. Moreover, this could boost Husted in his competitive contest with former Sen. Sherrod Brown, D-Ohio. In fact, it was the Senate GOP’s campaign arm which specifically flagged vulnerabilities for Republicans generally and Husted in particular over the summer.

Thune tees up a test vote on Wednesday to dare Democrats to either start debate on the bill or block it again. That vote requires 60 yeas. So Democratic cooperation is required. Although there’s skepticism anything happens, some Democrats may vote for it. That means the Senate is on the bill. And it’s open to debate and amendments. Thune would have to forge a bipartisan time agreement to finish the measure quickly.

Otherwise – by the book – this would drag into the weekend. And no one wants that. Especially Republicans with competitive races.

12 RACES SCRAMBLE SENATE BATTLEFIELD AS DEMOCRATS EYE COMEBACK

Thune and Schumer want senators back home campaigning. If Democrats impede the legislation Wednesday, the Senate might hang around Thursday or that’s it until after the midterms. Regardless, Republicans will have engineered a vote which they can boomerang against Democrats. Or, at least help Husted and send him back to the Buckeye State with a win.

While it’s not the best optic for Democrats to oppose this bill, their resistance might not directly wound anyone this fall. The reason: Democrats have a lot of chances to pick up seats. But vulnerable Democrats aren’t on the ballot. None of the Democratic Senate nominees in competitive seats like Maine, Florida, North Carolina, Ohio, Michigan, Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, Kansas and Alaska currently hold office. The only sitting Democrat in the cycle who has a mild race is Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va.

So for the Democrats, this is about playing defense. For Republicans, this is about playing offense. And the GOP is on offense primarily for Husted.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

But the willingness of Senate GOPers to spend an extra week in Washington speaks volumes. It underscores how worried they are about the affordability issue. And in particular, their concern about elevating the work of Husted.

World.title: FBI co-Deputy Director Andrew Bailey steps down after one year on the job
World.content:
WASHINGTON — Another top FBI official is leaving the bureau after just a year on the job.

Andrew Bailey, who joined the FBI in the newly created position of “co-deputy director” in September 2025 to work alongside then-Deputy Director Dan Bongino, is stepping aside, two people familiar with the matter told NBC News. Bailey confirmed his move later Monday morning on social media.

An internal FBI email said Bailey was leaving for family reasons, the two people familiar with the matter said. Bailey had been the attorney general of Missouri before resigning his position to join the FBI last year.

The FBI referred a request for comment to a post Bailey made on social media, stating that he wanted to thank President Donald Trump, Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel for the opportunity.

“Under President Trump’s leadership, we have delivered historic results in our mission to Make America Safe Again. With great pride in what we have accomplished, I am announcing that I am stepping down to return to my family in Missouri,” Bailey wrote. “I am confident Director Patel will continue to reform the FBI, combat violent crime, defend the homeland, ensure strong organizational accountability, and restore public trust in this institution of excellence.”

Bongino, a conservative podcaster and former Secret Service member, subsequently left his job to return to podcasting after just under a year at the FBI. The nontraditional co-deputy structure, set up when Bongino was in the position, remained in place. Bongino was then replaced by Chris Raia, whose background as a career FBI special agent was more in line with the tradition of having the critical No. 2 position filled by someone with extensive knowledge of the bureau.

MS NOW first reported Bailey’s planned departure.

Patel, who is suing The Atlantic for $250 million over an article about his leadership at the bureau, has recently gotten into heated exchanges with Democratic members of Congress over his leadership at the FBI.

World.title: Stocks fall, oil rises and bond yields surge as geopolitics keeps markets on edge
World.content:
Stocks fell on Monday alongside jumps in both bond yields and the price of oil as geopolitical upheaval remained front and center for traders.

The S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.6% as oil prices staged a 3% rally, pushing Brent crude oil to nearly $108 per barrel.

The level would be the highest for Brent, the European benchmark, since Sept. 15. U.S. crude oil also rose to almost $96.

Oil’s renewed rise was briefly halted earlier Monday after reports said that mediators planned to meet with U.S. and Iranian officials separately to discuss the ongoing stalemate between the two sides over the war with Iran. Iran’s semi-official ISNA news agency downplayed the significance of the meetings, saying that Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, would attend talks with mediators, but said no U.S. representatives would be present.

Over the weekend, President Donald Trump said he had rejected a recent proposal from Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, through which critical energy supplies flowed before the war.

“They want to make a deal, and I think that’s fine,” Trump told reporters in Washington. “I like making a deal too, but ... that deal would not be acceptable.”

The momentary pause in oil’s rise, a familiar feature of this year’s turbulent markets, was short-lived.

Bond yields surged to fresh multi-year highs.

By mid-morning, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield had risen to 5.27%, its highest level since mid-June 2007. A wide swath of other Treasurys also continued to trade above 5%, and the yield on the 30-year bond hit its highest level since May 2004.

The 2-year Treasury, which is often viewed as a signal of where the market expects central bank rates to go, reached its highest level since 2024.

Market watchers’ anxiety has grown alongside the rise in bond yields.

“The significant increase in oil prices so far this year hasn’t knocked the wind out of the global economy’s sails,” longtime market analyst Ed Yardeni wrote Saturday. “The question is whether rapidly rising interest rates will do so.”

“Unfortunately, these higher rates also exacerbate the outlook for large government deficits worldwide,” wrote Yardeni, president of Yardeni Research.

Still, stocks have largely remained resilient in the face of rising inflation from higher oil prices and bond yields that keep shooting higher.

Part of the reason why “is that financial conditions have changed little” since January, said analysts at Goldman Sachs. They added that “the substantial rise in interest rates has been nearly offset by the effects of higher equity prices.”

But the equity market’s rise this year has been driven primarily by just a few sectors, which troubles some analysts.

For the year so far, the S&P 500 has risen a little more than 12%. But a look under the hood reveals a different story. The information technology sector has gained 28% this year and the energy sector has added 38%.

The financial, real estate, utilities, consumer staples, consumer discretionary and communication services sectors have all gained less than 10%.

The health care, industrials and materials sectors are up 10%.

On top of higher oil prices, rising bond yields and geopolitical headlines that could swing stocks in either direction at a moment’s notice, the end of the month features prominent central bank meetings, including at the Federal Reserve, where rates could rise further.

World.title: White House releases new taxpayer-funded ad describing ‘final battle’
World.content:
The Trump administration put out a new ad this weekend as part of its “PSA” campaign, this time showing President Donald Trump walking down a hallway as he asks people to join him in his fight to “expel the warmongers from our government.”

The ad — which at the end says it was “Paid for by the U.S. government” — is nearly identical to an ad put out by Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign.

Trump posted that ad to Truth Social in January 2024. The repurposed ad now includes “Paid for by the U.S. government.” But it excludes the last few seconds of the 2024 ad, which ends with text reading “Join President Trump’s fight to save America” and his 2024 campaign logo.

The ad signals an expansion of the White House’s controversial use of government funds to air pieces that resemble campaign s. Last week, the White House ran a television ad in which Trump described how he wanted to “defeat communism,” set to the song “Love Me” by JMSN. The White House has called the ads “public service announcements.”

In the latest ad, dramatic black-and-white video shows President Trump walking down a hallway with audio of him saying it is the “final battle” and vowing to “demolish the deep state” and “throw off the sick political class that hates our country.”

“We will rout the fake news media, and we will liberate America from these villains once and for all,” it concludes.

Federal law requires political advertisers to submit certain public disclosures and generally bans using public funds for political advertising. Since the administration maintains the ads are public service announcements, it’s not clear whether those disclosures are available. The White House has not released a specific source of government funding used to air the ads.

AdImpact, a political ad tracking firm, has estimated that the administration has spent more than $1.7 million to run these ads, which have been running heavily in recent days during prominent television programming like football games, Sunday morning news shows, and prime time broadcast shows. That said, AdImpact doesn’t have full visibility into airings on every cable channel in every market in the country, hampering that estimate.

The White House defended the ad Sunday, pointing NBC News to a statement it had offered last week when it commented on the other ads released by the administration.

“These public service announcements are about reminding Americans to love their country and understand what makes it worth defending, at home, at our borders, and abroad. The ad is educational and unapologetically patriotic. We should be proud of our country,” a White House spokesperson said.

Another White House official pushed back on the line of questioning: “The PSAs are clearly not political. The president is not on the ballot, and the ads don’t have a call to action.”

The White House did not specifically respond to NBC News’ question about the ad’s being nearly identical to the 2024 Trump campaign ad.

A White House spokesperson also pointed to past examples of ads released by former administrations, including an ad by George W. Bush’s Department of Health and Human Services, a social media campaign by Barack Obama’s Environmental Protection Agency in 2014 and 2015 and an effort by Joe Biden’s administration encouraging Covid-19 vaccination.

The nonpartisan Government Accountability Office dinged the Bush and Obama ad campaigns — Bush’s for not properly disclosing the government was the source and Obama’s for violating “publicity or propaganda and anti-lobbying provisions.”

White House communications director Steven Cheung defended the recent pro-Trump ads Sunday on social media, writing, “Don’t let the Fake News get away with their lies about our epic Public Service Announcements that have been running on tv.”

CNN and The New York Times were first to report about the ad’s being almost identical to Trump’s 2024 campaign ad.

Spending taxpayer dollars on the ads has raised legal and ethical concerns and condemnation from both parties.

“This is the sort of government propaganda one might expect in North Korea, not the United States of America, and it is an egregious and utterly illegal misuse of Americans’ hard-earned tax dollars,” congressional Democratic appropriators wrote in a letter Friday addressed to White House chief of staff Susie Wiles.

The letter was signed by Sen. Patty Murray, D-Wash.; Sen. Jack Reed, D-R.I.; Rep. Rosa De Lauro, D-Conn.; and Rep. Steny Hoyer, D-Md.

Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., said Sunday in an interview with CBS that public officials should not “spend public money on private ads for themselves.”

World.title: The dozen games that turned Week 3 into one of the wildest in NFL history
World.content:
Two seconds remained in regulation in Denver. One final play to decide the game.

Could one of the wildest Sundays in NFL history have ended any other way?

When Denver safety Talanoa Hufanga intercepted Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford in the end zone as time expired to seal a 30-26 comeback win on “Sunday Night Football,” it also capped a day that will be remembered for producing one thriller after another.

Call it the Sunday of slim margins. Of the day’s 14-game slate in Week 3, 12 finished as one-score games, the most on any Sunday in NFL history. Thirteen games were within 8 points during the fourth quarter. Six teams won after go-ahead scores within the final three minutes.

“It’s tough,” Rams coach Sean McVay said. “But this is sports.”

After watching two weeks of offensive struggles under Denver’s new play caller, Broncos fans booed their team as they ran off the field after trailing the Rams, 16-0, at halftime. Then Denver scored 16 unanswered points, setting up a fourth quarter where the teams traded momentum swings. Hufanga intercepted Stafford and ran it back for a touchdown to lead, 23-19. When a Broncos defensive back fell down on the next possession, Stafford found an open receiver for an easy, go-ahead touchdown to lead, 26-23. Denver came back and moved the ball down the field after a succession of penalties, eventually taking a 30-26 lead and leaving the preseason Super Bowl favorite Rams only 47 seconds with which to try their own rally.

It fell short by only a few yards, with no time left to spare — and it might not have even been Sunday’s wildest finish.

In Rio de Janeiro, Baltimore got the ball back with seven seconds to play in regulation after Dallas had tied the score. Somehow, that was enough time for the Ravens to launch perhaps the latest comeback drive ever — at least since one database began tracking such figures — ending in Baltimore’s walk-off field goal from 56 yards. It was the first game since the 1970 merger to feature two teams that each made a field goal in the final 10 seconds.

Improbable? It wasn’t the only game that fit the description.

Previously winless, Washington couldn’t run the ball or convert third downs against Seattle yet knocked off the defending Super Bowl champion anyway, behind backup quarterback Marcus Mariota’s three touchdowns and three Seahawks turnovers. It ended the Seahawks’ 12-game winning streak and temporarily halted their historic run as the NFL’s best road team.

In New Orleans, the Las Vegas Raiders improved to 3-0 after a 35-27 victory that saw the franchise match last season’s entire win total. They are now only the seventh team since the 1970 merger to open 3-0 after finishing the previous season with the league’s worst record, according to NBC Sports research.

The Raiders pulled it off after trailing by 11 points in the second half. A controversial fumble call on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough helped the Raiders set up their go-ahead touchdown, but it was just one of four consecutive Saints turnovers forced by the Raiders in the second half.

“In those big moments, there’s no panic,” Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby said. “We went down 11 and got together on the sideline and talked about not panicking.”

Neither did the Bills (3-0). Like Baltimore and Las Vegas, Buffalo overcame a deficit of at least 10 points, eventually beating the Los Angeles Chargers, 24-16. It was the first time since 1997 that the Bills won a game despite committing at least five turnovers. Bills quarterback Josh Allen hadn’t committed a single turnover through two weeks, only to be intercepted twice and lose a fumble against Los Angeles (0-3).

If Allen’s poor play was unexpected considering how good he had looked in MVP-level performances to begin the season, then what happened in Cleveland was the opposite. After ranking among the least efficient quarterbacks in the league for much of his tenure in Cleveland, Deshaun Watson has suddenly looked competent — and the Browns are now 2-1, after a 21-18 win. Watson threw two touchdowns, including a go-ahead score with 1:48 left in the fourth quarter. An interception of Carolina’s Bryce Young with seconds remaining clinched Watson’s 10th fourth-quarter comeback.

Indianapolis (1-2) earned its first win since last November after Spencer Shrader kicked a 43-yard field goal with 16 seconds left for a 19-17 victory that dumps Houston, a preseason Super Bowl candidate, to 0-3. The Texans made the playoffs last year after starting 0-3, too, becoming only the seventh team in NFL history to do so. Another hard road to the playoffs awaits.

In whipping rain and wind in New Jersey, the New York Giants held on for a 12-7 win in their first game since quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury. Sack artist Brian Burns injured his knee in the fourth quarter, and with 24 seconds left in regulation, Tennessee moved within 7 yards of a go-ahead touchdown. Instead, the Giants (2-1) survived after Jevon Holland intercepted Titans quarterback Cam Ward.

In Tampa Bay, the Buccaneers played in their franchise-record ninth consecutive one-score game, but Minnesota (3-0) held on, 23-16, after batting down a desperate Hail Mary heave as time expired. For Tampa, what was even more dispiriting than falling to 0-3 was that quarterback Baker Mayfield left with a dislocated thumb that puts his active league-high streak of 54 consecutive starts in jeopardy.

Defensive tackle Derrick Harmon of the Pittsburgh Steelers forces a fumble by quarterback Joe Burrow during a game at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh on Sunday. Jeff Dean / Getty Images

When Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow fumbled late in the fourth quarter, Pittsburgh exhaled with a 30-27 win over a division rival. It also breathed a sigh of relief for a different reason. Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, the NFL’s oldest active player, was showing his age. He entered Sunday having gone seven consecutive starts without throwing multiple touchdown passes. He responded with touchdown passes to three different receivers and led Pittsburgh (2-1) on a game-winning drive that ended with a 33-yard field goal with 2:15 remaining. Burrow’s fumble occurred just before the Bengals (2-1) could reach field-goal range of their own.

With one game remaining in Week 3, six teams remain undefeated after San Francisco edged out a 36-30 win over Arizona. Can the 49ers keep it up, though? A franchise known for suffering a rash of injuries got more bad news Sunday when receiver Mike Evans (ribs) and left tackle Trent Williams (stinger) left the game.

That left the Broncos and Rams to play a vital primetime game — the two Super Bowl contenders each hoping to avoid a second loss within their first three weeks. A pair of controversial defensive pass interference penalties on Denver’s go-ahead drive in the final minute rankled the Rams after the game, but comebacks have become something of a Broncos specialty.

Last season, the Broncos’ 12 comeback wins set an NFL record. Last week, Denver overcame a 10-point deficit to beat Jacksonville. Sunday’s latest rally was the 50th fourth-quarter comeback of coach Sean Payton’s career to move past Mike Tomlin for fourth-most in NFL history. It relied on the 20th touchdown of quarterback Bo Nix’s career when trailing by one score — the most in the league since 2025, when Nix entered the NFL — and resulted in Nix’s seventh career fourth-quarter comeback.

“Just a couple plays short that we left out there,” Rams receiver Konata Mumpfield said.

On a day of wild finishes and tight margins, it was a sentiment shared across the league.
