World.title: Harles Tammeleht: Business tourism could help Tallinn hotels survive the winter
World.content:
A conference center at Tallinn's Linnahall could bring visitors during the low season and help hotels and restaurants operate year-round, writes Harles Tammeleht.

According to the Estonian Convention Bureau (EKB), organizers of dozens of international professional conferences have considered Tallinn in recent years but ultimately chose other destinations. Most of these conferences draw between 1,000 and 3,500 participants, while the largest attract more than 7,000. Together, they represent nearly 60,000 delegates and an estimated €65.5 million.

Nearly all of these conferences have more than 1,000 participants and none of Tallinn's existing venues was suitable for them.

According to consulting firm Gaining Edge, the leading criterion in choosing a destination for an international conference is whether its venues have the capacity and facilities the event requires. The availability of hotels also matters.

Tallinn is ruled out because it lacks the necessary venues. Organizers generally need more than one large room: they also need smaller rooms nearby for working groups, as well as space for exhibitions, networking and catering. These requirements are why the planned large arena would not remove the need for a conference center. Estonia needs both.

Tallinn is the only capital in the Nordic and Baltic region without a large, multifunctional conference and exhibition center that meets international standards. Tampere, for example, has a population of 245,000 and hosts nearly 900 events a year. Vilnius' LITEXPO hosts 1,300, while Riga has the ATTA Center.

A conference's significance for hotels

Take an event with 2,000 delegates, each staying an average of four nights. About 85 percent of delegates at international professional conferences arrive from abroad and need a hotel room, though some share with a colleague or companion.

That amounts to 5,900 room nights or about 1,480 rooms each night. In Tallinn's hotel market, which has more than 7,100 rooms, that would occupy 21 percent of the city's total room capacity at once.

Alongside the large conference hotels, midsize and smaller hotels would fill up too. During the low season, those hotels might otherwise be half empty or closed altogether. One such event would generate about €470,000 in room revenue during the low season. Delegates' direct spending in Estonia would total approximately €2.1 million, of which nearly €540,000 would go to taxes.

International professional conferences are planned three to five years in advance and generally avoid the summer months.

Consider what would happen if the Estonian Convention Bureau's forecast proves correct and the center brings Tallinn an additional 18,000 business visitors a year or roughly eight large international conferences. Hotel occupancy would rise by 2.5 percentage points.

Two and a half percentage points may not sound like much, but it means an additional 26,600 room nights in the months when occupancy is lowest. In the hotel business, a few percentage points of winter occupancy often determine whether the year ends in a loss or a profit.

More important still, conference demand enters the market differently from leisure travel demand. During the low season, a hotel usually fills its last rooms by lowering prices. A conference room block, however, comes at a contracted rate that is generally higher than what the hotel would otherwise charge for a room in January.

Conferences are also known about well in advance. A leisure traveler books two weeks ahead; a large international conference books two to five years ahead. A hotel that knows two large conferences are coming to the city in February the year after next can plan staffing, renovations and pricing very differently from one that faces each winter with uncertainty.

Labor and investment capacity

That brings us to two problems the accommodation sector has complained about for years, both directly fueled by seasonality.

The first is staffing. Estonia's long-term tourism strategy identifies staff turnover caused by seasonality as one of the main obstacles facing accommodation and food service businesses. It sets a goal of raising the sector's value added per employee from €21,839 to €48,000. More consistent demand throughout the year is essential to reaching that goal: it allows businesses to retain permanent staff, invest in training and pay competitive wages. A seasonal hotel cannot do that, however much it wants to.

The second is accommodation capacity itself. According to an analysis by Tallinn's Strategic Management Office, the city will need another 1,400 to 2,200 rooms by 2040 to accommodate the projected number of overnight stays. But a new hotel cannot be built on the strength of seasonal demand alone. The return on such an investment is calculated over years, not three months.

Catering and the rest of the city

Conference delegates differ from the average visitor chiefly in how long they stay. An international conference delegate is known to spend about €1,045 per trip in Estonia, compared with €316 for the average foreign tourist, according to the border survey. The difference in daily spending is smaller, but two-thirds of delegates stay for three to six nights and 25 to 40 percent extend their visit for a vacation. The average foreign tourist stays 2.6 nights.

According to the border survey, foreign tourists spend an average of €34 a day on food and drink. Coffee breaks, lunches, receptions and gala dinners paid for by conference organizers come on top of that. EIS (Estonian Business and Innovation Agency — ed.) estimates that local businesses earn more than 40 percent additional revenue while an event is taking place.

Unlike some other types of visitors, conference delegates stay in the city: they sleep in hotels, eat in restaurants, use transportation and shop at local stores. According to EIS, 60 percent of international conference delegates would like to return for a vacation.

Linnahall

The Estonian Convention Bureau considers Tallinn's Linnahall suitably located and believes it could accommodate a main hall with more than 3,000 seats, a modular conference area for more than 7,000 delegates and over 10,000 square meters of exhibition space. Such a venue would also make it possible to host trade fairs, cultural events and other international gatherings that bring guests to the city's hotels and restaurants.

For the center's business model to work, it would need an operator with international expertise that actively attracts events. Nor would a conference center alone solve the seasonality of Estonia's tourism industry. Tallinn is in a region through which approximately 2,750 international conferences and trade fairs with 500 to 4,000 delegates rotate each year, so the demand already exists.

Estonia's long-term tourism strategy for 2025–2035 lists the availability of a multifunctional conference center as a measure to track. Tallinn accounts for 69 percent of overnight stays by foreign visitors in Estonia, which means Tallinn's low season is also Estonia's low season.

For years, the accommodation and food service sector has been tasked with increasing value added, lengthening visits and reducing seasonality. But those three goals cannot be achieved together without the facilities to host multiday international conferences.

World.title: 3 drones target Iranian opposition camp in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Three drones targeted the Azadi camp, a facility affiliated with the opposition Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan (PDKI) in the Koya district southeast of Erbil in the Kurdistan region of Iraq early on Monday.

According to the Kurdistan Regional Government’s (KRG) security agency, Asayish, the attacks took place in two waves between 1:40 and 2:10 a.m. local time.

The attack damaged the facility but resulted in no casualties.

Local Kurdish media, citing anonymous PDKI sources, claimed that the drones used in the attack were Iranian-made “Hadid” versions.

According to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-affiliated media agencies, the attacks targeted separatist organizations in the region.

Officials in Iraqi Kurdistan warned that the camp, which has housed displaced Iranian Kurds and the families of the party’s Peshmerga forces for over 25 years, has come under fire several times amid rising regional tensions.

The attack is the latest in a series of drone and missile strikes against Iranian Kurdish dissident sites in Iraq’s Kurdistan region.

World.title: Iraq officially declared as host of 2028 Arabian Gulf Cup
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has been officially announced as the host country for the 2028 Arabian Gulf Cup, which will be held in either Basra or Baghdad.

The Executive Office of the Arabian Gulf Cup Football Federation (AGCFF) ratified the decision during a meeting in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, where Iraq made the only formal bid to host the event.

The tournament will take place from December 9 to December 22, 2028.

The 27th Arabian Gulf Cup is currently underway in Jeddah, running from September 23 to October 6, 2026.

While Basra is anticipated to be the primary location following the successful conclusion of the 2023 edition, Baghdad is still in contention.

The Iraqi Football Association (IFA) has set a deadline to formally confirm the host city and will be expected to meet all organizational criteria in accordance with authorized standards.

The decision marks the third time Iraq hosts the tournament, with the fifth edition in Baghdad in 1979 and the 25th edition in Basra in 2023.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports to Jordan completely halt
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil exports to Jordan have completely stopped since the end of December 2025, despite ongoing negotiations this year aimed at resuming crude supplies to Amman.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that the halt in exports is linked to commercial matters and other factors involving Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) and the Jordanian side.

Al-Rikabi’s remarks come amid ongoing disputes regarding the terms of a new agreement. Informed sources had previously revealed Baghdad’s insistence on reducing tanker transport fees, while months of negotiations failed to result in a resumption of supplies.

Jordan used to receive approximately 10,000 barrels per day of Iraqi crude—representing about seven percent of its oil needs—before shipments ceased at the end of 2025.

In January, Amman has not imported oil from Iraq, compared to approximately 309,712 barrels the previous month.

Iraq’s oil supplies to Jordan stood at around 299,824 barrels in November 2025, reflecting a steady flow of approximately 300,000 barrels per month during the period before the suspension takes place.

The previous annual contract expired on June 26, 2025, prior to a three-month extension running from October through December. The extension was intended to ensure the completion of the delivery of specified volumes that had been impacted by logistical challenges.

World.title: US troops completely withdraw from Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An Iraqi government official announced on Sunday that the withdrawal of the US troops from Iraq has been completed.

The official stated that both combat and logistical support personnel have departed the country, although there has been no formal confirmation from the US side, Sky News Arabia reported.

In 2024, Iraq and the United States agreed on a timeline to end the US military presence in the country. According to the US Department of Defense, approximately 2,500 US troops had been stationed in Iraq in the past few years.

Prior to the withdrawal, US forces were deployed across Erbil in the Kurdistan region of Iraq, a base near Baghdad International Airport, and locations within the Green Zone in the capital, Baghdad.

US forces returned to Iraq in 2014 in response to a request by the Iraqi government—as part of the international coalition to combat ISIS—three years after their withdrawal following the 2003 US invasion.

While the terrorist group’s defeat in Iraq was announced in 2017, its cells remain in remote areas.

The withdrawal comes as Iraq faces security consequences linked to the conflict involving Iran, amid recent attacks targeting US facilities and forces.

World.title: India buys two million barrels of Iraqi oil at $28 discount per barrel
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Indian Oil Corp. (IOC), India’s largest state-owned refiner, has acquired 2 million barrels of Iraqi oil at a discount of almost $28 per barrel compared to the October Dubai benchmark.

The acquisition includes Basrah medium and heavy crude oil grades. IOC contracted to receive the cargo from the international trading business Mercuria on a free-on-board (FOB) basis, according to Reuters.

The crude is expected to be loaded and lifted between October 21 and October 31, 2026.

The enormous $28 reduction is due to significant regional logistics challenges. Shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, which are associated with wider geopolitical tensions, have led to substantial increases in marine freight prices, insurance costs, and transit risks for buyers.

To address these export restrictions and ensure that its oil remains attractive to major global consumers like India, significant price discounts have been introduced. These discounts aim to offset the heightened risks that refiners encounter when arranging their own transportation.

This acquisition comes after IOC purchased one million barrels of October-loading Iraqi crude straight from Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) at a discount ranging between $23 and $28 per barrel only a few days ago.

World.title: Iraq recovers 80 smuggled artifacts
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Justice successfully repatriated 80 smuggled historical artifacts and rare artworks on Monday, September 28, 2026, marking another breakthrough in federal legal campaigns to recover looted antiquities from abroad.

According to an official statement issued by the ministry, the restitution was finalized through intensive international legal proceedings managed by the Directorate of External Litigation, executed in direct operational coordination with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Embassy of the Republic of Iraq in Washington, D.C.

The ministry stated that the legal recovery operations, directed and monitored by Minister of Justice Dr. Khaled Shwani, form an integral part of Baghdad’s overarching policy to safeguard Iraq’s cultural heritage and reclaim sovereign historical assets dispersed through illicit trading networks.

Through its dedicated Department for the Recovery of Antiquities and Assets, the Directorate of External Litigation manages active cross-border claims, targeting antiquities illegally excavated from unmonitored archaeological digs as well as stolen cataloged pieces traded internationally in violation of Iraqi heritage statutes and UNESCO conventions.

Federal judicial authorities emphasized that these coordinated actions reflect the justice ministry’s structured legal mandate to track, document, and pursue stolen national assets worldwide.

By leveraging bilateral judicial agreements and working through diplomatic missions across North America and Europe, the Iraqi government aims to ensure the comprehensive preservation of Mesopotamia’s civilizational legacy and institutionalize robust legal frameworks against the illicit trafficking of cultural antiquities.

World.title: Gulf Cup 27: Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Qatar clinch semifinals as Iraq eyes decisive clash
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Matchday Two of the group stage at the 27th Arabian Gulf Cup in Jeddah concluded with three national teams securing early qualification for the semifinals, leaving the remaining knockout berth in Group A contested ahead of the final group round.

Host nation Saudi Arabia confirmed its place in the final four alongside Group B qualifiers the United Arab Emirates and Qatar, while regional football powerhouses Kuwait, Bahrain, and Yemen suffered early mathematical elimination from tournament contention.

In Group A, tournament hosts Saudi Arabia solidified their standing at the summit of the table with a maximum of 6 points and a positive four goal difference following back-to-back victories. Iraq occupies second place with 4 points and a plus-one goal differential, having recorded one win and one draw across their opening fixtures.

Oman sits third with 1 point and a negative three goal differential, while Kuwait trails at the bottom of the group with zero points and a negative two goal difference. The distribution leaves Iraq positioned for a decisive final-round Gulf derby against Saudi Arabia, coinciding with the simultaneous encounter between Oman and Kuwait to determine the group’s second qualifying spot.

Group B witnessed a decisive resolution as both the United Arab Emirates and Qatar secured semifinal qualification with a match to spare, each accumulating 6 points from two consecutive victories. The UAE maintains the top position by virtue of an advantageous goal difference of plus-seven compared to Qatar’s plus-three.

Yemen and Bahrain sit eliminated at the foot of the table without points, both carrying identical negative five goal differentials. The final group fixtures will settle group positioning between the two leading sides as the tournament bracket prepares for the knockout stage.

World.title: Iraq officially licenses Starlink satellite internet
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Communications and Media Commission (CMC) confirmed on Sunday, September 27, 2026, that satellite internet provider Starlink has secured an official operational license, formally legalizing its low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite broadband services across Iraqi territory.

Speaking to the official state news agency, CMC Chief Executive Officer Baligh Abu Kalal dismissed claims that Iraqi telecommunications traffic and user data are hosted or routed through Qatar, stating that federal security authorities maintain complete sovereign oversight over all network operations and registered hardware within the country.

The licensing milestone follows public contention between federal regulatory bodies and the Ministry of Communications. In mid-August 2026, Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad argued that the ground gateway servicing Iraq was located in Qatar, raising sovereignty concerns regarding regional content filtering, pornography blocks, and executive internet throttling during national examinations and public demonstrations.

Sanad had framed terrestrial Fiber-to-the-Home (FTTH) expansion as Iraq’s premier digital priority against foreign satellite conglomerates. Responding to these concerns, Abu Kalal clarified that Starlink’s regulatory framework incorporates a rigorous security annex, granting Iraqi intelligence and regulatory apparatuses real-time visibility into all active terminals, user registries, and equipment distributed nationally.

Abu Kalal explained that while initial deployment encountered minor delays due to multi-agency security vetting, the first batch of customer subscription terminals has been released, with sequential hardware shipments proceeding smoothly to fulfill pending consumer orders via the company’s official portal.

Although Starlink originally scheduled the construction of domestic terrestrial ground stations within two years, surging local demand has prompted expedited bilateral negotiations to install local ground gateways across Iraq ahead of schedule.

The CMC executive stressed that satellite internet governance relies fundamentally on sovereign licensing frameworks, statutory compliance, and contractual obligations, ensuring that national security protocols remain fully enforced regardless of atmospheric broadcast mechanics.

World.title: Indian imports of Russian crude oil to decline further amid lower exports, Chinese competition
World.content:
Tourists watch marine life, with the MT Desert Kite oil tanker carrying Russian oil in the background (Photo: Reuters).

Alternatives

NEW DELHI: Indian refiners expect Russian oil supplies to decline further in October and November, owing to lower exports and stiff competition from China, forcing the country to buy costlier alternatives for the rest of the year.People familiar with procurement plans told Reuters that some Indian refiners would not receive adequate Russian supplies in October and November."Demand from China has been really high. They were willing to book cargoes in advance and to pay firmer prices compared to Indian refiners," a source involved in the sale of Russian crude said.According to analytics firm Kpler, Russian oil arrivals in India are set to drop to around 1.75 million barrels per day in September, the lowest level since April.Trade data showed that arrivals had already fallen 16.5 per cent to about 2.1 million bpd in August from July, although Russia remained India's main supplier, ahead of the UAE and Venezuela.Overall availability of Russian exports has reportedly shrunk, particularly from the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk, where shipments have roughly halved as repeated drone attacks have suspended loadings.India has been the top buyer of seaborne Russian Urals crude since 2022, when Moscow diverted its energy flows away from Europe at deep discounts.In recent months, however, China, the world's top crude importer, has stepped up its purchases as Middle Eastern supplies tightened because of the Iran war.Traders told Reuters that refiners have turned to pricier replacement barrels, seeking UAE Murban, a close substitute for Russia's Urals grade, while also buying Iraqi Basrah and Angolan cargoes.Shipping dynamics have helped redirect flows to China.Seasonal navigation along the Arctic Northern Sea Route (NSR) offers a secure and cost-effective channel for Russian crude exports to China, whereas shipments to India via the Red Sea face heightened security risks linked to the conflict involving Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis."It's not so much about the price as ensuring the cargo actually reaches its destination," another trader told Reuters, adding that freight costs via the Arctic route to China are now broadly comparable with shipments through the Suez Canal.

World.title: Indo-French sat mission 'Trishna'  to map Earth's water sources on fast-track: Space minister Jitendra Singh
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India and France are preparing to launch 'Trishna' from Sriharikota in 2027 to monitor energy and water budgets of the Earth. The earth observation satellite 'Trishna' (Thermal Infra-Red Imaging Satellite for High-resolution Natural Resource Assessment), a collaborative endeavour between Isro and French space agency CNES, is engineered to deliver high spatial and high temporal resolution monitoring of Earth's surface temperature, emissivity, biophysical and radiation variables for surface energy budgeting at regional to global scale.

While meeting a big French delegation related to cooperation in the space and science sector, space and science minister Jitendra Singh said the realisation of the âjoint satellite, TRISHNA, is progressing well, and also appreciated CNES support to India's Gaganyaan programme, including supply of consumables and training of flight surgeonsâ. Indian and French teams have also initiated discussions on microgravity research and parabolic flights in connection with human spaceflight.

The 'Trishna' mission will also help in a comprehensive assessment of urban heat islands, detection of thermal anomalies linked to volcanic activity and geothermal resources, and precise monitoring of snow-melt runoff and glacier dynamics. The mission will also provide valuable data on aerosol optical depth, atmospheric water vapor, and cloud cover.

A high-level French delegation led by Philippe Baptiste, French minister for higher education, research and space, met Singh in Delhi on Monday and they talked about the Space Summit, India-France Year of Innovation 2026 and priorities in scientific and technological cooperation, including space, CEFIPRA and blue economy.





Singh said India-France space cooperation has evolved from the early sounding rocket experiments of the 1960s into a broad and expanding partnership encompassing joint satellite missions, launch vehicle technologies, human spaceflight and emerging space applications. Indian and French teams have also initiated discussions on microgravity research and parabolic flights in connection with human spaceflight.

Referring to Indiaâs space-sector reforms and the growth of the private ecosystem, he said over 400 Indian space startups are now engaged in areas, including rocket building, satellite building and space applications. He said the next phase of India-France cooperation can bring together government institutions, industries and start-ups on both sides to create a larger ecosystem and wider resource pool.

Philippe Baptiste described 'Trishna' as a strong example of what India and France can achieve together, and welcomed greater cooperation in human spaceflight, astronaut health, microgravity research and parabolic flights.

World.title: Gandhinagar civic polls: BJP hits back as Congress, AAP accuse party of misusing police, EC
World.content:
The Congress and Aam Aadmi Party accused the BJP of misusing the Election Commission and police in Gujarat.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party on Monday accused the BJP government in Gujarat of misusing the Election Commission and police to force opposition candidates to withdraw their nomination papers or have their nominations rejected ahead of the October 11 Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation elections.The BJP rejected the allegations as "baseless" and described them as a "modus operandi" of the opposition to attack constitutional organizations.The Congress, meanwhile, submitted a memorandum to the State Election Commission alleging that the BJP was misusing government machinery and police to intimidate its candidates and their family members into withdrawing their nomination papers for the civic polls, party sources told news agency PTI.According to the memorandum, Congress candidates from civic wards 6 and 7, along with their families and relatives, were allegedly being pressured by personnel from the local crime branch and local police, including an LCB police inspector, to withdraw their nominations."Such actions amount to intimidation and an abuse of power, and they seriously jeopardise the candidates' freedom of choice," the memorandum said.The deadline for filing nominations for the October 11 polls was September 26, according to the election schedule.The AAP separately alleged that the nomination form of its candidate Jitendra Chauhan from ward number 5 was rejected "solely for political reasons".AAP chief spokesperson Karan Barot said Chauhan had submitted his nomination along with all the required documents and had received an acknowledgement confirming the submission."However, he said that his form was rejected today without warning on the grounds that the mandate was lacking," Barot said.Barot alleged that there were attempts to prevent AAP candidates from contesting the elections."If Congress candidates run and win, the underlying 'arrangement' is such that they eventually desert to the BJPâa process that the AAP does not engage in. This is the reason why the forms of one of our candidates and an independent candidate were denied," he said.He also questioned the Election Commission and accused the BJP of misusing central agencies such as the CBI and the ED.Responding to the allegations, Gujarat BJP chief spokesperson Anil Patel accused the Congress of following a "modus operandi" of making baseless allegations against constitutional institutions."Congress has made the decision to target and discredit constitutional institutions both at home and abroad. Institutions established by the Constitution should be trusted," Patel said.He said democratic elections had recently been held in several states and their results announced impartially.Patel also rejected the Congress's allegations of forced withdrawals, saying it resorted to "baseless allegations" whenever it felt it was losing an election."The Congress has little faith in its own candidates. They started with EVMs, followed by SIR, and now they are accusing the Election Commission. Congress turns to fabricating accusations rather than owning up to their own failings and fortifying themselves," he said.The allegations come ahead of the Gandhinagar civic polls, where the BJP is seeking to retain its position in Gujarat's urban local bodies.In the April elections, the BJP won all but Gandhinagar and Junagadh among Gujarat's 15 municipal corporations. The ruling party also recorded victories across municipal corporations, municipalities, district panchayats and taluka panchayats, while the Congress finished second and the AAP made modest gains.The results also saw the Samajwadi Party and the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) open their accounts in Gujarat.

World.title: Parvesh Verma slap row: AAP, BJP trade barbs as protests erupt in Delhi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A war of words erupted between the ruling-BJP and the Aam Aadmi Party on Monday over a video purportedly showing Delhi PWD minister Parvesh Verma slapping a young man during a road inspection in Tilak Nagar.

The incident took place on Sunday during an inspection of road repair work on the Outer Ring Road between Janakpuri District Centre Chowk and the Najafgarh Drain.

The video, which showed Verma slapping the man who was recording the proceedings, was widely shared on social media.

The row intensified on Monday after police filed a non-cognisable report against Verma under charges of voluntarily causing hurt.

Former Delhi chief minister and AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal demanded Verma's dismissal and arrest, accusing him of attacking a young man who was questioning the quality of the road work.

"The minister slapped a young boy. This country does not belong to your father. You cannot slap anyone like this. This country belongs to 140 crore Indians," Kejriwal said after reaching the Tilak Nagar area.

"Gen Z does not trust you at all because of such acts by you. Parvesh Verma says he is Modi ji's favourite. I want to tell both of them, people of the country do not accept this kind of behaviour," he said.

Kejriwal also alleged corruption in the road construction work and demanded an investigation against Verma.





"This is a new road and it is already damaged. We had not seen such roads before in Delhi. We were also in government for 10 years. It is clear there has been corruption in construction of this work and should be investigated," he said.

The incident unfolded after AAP MLA from Tilak Nagar Jarnail Singh, who was present during the inspection, pulled out portions of the newly laid road surface by hand and questioned its quality.

The young man was recording the proceedings when Verma allegedly slapped him.

Verma hit back at the AAP on Monday, accusing its workers of trying to obstruct government work.

"I warn you... you remember me, right?" Verma said, directly addressing Kejriwal.

He also rejected the description of the man as a member of Gen Z.

"That person is not any Gen-Z. He is a goon who has an FIR registered against him for assaulting an MCD official three months back.

He was arrested also," Verma said.

Verma also accused Jarnail Singh of seeking a commission from the road contractor and said the video being circulated by the AAP did not show the full context of the incident.

The PWD has separately filed a complaint at Tilak Nagar police station against Jarnail Singh, accusing the MLA of obstructing officials from carrying out their duties.

The police action has further intensified the political confrontation.

AAP Delhi chief and former Greater Kailash MLA Saurabh Bharadwaj alleged that police had delayed registering an FIR against Verma despite the video being widely available.

"First, the DCP told us to send all the people and said they were ready to register an FIR. They wasted two hours of our time and did not register the FIR. So we asked the ACP, you have been saying that you have been conducting an inquiry for the past 24 hours, what inquiry have you conducted so far? They have no answer...

This means that the video which the whole of India has seen has still not been seen by the ACP, DCP and SHO of the police.

So they are directly acting as Parvesh Verma's lawyers, and they are working to provoke the youth of the country because if the youth do not get justice, they will take to the streets."

Delhi minister and BJP leader Kapil Mishra also joined the attack on Kejriwal, linking the row to the AAP's political prospects in Punjab.

"People of Punjab are fed up with AAP government; whenever Kejriwal panics, it is a sign that his party will lose elections", Mishra said.

Meanwhile, members of the Sikh community staged a protest outside Verma's residence on Monday over the slapping incident.

Police deployed heavy security and barricades near his residence on Janpath Road, and several protesters were detained as they tried to reach the house.

World.title: Centre discusses drought measures to protect Rabi crops in the country
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Apprehending a threat of deficient monsoon rainfall to the upcoming sowing season, Centre on Monday discussed contingency measures to minimise its impact on Rabi (winter-sown) crops, with Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan calling for data-driven planning, stronger centre-state coordination, weekly crop monitoring, balanced fertiliser use and water budgeting.

Amid indications that the kharif (summer-sown) cropsâ output may not match last yearâs level despite progress in acreage, the minister, while addressing farm scientists and policymakers during a national conference, also emphasised the need to drive the Rabi strategy through less water-consuming pulses and oilseeds. The latest acreage data shows the total sown area at 1,107 lakh hectares (ha) as of Friday was about three lakh ha more than the ânormalâ (average of last five years) acreage (1,104 lakh ha) despite a cumulative deficit of 12% in monsoon rainfall in the country.

It was, however, 14 lakh ha less than the same period of 2025, a year which recorded 8% more than normal rainfall.

The conference was convened to discuss the farm strategy, keeping in view the current drought situation in many states, so that the impact of low moisture content in the soil and shortage of water for irrigation due to deficient rainfall may not impact farming operations much. Sowing of rabi crops such as wheat and mustard begins in October.





The Centre will, meanwhile, send teams to Karnataka and Maharashtra to assess the drought situation. Nearly two-thirds of Maharashtra has been affected and the state has already declared a drought, while Karnataka is also facing drought-like conditions due to the monsoon rainfall deficit of 30%.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The monsoon season will end on Wednesday with a strong possibility of an overall rainfall deficit of more than 10% in the country as a whole â a deficient condition which is considered a drought.

As of Monday, India recorded a deficit of 12% in cumulative (June 1âSept 28) monsoon rainfall, with 12 states reporting a deficit of 20% or more.

Underlining the current situation, Chouhan asked every district to assess the water available for irrigation before finalising crop plans. âAreas with limited water availability should prioritise less water-intensive crops such as pulses and oilseeds, while areas with assured irrigation can plan other crops accordingly,â he said while noting that the rainfed areas, in particular, require careful planning as the availability of soil moisture largely determines the crop choice and outcome.

Rabi crops are normally sown in a total area of about 638 lakh hectares, out of which wheat generally covers nearly 50% of it, with the remaining around 50% being covered by pulses, oilseeds and coarse cereals.

World.title: Kerala HC calls for Centre's intervention on exorbitantly priced patented medicines
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Kerala high court has said the Centre can invoke provisions of the Patents Act to manufacture and distribute a patented medicine to patients in need when the drug is being sold at an exorbitant price.

The court made the observation while dealing with a 2022 petition filed by a woman suffering from breast cancer, who had sought affordable access to the drug Ribociclib, news agency PTI reported. She died while the case was pending.

Justice Harisankar V Menon, in a 65-page judgment, said the Centre can use a patent or invention to manufacture a patented medicine and sell it on a non-commercial basis to a person in need under Section 100 of the Patents Act, which deals with the government's power to use inventions for government purposes.

The court held that Section 100 "is required to be invoked in circumstances, where the government is required to intervene", including cases where a patented medicine is being sold at an exorbitant price, PTI reported.

The court, however, said the government would first have to collect the relevant information and assess whether the price of a particular medicine is affordable before taking action under the provision.





The petition was filed by a former bank employee who had been diagnosed with HR+/HER2-metastatic breast cancer and was undergoing treatment with a CDK 4/6 inhibitor, Ribociclib.

According to the petition, the medicine cost around Rs 58,140 for a 21-day course. She had approached the court seeking a reduction in its price or access to the drug at an affordable cost.

After her death, the high court took suo motu cognisance of the larger issue of the high prices of patented life-saving medicines, PTI reported.

During the proceedings, the Centre and pharmaceutical industry representatives argued that Section 100 could be invoked only for government purposes and could not be used in the circumstances before the court.

The high court rejected that interpretation.

The court said the expression "for the purposes of government" must be understood to include the government's power to sell or supply products manufactured using a patent or invention to a buyer on a non-commercial basis.

"In that event," the court said, Section 100 would include the government's entitlement to manufacture the patented medicine and sell it on a non-commercial basis to a person who could be "none other than the needy patient".

The court also said the government has an obligation to ensure access to healthcare, including life-saving treatment.

In reaching its conclusions, the high court referred to the 139th Report of the Department-Related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare on cancer treatment.

The report had emphasised the need for government and private-sector participation to make cancer care more affordable.

The court also referred to the Malayalam film 'Sukrutham', starring Mammootty, which depicts the difficulties faced by cancer patients and their families.

The court observed that it was "highly distressing" that despite nearly three decades having passed since the film's release, the situation had not changed substantially.

The judgment stressed the need for a balance between ensuring affordable access to medical treatment and maintaining adequate incentives for innovation.

"It is imperative that, we, as a community and as a system that caters to billions, strike the balance between affordable access to medical treatment and maintaining adequate incentives," the court said.

World.title: 'Not your father's country': Kejriwal attacks Delhi minister Parvesh Singh over viral slapping video
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A political row erupted in Delhi on Monday over the alleged slapping of a man during a road inspection in Tilak Nagar, with AAP national convener

demanding the arrest of Public Works Department (PWD) Minister Parvesh Verma and action over alleged corruption in the road project.

Kejriwal also raised questions on the quality of a newly constructed road, alleging that portions of the road could be pulled apart by hand. He accused the Delhi government of allowing corruption in the project and said the incident showed the need for action against those responsible. "This is not your father's country; you cannot slap someone like this," Kejriwal said while demanding Verma's arrest.

The former Delhi chief minister had also targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his outreach to Gen Z, saying the government could connect with young people by demonstrating accountability rather than through social media initiatives.

"You do all kinds of drama to connect with Gen Z. Sometimes you make a reel at 12 in the night, sometimes you go to bhajan clubbing, still Gen Z is not able to connect with you," Kejriwal said in a video posted on X earlier.

He alleged that the road constructed under the Rekha Gupta government had begun to crumble soon after being laid and demanded that those involved in the alleged corruption be arrested. "Arrest the minister today.





Whoever was involved in the corruption on this road, arrest them. If you do these things, you won't need to make reels at night or go to bhajan clubbing. They will automatically connect with you," Kejriwal said.



Kejriwal also alleged that

had been instructed to protect Verma, but did not provide evidence for the claim. He said citizens expected the government to demonstrate "honesty and straightforwardness".

The controversy stems from a video circulated by AAP showing Verma appearing to slap a man during Sunday's road inspection. The man was identified as Saheb Singh, who is associated with Tilak Nagar AAP MLA Jarnail Singh and handles his social media work. The footage shows Verma pulling down Singh's mobile phone before appearing to slap him.

Verma has rejected the allegations that the incident was simply over questions about road quality.

Responding to Kejriwal, he alleged that Singh was an AAP worker who had abused his family during the inspection.

Verma also disputed Kejriwal's description of Singh as a member of Gen Z, calling him a "goon" of the AAP. He said, "Kejriwal ji, the person who came into my round yesterday was not a Gen Z; he was your goon."

The minister alleged that Singh had previously been booked in a case involving an MCD contractual employee and claimed that the MLA's nephew was also named in the case.

He further alleged that AAP leaders had sought commissions from officials involved in road projects, claims that were not independently established.



Verma said he would not tolerate obstruction of government work or harassment of officials and contractors. He also claimed that a complaint and an FIR had been registered against the MLA and his associates over alleged obstruction of public works.

Meanwhile, a complaint was filed with Delhi Police over the alleged slapping incident. Police were also reported to have confirmed that Singh had previously been booked in an assault case and was out on bail

World.title: YouTuber Aswanth Kok taken into custody over suspected drunk driving
World.content:
The Nadakkavu police on Monday (September 28, 2026) took into custody YouTuber Aswanth Kok following allegations that he was driving under the influence of alcohol and hit three other vehicles.

The incident occurred near Eranhipalam, where the vehicle allegedly driven by him collided with other vehicles on the road. Residents reportedly stopped the vehicle and alerted the police.

The police reached the spot shortly afterwards and took him into custody. He was subsequently subjected to a medical examination to determine whether he had consumed alcohol while driving.

The police said further action would be taken based on the medical examination report and the findings of the investigation into the accident.

World.title: SIR: Over 4,000 Form-7 seek deletion of names, largely Muslim voters, across Congress, BJP seats
World.content:
Bulk Form-7 applications seeking deletion of names, largely Muslim voters, have been filed across several Assembly constituencies in the State, with more than 4,000 deletions being sought, according to Form-10 statutory report, which consolidates details of Form-7 objections.

In a few cases, the applications were found to have the details of the voters “already printed”, with only the objectors’ names handwritten.

In Babaleshwar alone, 1,373 Form-7 applications were received on September 22. Of these, 1,363 were filed by just 10 people, seeking deletions largely against Muslim voters outside their own polling stations. Babaleshwar is represented by Congress Minister M.B. Patil.

Between September 22 and 23, Huchappa Ganiger, an elector in Babaleshwar Assembly constituency, filed 493 Form-7 applications seeking deletions, largely against Muslim voters, across about 30 polling stations. Of these, 423 were filed on September 22, a day before the deadline for claims and objections ended. On September 23, Mr. Ganiger filed another 70 applications, while several other individuals also appeared in the data as having filed multiple objections. On the same day, another elector, Govindaraj Mundur, filed 413 applications across 33 polling stations.

Data suggests similar pattern at Bhalki in Bidar district, represented by Minister Eshwar Khandre. At least 30 people filed objections seeking the deletion of more than 1,700 names on September 23. Several of those who filed bulk objections that day had also submitted multiple Form-7 applications the previous day. An elector named Santosh filed 120 applications on September 23, after filing 54 on September 22.

BJP seats

In Basavakalyan, an elector named Siddappa filed 32 of the 37 Form-7 applications received on a single day. All the objections were all against Muslim voters within a single polling station (Part No. 163). At Belthangady in Dakshina Kannada, an elector named Umesh Bangera filed 21 applications, again all targeting Muslim voters in a single polling station (Part No. 47). Both Basavakalyan and Belthangady are represented by the BJP.

The reason cited against the electors in the applications is “Absent/Permanently Shifted”.

Already printed

The applications in Bhalki also raise questions about how some of the objections were prepared.

In two such cases, the details of the objectors were handwritten, while the names of the voters whose deletion was being sought were already filled in and printed on the forms.

For instance, multiple Form-7 applications named “Vishnuvardhan Kote”, an elector at Booth 129, as the person filing the objection. When contacted by The Hindu, however, the person said he was not Vishnuvardhan and identified himself as “Suresh”. The EPIC details mentioned in the applications, when cross-checked, were linked to an elector named Vishnuvardhan.

The Hindu furtherobtained photographs of the physical Form-7 applications. In these, only Vishnuvardhan’s details were handwritten, while the details of the voters whose deletion was being sought were already printed on the forms. The same was seen in applications bearing the name “Santosh Eshwar”, who has filed more than 170 Form-7.

However, when The Hindu cross-checked the physical applications against the Form-10 data available for download on the website, Vishnuvardhan’s name could not be found in the list of those shown as having filed objections, while Santosh’s name was there in the list. Officials in Bidar said many applications had been filed offline and might not have been digitised yet.

Before September 22, Form-7 applications seeking deletion on the ground that a voter had shifted were generally few in number, usually around two or three per polling station. In these cases, mostly electors had filed applications seeking deletion of their own names on the ground that they had shifted. Bulk applications began appearing on September 22, a day before the September 23 deadline for filing claims and objections.

When contacted, officials in Bidar and Vijayapura said all such objections would be scrutinised before any action was taken, to ensure that no eligible voter was deleted. They also said those who filed objections in bulk had been instructed that submitting claims without valid grounds, if proved, could invite punishment.

World.title: Russian drones hammer apartments, offices and a cultural landmark in Ukraine, killing 7
World.content:
Russia’s round-the-clock bombardment of targets in Ukraine killed at least seven people and wounded more than 80 others, officials said Monday (September 28, 2026).

Moscow’s forces pounded apartment buildings, offices, gas stations, data centers and a building of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine in downtown Kyiv, among other targets.

The ceaseless Russian drone attacks on cities and towns aim to wear down Ukraine’s resistance and cripple the Ukrainian economy.

The attacks followed a week of diplomatic efforts at the United Nations to get traction for negotiations on ending Moscow’s invasion that began 4½ years ago.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov indicated Monday (September 28) that the chances of making speedy headway on forging a peace settlement were bleak after recent Ukrainian attacks, including during recent parliamentary elections in Russia.

“Ukraine will have to pay a price for the actions that have taken place in recent months,” Mr. Peskov told reporters. “That is happening right now.”

Russian drone attacks on the Kyiv region killed four people and wounded eight, officials said.

A woman was killed in a Russian strike on Kyiv’s Shevchenkivskyi district on Monday afternoon, the Kyiv city military administration said. The strike hit the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine, the latest cultural landmark in the capital to be damaged.

Some staff escaped the burning building by climbing from windows down firefighters’ ladders.

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the Russians were conducting a campaign of “pure terror” on the civilian population.

“The terror goes on,” he told reporters at the site of the academy strike. “For more than a week Russia has kept attacking Kyiv, disrupting normal life in the city and destroying buildings.”

Russian forces also hit a pharmaceutical company and gas stations in Kyiv.

One drone struck an office center in central Dnipro during working hours Monday, killing three people and wounding at least 18, local authorities said.

A Russian strike on a nine-story apartment building in the northeastern city of Kharkiv wounded 43 people, including 11 children, Mayor Ihor Terekhov said.

Thirty civilians were injured in Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia, officials said, while another Russian attack damaged a multistory apartment building in Odesa, wounding three people, according to Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa regional military administration.

Four people, including two teenage girls, were hurt when a Russian drone struck a residential area in northern Ukraine’s Chernihiv region on Sunday evening (September 27), said Viacheslav Chaus, head of the regional military administration.

Russia’s Defense Ministry said its forces struck two data centers in Kyiv, as well as gas stations in the Ukrainian capital. A distribution hub belonging to the Nova Poshta postal service was struck in the southern city of Odesa, it said.

The Russian military also hit a cargo ship in the Black Sea and another one in the Ukrainian port of Chornomorsk, the ministry said. The strikes aim to curb Ukraine’s grain exports, though they may also create food shortages in countries that rely on Ukrainian imports.

The Russian aerial attacks regularly hit civilian areas. Moscow claims it targets only military-related sites.

Battlefield positions have changed little since last year, in part because swarms of drones severely restrict troop movements, but Kyiv’s forces launched a recent offensive, code-named Operation Vivaldi, on part of the 1,250-kilometer (800-mile) front line.

Ukraine’s Third Army Corps said Monday it had recaptured another 51 square kilometers (20 square miles) from the Russians, bringing the total to 176 square kilometers (68 square miles) since the offensive began several months ago.

The corps said that in order to break through Russian defenses, it converted Soviet-era BTR-60 armored personnel carriers into kamikaze vehicles that blew up the strongest Russian fortifications. The operation has also used ground robots to attack Russian positions.

The claimed breakthroughs came in the Donetsk region of eastern Ukraine, which the bigger Russian army has been trying in vain to conquer.

Russian officials made no immediate comment on the Ukrainian claim.

Russia’s Defense Ministry, meanwhile, said Russian troops captured the villages of Novovodiane in the Donetsk region and Ulanove in the northern Sumy region.

It was not possible to independently verify the claims.

Zelenskyy said long-range strikes on Russian soil hit two defense plants in the Tula and Voronezh regions and oil facilities in the Krasnodar region, all in southern and western Russia.

Ukraine’s long-range drones have repeatedly targeted Russian fuel depots and industrial plants that are a mainstay of Moscow’s economy and war effort.

Ukrainian drone attacks overnight started fires at three infrastructure facilities in Russia’s Krasnodar region, local emergency officials said Monday (September 28), without identifying the locations.

Russia’s Defense Ministry said air defenses downed 254 Ukrainian drones overnight.

World.title: BJP’s SC/ST Lok Sabha MPs took part in fewer debates than House average and party peers
World.content:
Days after Union Minister Jitan Ram Manjhi wrote to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla asking for more floor time for the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe MPs from the ruling NDA coalition, an analysis reveals that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MPs elected from SC and ST seats have taken part in fewer Lok Sabha debates than the House average and than their own party colleagues.

Also Read: Jitan Ram Manjhi says SC/ST MPs not given enough time to speak in Parliament

An analysis of the PRS Legislative Research’s MP Track data, from June 24, 2024, to August 23, 2026, by The Hindu reveals that the 24 BJP MPs from SC seats averaged 14.67 debates. This data excludes six Ministers from SC/ST constituencies. The 22 MPs from ST seats averaged 13.05. Together, the 46 MPs averaged 13.89, against 21.53 for all 483 sitting MPs. Party colleagues from other seats did more. The 145 BJP MPs outside SC and ST seats averaged 19.68.

Compared with all BJP MPs elected on non-reserved seats, SC-seat BJP MPs averaged 4.14 fewer debates (14.67 against 18.80). ST-seat BJP MPs averaged 5.92 fewer (13.05 against 18.96).

The 42-year-old Mahendra Singh Solanky, elected for a second time from Dewas, is the only one among the 46 MPs who has not participated in any debate. Nine are above the House average, with BJP MP from Palamau, Vishnu Dayal Ram, leading with 44 debates and Hemant Vishnu Savara of Palghar a close second with 43.

The pattern is not limited to the BJP. Across all parties, SC-seat MPs averaged 18.22 debates compared with 22.15 for others, and ST-seat MPs averaged 17.67 against 21.91.

The principal Opposition party Congress also recorded a gap, with MPs from SC seats averaging 19 against 23.38 for party peers. Congress MPs from ST seats averaged 24.42, above the 22.22 of their peers.

In his letter dated September 16, Mr. Manjhi referred to an ‘NDA sansad samooh samvaad baithak’ (NDA MP group dialogue meeting) held at his residence on August 5. He said BJP Lok Sabha MP Gajendra Singh Patel, who represents Khargone, a reserved tribal constituency in Madhya Pradesh, had pointed out that MPs from SC/ST communities were not being given adequate time to speak during discussions on important Bills in Parliament. Mr. Manjhi urged the Speaker to take steps to rectify the situation.

World.title: Over 5,000 gold rings to be distributed under ‘Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam’  in Salem and Namakkal districts
World.content:
A total of 5,081 infants born between June 22 and September 27 this year will receive a one-gram gold ring under the ‘Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam’ in Salem and Namakkal districts.

Following Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay launching the ‘Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram Thittaam’ at Madurai, Salem District Collector K. Elambahavath distributed one-gram gold ring to 25 newborn babies in a function held at the Salem Government Hospital.

Addressing the media, the Collector said under the scheme, children born in government hospitals will receive a one-gram gold ring, for which, a unique serial number and a tamper-proof packaging was provided. To avail themselves of the scheme, pregnant women must register in the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) and receive the Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. The gold ring will be distributed to infants during discharge from the hospital, the Collector added.

Stating that around 17,000 children will benefit under the scheme in the Salem district every year, the Collector said a total of 3,502 infants born from June 22 to September 27 will receive the gold ring. These rings will be distributed in the government hospitals concerned on the scheduled date and time. Through village health nurses, invitations will be given to the beneficiaries. For details, contact 73581-29149/73581-45378, the Collector added.

Likewise, in a function held at Namakkal Government Hospital, Minister for Registration and Commercial Taxes Department D. Logesh Tamilselvan distributed gold rings to the newborns. Under this scheme in Namakkal district, 1,579 infants born between June 22 and September 25 will receive gold rings.

World.title: TVK govt. has insulted voters by thrusting byelection, says Kanimozhi
World.content:
The TVK government has slighted voters by thrusting byelection through “deceptive means”, DMK deputy general secretary and Thoothukudi MP Kanimozhi Karunanidhi said on Monday (September 28, 2026), while campaigning for her party candidate S. Suganya.

“Where did the ₹50 crore (stated to be given for buying out erstwhile AIADMK MLA and TVK candidate Sathyabama) come from?,” Ms. Kanimozhi questioned.

The Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay is fixated on DMK is evident from his campaign speeches that has umpteen mention of the party’s name. But, the people were getting bored, Ms. Kanimozhi said, referring to the CM’s campaign speech in Madurantakam Constituency.

The DMK will not be cowed down by the repression of its leaders through “foisted cases” by the TVK government.

The CM, Ms. Kanimozhi said, was reluctant to act on “corruption charges” against TVK Ministers. She attacked the TVK government on the law and order front, delay in implementing election promises, and ‘unethical approach’ of utilising children for winning in polls.

There have been more than 200 murders, 300 sexual assaults, eight custodial deaths, and 10 honour killings after the TVK came to power, she said.

Power cuts have become acute, and the ruling regime was incompetent to rectify the situation.

The TVK government has taken farmers for a ride by going back on the promise for agricultural loan waiver. The spurt in inflation rate in Tamil Nadu to 5.44%, as against national average of 4.4% has been an achievement, Ms. Kanimozhi remarked sarcastically, adding that job opportunities in the State has also fallen drastically.

Tamil language has been relegated by the TVK regime, Ms. Kanimozhi said.

The TVK government’s prioritisation of ‘Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam’ over combatting the dengue outbreak was “ridiculous”, she said.

World.title: Kerala HC grants pre-arrest bail to YouTuber
World.content:
The Kerala High Court has granted pre-arrest bail to YouTuber Muhammed Nihad, alias Thoppi, who was booked for conducting a livestream on the YouTube channel “Mrz Shameer” and allegedly publishing offensive content about the complainant.

Justice A. Badharudeen reviewed the video and found that there was nothing to show that Mr. Nihad had directly spoken any obscene words or made sexually coloured remarks against the victim. The court held that Mr. Nihad’s custodial interrogation was unnecessary in view of the allegations.

The prosecution had alleged before the District and Sessions Court, Manjeri, that the accused had conducted the livestream for four hours and deliberately displayed photographs and videos of the complainant without her consent, made obscene, sexually coloured and defamatory remarks, intruded on her privacy and insulted her modesty.

The court granted pre-arrest bail subject to conditions, including the execution of a bond for ₹1 lakh with two solvent sureties, full cooperation with the investigation, weekly appearance before the investigating officer and not leaving the State without the permission of the trial court.

World.title: Why Israel banned Arab parties ahead of polls
World.content:
Israel’s Central Elections Committee (CEC), on Wednesday (September 23, 2026), voted to bar the country’s main Arab parties from contesting next month’s elections to Israel’s parliament, the Knesset. There have been a series of attempts for decades to disqualify Arab parties from contesting elections, and the latest move comes at a time when these parties have a chance to play a crucial role in the upcoming government.

Recent polls by media outlets have suggested that neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition nor the Zionist opposition bloc will be able to secure the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority in the 120-member Knesset, and projected that the Arab parties could win up to 12 seats. The CEC’s move to disqualify the Ra’am party and the Joint List (an alliance of Arab parties Balad, Hadash and Ta’al) comes at this juncture. The panel has also voted to disqualify Joint List individual candidate Ofer Cassif and Balad leader Sami Abu Shehadeh.

However, the panel’s decision is not final. It requires the approval of the Supreme Court of Justice for disqualifying individual candidates, and the disqualified political party has the right to appeal to the Supreme Court.

Reason for the ban

The CEC, responding to petitions filed by Likud and Jewish Power parties as well as the Choose Life Forum, a non-government organisation, voted 18-5 with one abstention to disqualify the Ra’am party led by M.K. Mansour Abbas on grounds of supporting the armed struggle of a terrorist organisation/enemy state, inciting racism and rejecting Israel’s existence. However, as per Adalah, the legal centre for Arab rights in Israel, no supporting evidence was presented.

The move to bar the Joint List relied on bills and actions from previous Knessets, some of which have already been examined and dismissed by the Supreme Court. Mr. Cassif’s dismissal rested on his criticism of the army and the government for committing war crimes against Palestinians. Mr. Shehadeh’s disqualification rested on the claim that he expressed support for armed struggle.

Adalah, which represented the now-banned political partiesand individual candidates before the CEC, in its site referred to the hearings and the motions as “an arbitrary, inciting and racist process” aimed at “persecuting ideas the majority does not accept” which ended with disqualification of all Palestinian representations in the Israeli Knesset. The organisation is also representing them before the Supreme Court this week.

Previous attempts

The attempt is, however, not new. As per information published by Adalah on its site, the CEC has filed disqualification motions against Arab political parties and candidates in every election cycle for the past 20+ years. But the Supreme Court has cancelled the CEC’s decision and reinstated candidacy in each of these instances.

For instance, the CEC voted to disqualify the Balad party and its key founder Azmi Bishara from contesting the 2003 elections. In the 2013 elections, there was an attempt to bar Balad, Ra’am-Ta’al and Arab List candidate M.K. Zoabi. Less than two years later, the CEC approved the disqualification of Mr. Zoabi. In the 2020 election, motions were filed to disqualify Joint List’s Heba Yazbak and in 2022, it voted to disqualify the Balad party.

Arbitrary provisions

These processes are valid under the existing Knesset Elections Law as per which any political party or any citizen aged 18 years and over or the attorney general can file a disqualification motion to the Knesset’s Central Elections Committee (CEC) requesting the barring of a political party or an individual from contesting elections. The motion is approved if it receives a majority approval of 51% from CEC members.

Under Article 7A of the Basic Law, the Knesset has the right to disqualify any party or individual if their goals or actions (including speech) either deny the existence of the State of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state or incite racism or offer support to armed struggle to an enemy state or to a terrorist organisation against the State of Israel.

But, this law has several shortcomings. Firstly, the CEC which is established to carry out election processes, is itself a politicised body comprising roughly 30-35 representatives of outgoing members of the Knesset and is chaired by a Supreme Court Justice. In a Knesset where Arab parties have only been able to secure a smaller share of seats, and where blocs are not inclined to join hands with Arab parties, the chances of arbitrary disqualification from outgoing Knesset members remains a looming crisis.

Secondly, the provisions of Article 7A are pretty vague. There is no definition for what constitutes a “terror organisation” or what “offering support” means. Further, even a political position like a “State for all its citizens” could be implied as denial of the nature of Jewish state.

Arab representation

The disqualification that effectively bars all Arab parties is a blow to the country’s already underrepresented Arab population.

According to Israel’s Central Bureau of Statistics, around 2.157 million Arabs live in the country and account for 21% of the country’s population. The parties representing the Arab population have never held more than 15 seats in the 120-member Knesset. For instance, the Joint List, which included Ra’am, till 2021 secured 13, 13, and 15 seats in the 2015, 2019 and 2020 Knesset elections respectively and was part of the opposition.

It was in 2021 that Ra’am, which broke away from the Joint List, became the first Arab party in more than 50 years to be part of the coalition government. It returned to being part of the opposition the next year with Mr. Netanyahu’s return to power.

This time the disqualifications, if upheld, could have electoral implications beyond Arab representation. With neither of the present ruling and the opposition blocs showing any inclination to include Arab parties in the future government and polls predicting no clear winner, the move constrains the chances of the Arab parties to be part of the ruling coalition.

World.title: US delegation meets CDF Munir, acknowledges Pakistan's 'longstanding role, sacrifices' during Afghan war
World.content:
A delegation of America’s Afghanistan War Commission called on Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir on Monday and acknowledged Pakistan’s “longstanding role and sacrifices during the conflict in Afghanistan”, according to the military’s media affairs wings.

The visiting delegation also appreciated Pakistan’s continued contribution to regional peace and stability, the Inter-Services Public Relations said in a statement.

The delegation, led by its co-chairs, Shamila N. Chaudhary and Dr Colin F Jackson, met CDF Munir at General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi.

“The delegation is undertaking a review of the United States’ 20-year engagement in Afghanistan,” the statement said, adding that its discussion with the military chief covered topics including “Pakistan’s support, the regional security environment and developments in Afghanistan, with focus on perspectives relevant to the commission’s work”.

For his part, CDF Munir shared Pakistan’s perspective on the security dynamics that shaped the conflict, also highlighting the challenges the country faced during the prolonged US engagement in Afghanistan.

The ISPR statement added that he highlighted the need to incorporate a regional perspective, as well as Pakistan’s experience in assessing the strategic, diplomatic and operational dimensions of the conflict.

The US Congress established the Afghanistan War Commission in 2021 as an independent body to review US decisions pertaining to the war in Afghanistan from June 2001 to August 2021, according to the commission’s website.

US forces had withdrawn from Afghanistan in Aug 2021, ending a 20-year war. The withdrawal was completed a minute before midnight on Aug 30, 2021.

The US had launched a military intervention in Afghanistan following the Sept 11, 2001, attacks, ushering in two decades of conflict in which civilians suffered widespread violence and abuses.

Some 800,000 US servicemembers served in Afghanistan during this period. During the war, 2,238 US servicemembers died and nearly 21,000 were wounded.

Meanwhile, over 40,000 civilians were killed and 77,000 wounded in attacks by Taliban insurgents, the Islamic State (IS) group, and in operations by the armed forces of the Afghan Republic or the international coalition led by the US, according to the United Nations mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA).

Independent estimates put the total number of Afghan security forces and civilians killed at more than 100,000.

A detailed report in The Wall Street Journal in 2022 showed that since Sept 11, 2001, US military outsourcing had pushed up Pentagon spending to $14 trillion. One-third to half of that sum went to contractors.

World.title: CM Afridi strikes defiant tone as federal ministers rail against KP govt's counter-terror fight
World.content:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday struck a defiant tone and again panned the Centre’s counterterrorism policy as federal ministers railed against his government’s efforts to combat terrorism.

Afridi, who was elected as the KP CM in October 2025, has repeatedly voiced his opposition to the federal government’s policies on counterterrorism and Afghanistan.

Earlier in the day, Kashmir affairs and frontier regions minister Amir Muqam held a press conference in Peshawar, where he slammed the PTI and Afridi for focusing on the party’s planned long march rather than the security challenges that KP was facing.

Later, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, during a press briefing in Islamabad, highlighted flaws in the KP government’s “leadership” and use of resources to fight terrorism.

This was followed by another press conference in Peshawar, where the prime minister’s coordinator to KP, Ikhtiar Wali Khan, and MNA Samar Haroon Bilour presented a white paper on the KP government’s “failure” to equip police with sophisticated weapons.

Meanwhile, addressing a meeting regarding law and order in Peshawar, the KP CM stressed that merely providing resources to the police would not solve the problem until there was a policy shift.

“We repeatedly stated that the state’s current policy was flawed. The blood of our Pakhtuns will flow again,” Afridi said, regretting that federal ministers “dismissed our repeated warnings as propaganda and lies”.

The chief minister highlighted that he had been consistently calling for a change to the “failed policy of 22 years”.

The PTI leader declared he would not back down from his stance over threats of imposition of governor’s rule or a state of emergency.

Afridi called for a new counterterrorism policy to be formulated that took all stakeholders into confidence, including the provincial government, administration and police.

He contended that if the new policy was implemented as proposed, peace could be restored in KP within 100 days — “yet no one is willing to listen”.

“Some people act as if they know it all and are unwilling to listen to the stakeholders of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” he said. “Where is the country being led? Is the blood of our people so cheap that it should be sacrificed for the sake of politics?”

CM Afridi also defended his government’s performance, recalling that it had diverted Rs35 billion from the development budget to the police force, doubling its allocation.

He added that the Special Branch was being stabilised and modern weaponry and essential gear were being provided to the police force.

The KP CM went on to accuse the federal government of adopting a “dual-standard policy”: “one for the favourites and another for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa”, terming this unacceptable.

He again expressed concern over Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s comments that the other three provinces posed a threat rather than India, noting that she was contradicting the state’s stance that New Delhi had a role in sponsoring terrorism in Pakistan.

“Federal ministers label the residents of KP as terrorists and savages; they are forgiven because they are favourites … no action is taken against them,” the PTI leader said.

Azam Tarar says governor’s rule or emergency can happen

Meanwhile, calls from federal representatives for imposing governor’s rule or an emergency in KP intensified, with Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar saying that such a move could be made if required.

“If such conditions, where the constitution demands governor’s rule to be implemented or an emergency declared, are there or they arise, it can and will definitely happen,” he told Geo News.

“If the mechanism in the constitution requires it, all these things will happen,” Azam said.

In his media talk at Peshawar Press Club, Muqam said “all conditions” required by the law for imposing governor’s rule existed.

Criticising Afridi’s governance, Muqam asserted that his “CM-ship would not continue and no one will be able to save him”.

“Afridi sahib, be ready, you will be behind bars. You will be held accountable for the loot and plundering you have done,” the minister said.

He criticised the PTI’s alleged lack of concern regarding the security challenges, contending that the party did not have enough public support.

The federal minister described the Afridi-led provincial government as a complete failure on all fronts, claiming that it had neglected public welfare and that corruption was widespread in KP.

Muqam further said that PTI leaders were conducting political activities across the country and did not appear to have any fear of terrorist attacks, even as other parties’ leaders faced such threats.

Separately, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi held a meeting with Muqam to discuss the deteriorating law and order situation in the province and political developments, state-run APP reported.

NA Standing Committee on Defence Chairman Fatihullah Khan Miankhel, National Democratic Movement (NDM) chief Mohsin Dawar, PPP Parliamentary Leader in KP Assembly Ahmad Kundi and MPA Sobia Khan were among those present.

The participants exchanged views on the prevailing security situation, political uncertainty and other issues, and “deliberated on a number of proposals”, the APP report said.

The leaders expressed serious concern over the rising incidents of insecurity in the province and termed the worsening situation a result of what they described as the provincial government’s failure to maintain law and order.

Speaking to the media, Kundi warned the PTI government not to “force the Centre” to impose governor’s rule and urged it to further postpone its long march currently set for Oct 4.

Kundi said that in his opinion, governor’s rule could be imposed if the federal government deemed it necessary “to save the province”.

“Fire is raging here,” he said while speaking on the province’s security situation.

“I advise the provincial government to postpone their long march due to the law and order situation, call all stakeholders and political parties to discuss peace in the province, and fight terrorism on the frontline.”

He contended that the PTI wanted to march on Islamabad and “spread chaos” even when terrorist incidents in KP were claiming people’s lives.

Afridi responds to ‘white paper’ on KP govt

In a post on X in the evening, CM Afridi asserted that the KP police and the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) were “extremely capable and equipped with modern weapons”.

He appeared to be specifically responding to Wali’s allegations, sharing a screenshot from the latter’s press conference earlier.

According to state broadcaster Radio Pakistan, the PML-N’s KP chapter issued a white paper on the provincial government’s performance.

Pictures of the white paper’s cover shared by Wali and Bilour said the document pertained to the KP government’s “misgovernance during past one year” — since Afridi came to power.

The PML-N leaders said over Rs800bn had been given to KP for counterterrorism efforts, but the provincial government had miserably failed to equip the police with much-needed sophisticated weapons and equipment.

Giving a presentation, Wali said the KP CTD had only nine M4 rifles and 11 night vision devices for the entire province.

“Bulletproof vehicles provided by the Centre were returned with arrogance and mockery, and today the province has just 17 vehicles. In contrast, Punjab has 76, and even a low-budget province like Balochistan has 42 bulletproof vehicles.”

The PM’s coordinator said the number of police personnel martyred between January and June in 2025 rose by almost 94 per cent in the same period this year.

Similarly, injuries to police personnel rose 108pc during the period, while terrorist attacks between January and September 2026 increased by 33pc compared to the same period in 2025.

Speaking alongside him, Bilour highlighted that CM Afridi held his first meeting of the provincial apex committee in February, 112 days after taking oath.

She particularly pointed out that Afridi focused a Sept 21 media talk, held just three days after the Kohat attack, on the PTI’s long march plans and dismissed a journalist’s question on the province’s situation.

The PML-N leaders further alleged that the Afridi-led government has failed to curb the spread of drugs.

According to his post, Afridi saw a conspiracy for an attack, which he described as an attempt to prove that KP police and CTD were weak.

“Is the PML-N seeing KP as a testing ground and planning a major move?” he questioned.

He alleged that Heavy Industries Taxila, which operates under the Centre, “is deliberately slowing down the delivery of the supplies despite payment by the provincial government”.
